manualTranslations.zh: 袁紹攻公孫瓚，先主與田楷東屯齊。
manualTranslations.literal: Yuan Shao attacked Gongsun Zan; the Former Lord with Tian Kai camped east at Qi.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Yuan Shao attacked Gongsun Zan, Liu Bei and Tian Kai camped east in Qi.

manualTranslations.zh: 曹公征徐州，徐州牧陶謙遣使告急於田楷，楷與先主俱救之。
manualTranslations.literal: Lord Cao campaigned against Xu Province; Xu Province Governor Tao Qian sent envoys in urgent appeal to Tian Kai; Kai and the Former Lord together went to rescue him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Cao Cao marched on Xu province, Governor Tao Qian appealed to Tian Kai, and Kai and Liu Bei went together to his aid.

manualTranslations.zh: 時先主自有兵千餘人及幽州烏丸雜胡騎，又略得饑民數千人。
manualTranslations.literal: At that time the Former Lord himself had more than a thousand troops and mixed Wuhuan and foreign cavalry from You Province, and also gathered several thousand starving commoners.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Liu Bei then had a little over a thousand men of his own plus Wuhuan and foreign cavalry from You province, and he also pressed several thousand hungry refugees into service.

manualTranslations.zh: 既到，謙以丹楊兵四千益先主，先主遂去楷歸謙。
manualTranslations.literal: When they arrived, Qian with four thousand Danyang troops augmented the Former Lord; the Former Lord thereupon left Kai and returned to Qian.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On arrival Tao Qian gave him four thousand Danyang troops; Liu Bei then left Tian Kai and attached himself to Tao Qian.

manualTranslations.zh: 謙表先主為豫州刺史，屯小沛。
manualTranslations.literal: Qian memorialized the Former Lord as inspector of Yu Province and garrisoned him at Little Pei.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Tao Qian memorialized him as inspector of Yu province and posted him at Little Pei.

manualTranslations.zh: 謙病篤，謂別駕麋竺曰：「非劉備不能安此州也。
manualTranslations.literal: Qian was gravely ill; he said to chief aide Mi Zhu: "If not Liu Bei, this province cannot be settled.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: As Tao Qian lay gravely ill he told chief aide Mi Zhu, "Only Liu Bei can secure this province.

manualTranslations.zh: 」謙死，竺率州人迎先主，先主未敢當。
manualTranslations.literal: " When Qian died, Zhu led the province's people to welcome the Former Lord; the Former Lord did not yet dare accept.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: " When Tao Qian died, Mi Zhu led the people to offer him the province, but Liu Bei did not yet dare accept.

manualTranslations.zh: 下邳陳登謂先主曰：「今漢室陵遲，海內傾覆，立功立事，在於今日。
manualTranslations.literal: Chen Deng of Xiapi said to the Former Lord: "Now the house of Han declines; all within the seas overturns; to establish merit and accomplish enterprise is a matter of today.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Chen Deng of Xiapi told him, "The house of Han is failing and the realm is overturned; the moment to build a career is now.

manualTranslations.zh: 彼州殷富，戶口百萬，欲屈使君撫臨州事。
manualTranslations.literal: That province is rich and populous, a million households; we wish to bend you, my lord, to oversee the province's affairs.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: This province is rich and holds a million households; we ask you to take charge of it.

manualTranslations.zh: 」先主曰：「袁公路近在壽春，此君四世五公，海內所歸，君可以州與之。
manualTranslations.literal: " The Former Lord said: "Lord Yuan Shu is near at Shouchun; this lord is four generations and five dukes; all within the seas turn to him; you may give the province to him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: " Liu Bei answered, "Yuan Shu is close at Shouchun—a man of four generations and five marquisates whom the realm follows; you might give the province to him.

manualTranslations.zh: 」登曰：「公路驕豪，非治亂之主。
manualTranslations.literal: " Deng said: "Lord Shu is arrogant and overbearing; he is not a ruler for order and disorder.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: " Chen Deng replied, "Yuan Shu is arrogant and no ruler for troubled times.

manualTranslations.zh: 今欲為使君合步騎十萬，上可以匡主濟民，成五霸之業，下可以割地守境，書功於竹帛。
manualTranslations.literal: Now I wish for you, my lord, to assemble a hundred thousand foot and horse; upward you may support the ruler and aid the people, accomplishing the enterprise of the Five Hegemons; downward you may carve territory and guard the borders, inscribing merit on bamboo and silk.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I can raise a hundred thousand foot and horse for you—high enough to restore the ruler and aid the people in a hegemon's work, low enough to hold territory and inscribe your merit on bamboo and silk.

manualTranslations.zh: 若使君不見聽許，登亦未敢聽使君也。
manualTranslations.literal: If you, my lord, do not heed and permit this, Deng also dares not heed you, my lord.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If you will not accept, I dare not accept you either.

manualTranslations.zh: 」北海相孔融謂先主曰：「袁公路豈憂國忘家者邪？
manualTranslations.literal: " Beihai Chancellor Kong Rong said to the Former Lord: "Is Lord Yuan Shu one who grieves for the state and forgets his family?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: " Beihai chancellor Kong Rong told him, "Is Yuan Shu a man who cares for the state and forgets his family?

manualTranslations.zh: 冢中枯骨，何足介意。
manualTranslations.literal: A withered bone in a tomb—what is there worth minding?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He is a withered bone in a tomb—why heed him?

manualTranslations.zh: 今日之事，百姓與能，天與不取，悔不可追。
manualTranslations.literal: In today's affair, the people grant the capacity; Heaven grants it—if you do not take it, regret cannot be pursued.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The people offer you the charge; Heaven offers it—if you refuse, regret will not wait.

manualTranslations.zh: 」先主遂領徐州。
manualTranslations.literal: " The Former Lord thereupon took charge of Xu Province.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: " Liu Bei thereupon took charge of Xu province.

manualTranslations.zh: 《獻帝春秋》曰：陳登等遣使詣袁紹曰：「天降災沴，禍臻鄙州，州將殂殞，生民無主，恐懼姦雄一旦承隙，以貽盟主日昃之憂，輒共奉故平原相劉備府君以為宗主，永使百姓知有依歸。
manualTranslations.literal: The Spring and Autumn of Emperor Xian says: Chen Deng and others sent envoys to Yuan Shao saying: "Heaven sends disaster and pestilence; calamity reaches our humble province; the provincial lord has died; the living people have no lord; we fear treacherous heroes will seize the gap in a day, to burden the alliance leader with the worry of the setting sun; we together install the former grand administrator of Pingyuan, Lord Liu Bei, as our clan leader, forever letting the people know they have dependence and return.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn of Emperor Xian records that Chen Deng and others sent envoys to Yuan Shao: "Heaven has sent disaster upon our province; our governor is dead and the people are leaderless; we fear traitors will seize the moment and trouble our alliance lord at day's end; we have installed the former grand administrator of Pingyuan, Liu Bei, as our leader so the people may know where to turn.

manualTranslations.zh: 方今寇難縱橫，不遑釋甲，謹遣下吏奔告于執事。
manualTranslations.literal: Now bandit hardship runs crosswise; we have no leisure to lay down armor; respectfully we send subordinate clerks running to report to the chief.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Bandits run wild and we cannot yet lay down our arms; we respectfully send clerks to report to you.

manualTranslations.zh: 」紹答曰：「劉玄德弘雅有信義，今徐州樂戴之，誠副所望也。
manualTranslations.literal: " Shao answered: "Liu Xuande is broad and elegant and has faith and righteousness; now Xu Province gladly honors him—truly it matches what was hoped.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: " Yuan Shao answered, "Liu Bei is generous and trustworthy; Xu province gladly follows him—this truly matches our hopes.

manualTranslations.zh: 」袁術來攻先主，先主拒之於盱眙、淮陰。
manualTranslations.literal: " Yuan Shu came to attack the Former Lord; the Former Lord resisted him at Xuyi and Huaiyin.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: " Yuan Shu attacked Liu Bei, who held him at Xuyi and Huaiyin.

manualTranslations.zh: 曹公表先主為鎮東將軍，封宜城亭侯，是歲建安元年也。
manualTranslations.literal: Lord Cao memorialized the Former Lord as General Who Guards the East and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Yicheng precinct; that year was the first year of Jian'an.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Cao Cao memorialized him as general who guards the east and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Yicheng precinct; that year was Jian'an 1 (196).

manualTranslations.zh: 先主與術相持經月，呂布乘虛襲下邳。
manualTranslations.literal: The Former Lord and Shu faced each other for a month; Lu Bu seized the opening and raided Xiapi.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After a month locked with Yuan Shu, Lu Bu struck Xiapi while Liu Bei's guard was thin.

manualTranslations.zh: 下邳守將曹豹反，閒迎布。
manualTranslations.literal: Xiapi garrison general Cao Bao rebelled and secretly welcomed Bu.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Cao Bao, the Xiapi garrison commander, rebelled and secretly admitted Lu Bu.

manualTranslations.zh: 布虜先主妻子，先主轉軍海西。
manualTranslations.literal: Bu captured the Former Lord's wife and children; the Former Lord shifted his army to Haixi.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Lu Bu seized Liu Bei's wives and children, and Liu Bei withdrew toward Haixi.

manualTranslations.zh: 《英雄記》曰：備留張飛守下邳，引兵與袁術戰於淮陰石亭，更有勝負。
manualTranslations.literal: The Record of Heroes says: Bei left Zhang Fei to guard Xiapi and led troops to fight Yuan Shu at Shiting in Huaiyin; again there were victories and defeats.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Record of Heroes says Liu Bei left Zhang Fei at Xiapi and fought Yuan Shu at Shiting in Huaiyin with mixed results.

manualTranslations.zh: 陶謙故將曹豹在下邳，張飛欲殺之。
manualTranslations.literal: Tao Qian's former general Cao Bao was at Xiapi; Zhang Fei wished to kill him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Tao Qian's old officer Cao Bao was at Xiapi, and Zhang Fei meant to kill him.

manualTranslations.zh: 豹眾堅營自守，使人招呂布。
manualTranslations.literal: Bao's host fortified the camp and held in self-defense; he sent men to summon Lu Bu.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Cao Bao fortified his camp and sent for Lu Bu.

manualTranslations.zh: 布取下邳，張飛敗走。
manualTranslations.literal: Bu took Xiapi; Zhang Fei was defeated and fled.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Lu Bu took Xiapi and Zhang Fei fled in defeat.

manualTranslations.zh: 備聞之，引兵還，比至下邳，兵潰。
manualTranslations.literal: When Bei heard this, he led troops back; by the time he reached Xiapi, the army collapsed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Hearing this, Liu Bei marched back, but his army collapsed before he reached Xiapi.

manualTranslations.zh: 收散卒東取廣陵，與袁術戰，又敗。
manualTranslations.literal: He gathered scattered soldiers and went east to take Guangling; he fought Yuan Shu and was again defeated.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He gathered stragglers and struck east for Guangling, fought Yuan Shu again, and lost again.

manualTranslations.zh: 楊奉、韓暹寇徐、揚閒，先主邀擊，盡斬之。
manualTranslations.literal: Yang Feng and Han Xian raided the borders of Xu and Yang; the Former Lord intercepted and struck them and beheaded them all.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Yang Feng and Han Xian raided the Xu and Yang borderlands, Liu Bei intercepted them and cut them down to the last man.

manualTranslations.zh: 先主求和於呂布，布還其妻子。
manualTranslations.literal: The Former Lord sought peace with Lu Bu; Bu returned his wife and children.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Liu Bei sued for peace with Lu Bu, who returned his wives and children.

manualTranslations.zh: 先主遣關羽守下邳。
manualTranslations.literal: The Former Lord sent Guan Yu to guard Xiapi.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Liu Bei sent Guan Yu to hold Xiapi.

items.acceptedSourceText: 袁紹攻公孫瓚，先主與田楷東屯齊。曹公征徐州，徐州牧陶謙遣使告急於田楷，楷與先主俱救之。時先主自有兵千餘人及幽州烏丸雜胡騎，又略得饑民數千人。既到，謙以丹楊兵四千益先主，先主遂去楷歸謙。謙表先主為豫州刺史，屯小沛。謙病篤，謂別駕麋竺曰：「非劉備不能安此州也。」謙死，竺率州人迎先主，先主未敢當。下邳陳登謂先主曰：「今漢室陵遲，海內傾覆，立功立事，在於今日。彼州殷富，戶口百萬，欲屈使君撫臨州事。」先主曰：「袁公路近在壽春，此君四世五公，海內所歸，君可以州與之。」登曰：「公路驕豪，非治亂之主。今欲為使君合步騎十萬，上可以匡主濟民，成五霸之業，下可以割地守境，書功於竹帛。若使君不見聽許，登亦未敢聽使君也。」北海相孔融謂先主曰：「袁公路豈憂國忘家者邪？冢中枯骨，何足介意。今日之事，百姓與能，天與不取，悔不可追。」先主遂領徐州。《獻帝春秋》曰：陳登等遣使詣袁紹曰：「天降災沴，禍臻鄙州，州將殂殞，生民無主，恐懼姦雄一旦承隙，以貽盟主日昃之憂，輒共奉故平原相劉備府君以為宗主，永使百姓知有依歸。方今寇難縱橫，不遑釋甲，謹遣下吏奔告于執事。」紹答曰：「劉玄德弘雅有信義，今徐州樂戴之，誠副所望也。」袁術來攻先主，先主拒之於盱眙、淮陰。曹公表先主為鎮東將軍，封宜城亭侯，是歲建安元年也。先主與術相持經月，呂布乘虛襲下邳。下邳守將曹豹反，閒迎布。布虜先主妻子，先主轉軍海西。《英雄記》曰：備留張飛守下邳，引兵與袁術戰於淮陰石亭，更有勝負。陶謙故將曹豹在下邳，張飛欲殺之。豹眾堅營自守，使人招呂布。布取下邳，張飛敗走。備聞之，引兵還，比至下邳，兵潰。收散卒東取廣陵，與袁術戰，又敗。楊奉、韓暹寇徐、揚閒，先主邀擊，盡斬之。先主求和於呂布，布還其妻子。先主遣關羽守下邳。

sourceRange.text: __FORCETOC__==後主劉禪==後主諱禪，字公嗣，先主子也。建安二十四年，先主為漢中王，立為王太子。及即尊號，冊曰：「惟章武元年五月辛巳，皇帝若曰：太子禪，朕遭漢運艱難，賊臣篡盜，社稷無主，格人群正，以天明命，朕繼大統。今以禪為皇太子，以承宗廟，祗肅社稷。使使持節丞相亮授印綬，敬聽師傅，行一物而三善皆得焉，可不勉與！」《禮記》曰：行一物而三善者，惟世子而已，其齒於學之謂也。鄭玄日：物猶事也。三年夏四月，先主殂於永安宮。五月，後主襲位於成都，時年十七，尊皇后曰皇太后。大赦，改元。是歲魏黃初四年也。《魏略》曰：初備在小沛，不意曹公卒至，遑遽棄家屬，後奔荊州。禪時年數歲，竄匿，隨人西入漢中，為人所賣。及建安十六年，關中破亂，扶風人劉括避亂入漢中，買得禪，問知其良家子，遂養為子，與娶婦，生一子。初禪與備相失時，識其父字玄德。比舍人有姓簡者，及備得益州而簡為將軍，備遣簡到漢中，舍都邸。禪乃詣簡，簡相檢訊，事皆符驗。簡喜，以語張魯，魯（乃）洗沐送詣益州，備乃立以為太子。初備以諸葛亮為太子太傅，及禪立，以亮為丞相，委以諸事，謂亮曰：「政由葛氏，祭則寡人。」亮亦以禪未閒於政，遂總內外。臣松之案：〈二主妃子傳〉曰“後主生於荊州”，〈後主傳〉云「初即帝位，年十七」，則建安十二年生也。十三年敗於長阪，備棄妻子走，〈趙雲傳〉曰「雲身抱弱子以免」，即後主也。如此，備與禪未嘗相失也。又諸葛亮以禪立之明年領益州牧，其年與主簿杜微書曰「朝廷今年十八」，與禪傳相應，理當非虛。而魚豢云備敗於小沛，禪時年始生，及奔荊州，能識其父字玄德，計當五六歲。備敗於小沛時，建安五年也，至禪初立，首尾二十四年，禪應過二十矣。以事相驗，理不得然。此則《魏略》之妄說，乃至二百餘言，異也！又案諸書記及《諸葛亮集》，亮亦不為太子太傅。建興元年223年夏，臧柯太守朱褒擁郡反。

manualTranslations.literal: The Later Lord's taboo name was Shan, courtesy name Gongsi; he was the Former Lord's son.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Later Lord's taboo name was Shan, styled Gongsi; he was the Former Lord's son.

manualTranslations.zh: 建安二十四年，先主為漢中王，立為王太子。
manualTranslations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year of Jian'an, the Former Lord became King of Hanzhong and installed him as royal crown prince.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In 219 the Former Lord became king of Hanzhong and named him royal heir.

manualTranslations.zh: 及即尊號，冊曰：「惟章武元年五月辛巳，皇帝若曰：太子禪，朕遭漢運艱難，賊臣篡盜，社稷無主，格人群正，以天明命，朕繼大統。
manualTranslations.literal: When he assumed the exalted title, the investiture edict read: "On xinsi in the fifth month of the first year of Zhangwu, the Emperor thus: Crown Prince Shan, We have encountered the Han dynasty's hard straits; wicked ministers usurped and stole; the altars of soil and grain had no lord. Examining the crowd, the upright, by Heaven's bright mandate We succeeded the great succession.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When he took the imperial title, the investiture edict read: "On xinsi in the fifth month of the first year of Zhangwu, the Emperor thus: Crown Prince Shan, We have endured the Han dynasty's hard straits; wicked ministers usurped the throne and the realm stood without a ruler. Surveying the worthy, by Heaven's bright mandate We succeeded to the great succession.

manualTranslations.zh: 今以禪為皇太子，以承宗廟，祗肅社稷。
manualTranslations.literal: Now We make Shan imperial crown prince, to inherit the ancestral temples and reverently secure the altars of soil and grain.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: We now make Shan imperial crown prince, to inherit the ancestral temples and reverently secure the altars of soil and grain.

manualTranslations.zh: 使使持節丞相亮授印綬，敬聽師傅，行一物而三善皆得焉，可不勉與！」
manualTranslations.literal: We send the envoy bearing credentials, Chancellor Liang, to confer the seal and cord. Respectfully heed your tutors—in performing one act the three goods are all obtained; can you not exert yourself?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: We send the credential-bearing envoy, Chancellor Liang, to confer the seal and cord. Respectfully heed your tutors—in performing one act the three goods are all obtained; can you not exert yourself?"

manualTranslations.zh: 《禮記》曰：行一物而三善者，惟世子而已，其齒於學之謂也。
manualTranslations.literal: The Book of Rites says: In performing one act and obtaining the three goods, this applies only to the heir apparent—it means his age at study.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Book of Rites says that performing one act and obtaining the three goods applies only to the heir apparent—it refers to his age at study.

manualTranslations.zh: 鄭玄日：物猶事也。
manualTranslations.literal: Zheng Xuan says: Wu means shi (affair).
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan glosses wu as "affair."

manualTranslations.zh: 三年夏四月，先主殂於永安宮。
manualTranslations.literal: In the fourth month of summer in the third year, the Former Lord died at Yongan Palace.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer in the third year, the Former Lord died at Yongan Palace.

manualTranslations.zh: 五月，後主襲位於成都，時年十七，尊皇后曰皇太后。
manualTranslations.literal: In the fifth month, the Later Lord succeeded to the throne at Chengdu; at the time he was seventeen, and the empress was honored as empress dowager.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the fifth month the Later Lord succeeded at Chengdu at age seventeen; the empress was honored as empress dowager.

manualTranslations.zh: 大赦，改元。
manualTranslations.literal: A general amnesty was proclaimed and the reign title was changed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the reign title.

manualTranslations.zh: 是歲魏黃初四年也。
manualTranslations.literal: That year was the fourth year of Wei's Huangchu.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: That year was the fourth year of Wei's Huangchu era (223).

manualTranslations.zh: 《魏略》曰：初備在小沛，不意曹公卒至，遑遽棄家屬，後奔荊州。
manualTranslations.literal: The Brief Account of Wei states: At first Bei was at Xiaopei; he did not expect Lord Cao to arrive suddenly; in haste he abandoned his family and afterward fled to Jing Province.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Brief Account of Wei records that Bei was at Xiaopei when Lord Cao suddenly appeared; he fled in haste, abandoning his family, and later escaped to Jing Province.

manualTranslations.zh: 禪時年數歲，竄匿，隨人西入漢中，為人所賣。
manualTranslations.literal: Shan was then several years old; he hid himself, followed others west into Hanzhong, and was sold by someone.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Shan was then only a few years old; he hid himself, followed others west into Hanzhong, and was sold into servitude.

manualTranslations.zh: 及建安十六年，關中破亂，扶風人劉括避亂入漢中，買得禪，問知其良家子，遂養為子，與娶婦，生一子。
manualTranslations.literal: When in the sixteenth year of Jian'an Guanzhong was broken in disorder, Liu Kuo of Fufeng, fleeing disorder, entered Hanzhong, bought Shan, questioned and learned he was a good-family child, thereupon raised him as a son, gave him a wife, and fathered a son.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In 211, when Guanzhong fell into chaos, Liu Kuo of Fufeng fled into Hanzhong, bought Shan, learned he came from a respectable family, and raised him as his own son, marrying him off and fathering a grandson.

manualTranslations.zh: 初禪與備相失時，識其父字玄德。
manualTranslations.literal: When Shan and Bei first lost each other, he knew his father's style was Xuande.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Shan and Bei were first separated, he already knew his father's style was Xuande.

manualTranslations.zh: 比舍人有姓簡者，及備得益州而簡為將軍，備遣簡到漢中，舍都邸。
manualTranslations.literal: A neighbor surnamed Jian—when Bei obtained Yizhou and Jian became a general, Bei sent Jian to Hanzhong and lodged at the commandery residence.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: A neighbor surnamed Jian—once Bei took Yizhou and Jian became a general, Bei sent Jian to Hanzhong, where he lodged at the commandery guesthouse.

manualTranslations.zh: 禪乃詣簡，簡相檢訊，事皆符驗。
manualTranslations.literal: Shan thereupon went to Jian; Jian examined and interrogated him, and the facts all matched verification.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Shan went to Jian, who questioned him; every detail checked out.

manualTranslations.zh: 簡喜，以語張魯，魯乃洗沐送詣益州，備乃立以為太子。
manualTranslations.literal: Jian rejoiced and told Zhang Lu; Lu then bathed and groomed him and sent him to Yizhou, and Bei thereupon installed him as crown prince.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Jian rejoiced and told Zhang Lu, who bathed and dressed Shan and sent him on to Yizhou; Bei then installed him as crown prince.

manualTranslations.zh: 初備以諸葛亮為太子太傅，及禪立，以亮為丞相，委以諸事，謂亮曰：「政由葛氏，祭則寡人。」
manualTranslations.literal: At first Bei appointed Zhuge Liang Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince; when Shan was installed, he made Liang chancellor and entrusted him with all affairs, saying to Liang: "Government by the Ge clan; sacrifices by Us alone."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At first Bei had named Zhuge Liang grand tutor of the crown prince; when Shan succeeded, he made Liang chancellor and entrusted him with all affairs, saying: "Let the Ge clan govern; I shall perform the sacrifices alone."

manualTranslations.zh: 亮亦以禪未閒於政，遂總內外。
manualTranslations.literal: Liang also, because Shan was not yet versed in government, thereupon took charge of both inner and outer affairs.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Liang too, seeing that Shan was not yet versed in government, took charge of both court and field.

manualTranslations.zh: 臣松之案：
manualTranslations.literal: Your subject Songzhi submits:
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi submits:

manualTranslations.zh: 〈二主妃子傳〉
manualTranslations.literal: 〈Biographies of the Two Lords' Consorts and Sons〉
manualTranslations.idiomatic: 〈Biographies of the Two Lords' Consorts and Sons〉

manualTranslations.zh: 曰“後主生於荊州”，
manualTranslations.literal: states "the Later Lord was born in Jing Province,"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: states "the Later Lord was born in Jing Province,"

manualTranslations.zh: 〈後主傳〉
manualTranslations.literal: 〈Biography of the Later Lord〉
manualTranslations.idiomatic: 〈Biography of the Later Lord〉

manualTranslations.zh: 云「初即帝位，年十七」，則建安十二年生也。
manualTranslations.literal: says "when he first assumed the imperial throne, age seventeen"—thus he was born in the twelfth year of Jian'an.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: says "when he first took the throne, he was seventeen"—so he was born in the twelfth year of Jian'an (207).

manualTranslations.zh: 十三年敗於長阪，備棄妻子走，
manualTranslations.literal: In the thirteenth year, defeated at Changban, Bei abandoned wife and children and fled,
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In 208, defeated at Changban, Bei abandoned wife and children and fled,

manualTranslations.zh: 〈趙雲傳〉
manualTranslations.literal: 〈Biography of Zhao Yun〉
manualTranslations.idiomatic: 〈Biography of Zhao Yun〉

manualTranslations.zh: 曰「雲身抱弱子以免」，即後主也。
manualTranslations.literal: states "Yun himself embraced the weak child and escaped"—this was the Later Lord.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: records that "Yun himself embraced the infant heir and escaped"—that infant was the Later Lord.

manualTranslations.zh: 如此，備與禪未嘗相失也。
manualTranslations.literal: Thus Bei and Shan never truly lost each other.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On this showing, Bei and Shan were never truly separated.

manualTranslations.zh: 又諸葛亮以禪立之明年領益州牧，其年與主簿杜微書曰「朝廷今年十八」，與禪傳相應，理當非虛。
manualTranslations.literal: Moreover, the year after Shan was installed Zhuge Liang took charge as governor of Yizhou; that year in a letter to chief clerk Du Wei he wrote "the court is eighteen this year"—corresponding with the Later Lord's biography, it surely cannot be false.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Moreover, the year after Shan succeeded, Zhuge Liang took charge as governor of Yizhou; that year he wrote to chief clerk Du Wei that "the court is eighteen this year"—matching the Later Lord's biography, this can hardly be false.

manualTranslations.zh: 而魚豢云備敗於小沛，禪時年始生，及奔荊州，能識其父字玄德，計當五六歲。
manualTranslations.literal: Yet Yu Huan says Bei was defeated at Xiaopei when Shan had just been born, and when fleeing to Jing Province could recognize his father's style Xuande—calculated, he should have been five or six.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yet Yu Huan says Bei was defeated at Xiaopei when Shan had just been born, and that when fleeing to Jing Province the boy could recognize his father's style Xuande—making him five or six at most.

manualTranslations.zh: 備敗於小沛時，建安五年也，至禪初立，首尾二十四年，禪應過二十矣。
manualTranslations.literal: When Bei was defeated at Xiaopei it was the fifth year of Jian'an; from then until Shan's first installation, head to tail twenty-four years—Shan ought to have passed twenty.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Bei's defeat at Xiaopei came in 200; from then until Shan's accession spans twenty-four years—Shan ought to have been past twenty.

manualTranslations.zh: 以事相驗，理不得然。
manualTranslations.literal: Testing by events, the principle cannot be so.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Checked against the facts, that cannot be right.

manualTranslations.zh: 此則《魏略》之妄說，乃至二百餘言，異也！
manualTranslations.literal: This then is the Brief Account of Wei's reckless tale, extending even to more than two hundred words—how strange!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: This is the Brief Account of Wei's reckless tale, running to more than two hundred words—how strange!

manualTranslations.zh: 又案諸書記及《諸葛亮集》，亮亦不為太子太傅。
manualTranslations.literal: Moreover, examining various records and the Collected Works of Zhuge Liang, Liang also was not Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Moreover, various records and the Collected Works of Zhuge Liang show that Liang never served as grand tutor of the crown prince.

manualTranslations.zh: 建興元年223年夏，臧柯太守朱褒擁郡反。
manualTranslations.literal: In the summer of the first year of Jianxing (223), Zhu Bao, Administrator of Zangke, seized the commandery and rebelled.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: That summer of 223, Zhu Bao, prefect of Zangke, rose in revolt and took the commandery for himself.

items.acceptedSourceText: 後主諱禪，字公嗣，先主子也。建安二十四年，先主為漢中王，立為王太子。及即尊號，冊曰：「惟章武元年五月辛巳，皇帝若曰：太子禪，朕遭漢運艱難，賊臣篡盜，社稷無主，格人群正，以天明命，朕繼大統。今以禪為皇太子，以承宗廟，祗肅社稷。使使持節丞相亮授印綬，敬聽師傅，行一物而三善皆得焉，可不勉與！」《禮記》曰：行一物而三善者，惟世子而已，其齒於學之謂也。鄭玄日：物猶事也。三年夏四月，先主殂於永安宮。五月，後主襲位於成都，時年十七，尊皇后曰皇太后。大赦，改元。是歲魏黃初四年也。《魏略》曰：初備在小沛，不意曹公卒至，遑遽棄家屬，後奔荊州。禪時年數歲，竄匿，隨人西入漢中，為人所賣。及建安十六年，關中破亂，扶風人劉括避亂入漢中，買得禪，問知其良家子，遂養為子，與娶婦，生一子。初禪與備相失時，識其父字玄德。比舍人有姓簡者，及備得益州而簡為將軍，備遣簡到漢中，舍都邸。禪乃詣簡，簡相檢訊，事皆符驗。簡喜，以語張魯，魯乃洗沐送詣益州，備乃立以為太子。初備以諸葛亮為太子太傅，及禪立，以亮為丞相，委以諸事，謂亮曰：「政由葛氏，祭則寡人。」亮亦以禪未閒於政，遂總內外。臣松之案：〈二主妃子傳〉曰“後主生於荊州”，〈後主傳〉云「初即帝位，年十七」，則建安十二年生也。十三年敗於長阪，備棄妻子走，〈趙雲傳〉曰「雲身抱弱子以免」，即後主也。如此，備與禪未嘗相失也。又諸葛亮以禪立之明年領益州牧，其年與主簿杜微書曰「朝廷今年十八」，與禪傳相應，理當非虛。而魚豢云備敗於小沛，禪時年始生，及奔荊州，能識其父字玄德，計當五六歲。備敗於小沛時，建安五年也，至禪初立，首尾二十四年，禪應過二十矣。以事相驗，理不得然。此則《魏略》之妄說，乃至二百餘言，異也！又案諸書記及《諸葛亮集》，亮亦不為太子太傅。建興元年223年夏，臧柯太守朱褒擁郡反。

sourceRange.text: 後主舉家東遷，既至洛陽，策命之曰：:惟三月丁亥，皇帝臨軒，使太常嘉命劉禪為安樂縣公。

localRange.text: 後主舉家東遷，既至洛陽，策命之曰：惟景元五年三月丁亥，皇帝臨軒，使太常嘉命劉禪為安樂縣公。

sourceRange.text: 食邑萬戶，賜絹萬匹，奴婢百人，他物稱是。子孫為三都尉封侯者五十餘人。尚書令樊建、侍中張紹、光祿大夫譙周、秘書令卻正、殿中督張通並封列侯。《漢晉春秋》曰：司馬文王與禪宴，為之作故蜀技，旁人皆為之感愴，而禪喜笑自若。王謂賈充曰：「人之無情，乃可至於是乎！雖使諸葛亮在，不能輔之久全，而況姜維邪？」充曰：「不如是，殿下何由並之。」他日，王問禪曰：「頗思蜀否？」禪曰：「此間樂，不思蜀。」郤正聞之，求見禪曰：「若王後問，宜泣而答曰『先人墳墓遠在隴、蜀，乃心西悲，無日不思』，因閉其目。」會王復問，對如前，王曰：「何乃似郤正語邪！」禪驚視曰：「誠如尊命。」左右皆笑。公泰始七年271年薨於洛陽。《蜀記》云：諡曰思公，子恂嗣。

context.beforeSource: 公其只服朕命，克廣德心，以終乃顯烈。

manualTranslations.zh: 食邑萬戶，賜絹萬匹，奴婢百人，他物稱是。
manualTranslations.literal: A fief of ten thousand households; ten thousand bolts of silk bestowed, a hundred male and female servants, other goods in proportion.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His fief held ten thousand households; he received ten thousand bolts of silk, a hundred servants, and comparable gifts besides.

manualTranslations.zh: 子孫為三都尉封侯者五十餘人。
manualTranslations.literal: Descendants who served as commandants of the three divisions and were enfeoffed as marquises numbered more than fifty.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: More than fifty of his descendants who served as commandants of the three divisions were enfeoffed as marquises.

manualTranslations.zh: 尚書令樊建、侍中張紹、光祿大夫譙周、秘書令卻正、殿中督張通並封列侯。
manualTranslations.literal: Director of the Masters of Writing Fan Jian, Palace Attendant Zhang Shao, Household Counsellor Qiao Zhou, Director of the Secretariat Xi Zheng, and Palace Supervisor Zhang Tong were all enfeoffed as full marquises.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Director of the masters of writing Fan Jian, palace attendant Zhang Shao, household counsellor Qiao Zhou, director of the secretariat Xi Zheng, and palace supervisor Zhang Tong were all enfeoffed as full marquises.

manualTranslations.zh: 《漢晉春秋》曰：司馬文王與禪宴，為之作故蜀技，旁人皆為之感愴，而禪喜笑自若。
manualTranslations.literal: The Han–Jin Annals of Spring and Autumn state: Sima Zhao feasted with Shan and had former Shu entertainments performed for him; bystanders were all moved to sorrow, yet Shan rejoiced and laughed as if at ease.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Han–Jin Annals of Spring and Autumn record that Sima Zhao feasted with Shan and had former Shu entertainments performed; bystanders were moved to tears, yet Shan laughed and smiled as if perfectly at ease.

manualTranslations.zh: 王謂賈充曰：「人之無情，乃可至於是乎！
manualTranslations.literal: The King said to Jia Chong: "That a man could be so devoid of feeling—can it really go this far!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The king said to Jia Chong, "Can a man really be so devoid of feeling as this!

manualTranslations.zh: 雖使諸葛亮在，不能輔之久全，而況姜維邪？」
manualTranslations.literal: Even if Zhuge Liang were present, he could not have helped him endure long in safety—how much less Jiang Wei?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Even if Zhuge Liang were still alive, he could not have kept him safe for long—how much less Jiang Wei?"

manualTranslations.zh: 充曰：「不如是，殿下何由並之。」
manualTranslations.literal: Chong said: "If it were not so, Your Highness, by what means would you have annexed him?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Chong replied, "If he were not so, Your Highness, how would you have conquered Shu?"

manualTranslations.zh: 他日，王問禪曰：「頗思蜀否？」
manualTranslations.literal: Another day the King asked Shan: "Do you miss Shu at all?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Another day the king asked Shan, "Do you miss Shu at all?"

manualTranslations.zh: 禪曰：「此間樂，不思蜀。」
manualTranslations.literal: Shan said: "Here is joy; I do not think of Shu."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Shan answered, "Life here is pleasant—I never think of Shu."

manualTranslations.zh: 郤正聞之，求見禪曰：「若王後問，宜泣而答曰『先人墳墓遠在隴、蜀，乃心西悲，無日不思』，因閉其目。」
manualTranslations.literal: Xi Zheng heard this, sought audience with Shan, and said: "If the King later asks, you ought to weep and answer, 'My forebears' graves lie far off in Long and Shu; my heart grieves westward; not a day passes without longing,' and thereby close your eyes."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Xi Zheng heard this and sought audience, advising Shan: "If the king asks again, weep and answer, 'My forebears' graves lie far off in Long and Shu; my heart grieves westward; not a day passes without longing,' and close your eyes as you speak."

manualTranslations.zh: 會王復問，對如前，王曰：「何乃似郤正語邪！」
manualTranslations.literal: When the King again asked, he answered as before; the King said: "Why does this sound like Xi Zheng's words!"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When the king asked again, Shan answered as before. The king said, "Why does this sound like Xi Zheng's coaching!"

manualTranslations.zh: 禪驚視曰：「誠如尊命。」
manualTranslations.literal: Shan looked up in alarm and said: "It is truly as you commanded."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Shan looked up in alarm and said, "It is exactly as you say."

manualTranslations.zh: 左右皆笑。
manualTranslations.literal: Those left and right all laughed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Everyone present burst out laughing.

manualTranslations.zh: 公泰始七年271年薨於洛陽。
manualTranslations.literal: The Duke died at Luoyang in the seventh year of Taishi (271).
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He died at Luoyang in the seventh year of the Taishi era (271).

manualTranslations.zh: 《蜀記》云：諡曰思公，子恂嗣。
manualTranslations.literal: The Records of Shu state: posthumous title Duke Si; his son Xun succeeded.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Records of Shu give his posthumous title as Duke Si; his son Xun succeeded him.

sourceRange.text: 先主穆皇后，陳留人也。兄吳壹，少孤，壹父素與劉焉有舊，是以舉家隨焉入蜀。焉有異志，而聞善相者相后當大貴。焉時將子瑁自隨，遂為瑁納后。瑁死，后寡居。先主既定益州，而孫夫人還吳，《漢晉春秋》云：先主入益州，吳遣迎孫夫人。夫人欲將太子歸吳，諸葛亮使趙雲勒兵斷江留太子，乃得止。群下勸先主聘后，先主疑與瑁同族，法正進曰：「論其親疏，何與晉文之於子圉乎？」於是納后為夫人。習鑿齒曰：夫婚姻，人倫之始，王化之本，匹夫猶不可以無禮，而況人君乎？晉文廢禮行權，以濟其業，故子犯曰，有求於人，必先從之，將奪其國，何有於妻，非無故而違禮教者也。今先主無權事之偪，而引前失以為譬，非導其君以堯、舜之道者。先主從之，過矣。建安二十四年，立為漢中王后。章武元年夏五月，策曰：「朕承天命，奉至尊，臨萬國。今以后為皇后，遣使持節丞相亮授璽綬，承宗廟，母天下，皇后其敬之哉！」建興元年223年五月，後主即位，尊后為皇太后，稱長樂宮。壹官至車騎將軍，封縣侯。延熙八年，后薨，合葬惠陵。孫盛《蜀世譜》曰：壹孫喬，沒李雄中三十年，不為雄屈也。

manualTranslations.zh: 先主穆皇后，陳留人也。
manualTranslations.literal: Empress Mu of the First Lord was a native of Chenliu.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Lady Mu, empress of Liu Bei, came from Chenliu.

manualTranslations.zh: 兄吳壹，少孤，壹父素與劉焉有舊，是以舉家隨焉入蜀。
manualTranslations.literal: Her elder brother was Wu Yi; orphaned young, Yi's father had long been on familiar terms with Liu Yan, and on that account the whole family followed Yan into Shu.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Her brother Wu Yi was orphaned young. Their father had been close to Liu Yan, so the whole family followed Yan into Shu.

manualTranslations.zh: 焉有異志，而聞善相者相后當大貴。
manualTranslations.literal: Yan harbored separate ambitions, and it was heard that a skilled physiognomist predicted the empress would attain great honor.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Liu Yan nurtured separate ambitions, and word came that a physiognomist had foretold the girl would rise to great rank.

manualTranslations.zh: 焉時將子瑁自隨，遂為瑁納后。
manualTranslations.literal: At the time Yan took his son Mao with him; thereupon he had Mao take the empress in marriage.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Liu Yan then had his son Mao marry her.

manualTranslations.zh: 瑁死，后寡居。
manualTranslations.literal: Mao died; the empress lived in widowhood.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Mao died she remained a widow.

manualTranslations.zh: 先主既定益州，而孫夫人還吳，《漢晉春秋》云：先主入益州，吳遣迎孫夫人。
manualTranslations.literal: After the First Lord had settled Yizhou, Lady Sun returned to Wu. The Spring and Autumn of Han and Jin states: When the First Lord entered Yizhou, Wu sent to welcome Lady Sun.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Once Liu Bei held Yizhou, Lady Sun went back to Wu. The Spring and Autumn of Han and Jin says Wu sent to fetch her when Liu Bei entered Yizhou.

manualTranslations.zh: 夫人欲將太子歸吳，諸葛亮使趙雲勒兵斷江留太子，乃得止。
manualTranslations.literal: The lady wished to take the crown prince back to Wu; Zhuge Liang had Zhao Yun draw up troops and block the river to keep the crown prince—only then was it stopped.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: She meant to take the crown prince with her, but Zhuge Liang had Zhao Yun seal the river and keep the boy—only then was she stopped.

manualTranslations.zh: 群下勸先主聘后，先主疑與瑁同族，法正進曰：「論其親疏，何與晉文之於子圉乎？」
manualTranslations.literal: The assembly urged the First Lord to take the empress as bride; the First Lord suspected she was of the same clan as Mao. Fa Zheng advanced and said, "As to degrees of kinship, how does this compare with Duke Wen of Jin and Zi Yu?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His court urged Liu Bei to wed her, but he worried she was kin to Mao. Fa Zheng argued: "By closeness of kin, how does this resemble Duke Wen of Jin and Zi Yu?"

manualTranslations.zh: 於是納后為夫人。
manualTranslations.literal: Thereupon he took the empress in as his lady.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He then took her as consort.

manualTranslations.zh: 習鑿齒曰：夫婚姻，人倫之始，王化之本，匹夫猶不可以無禮，而況人君乎？
manualTranslations.literal: Xi Zaochi said: Marriage is the beginning of human relations and the root of royal transformation; even common men cannot lack ritual—how much more a ruler?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Xi Zaochi wrote: Marriage begins human order and grounds royal civilizing rule; even commoners must observe ritual—how much more a sovereign?

manualTranslations.zh: 晉文廢禮行權，以濟其業，故子犯曰，有求於人，必先從之，將奪其國，何有於妻，非無故而違禮教者也。
manualTranslations.literal: Duke Wen of Jin set ritual aside and exercised expedient power to save his enterprise; hence Zi Fan said: when one has need of others, one must first yield to them; about to seize their state, what care for a wife?—this was not violating ritual teaching without cause.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Duke Wen of Jin set ritual aside and used expedient power to save his cause; hence Zi Fan said that when one needs others one must first yield, and when one is about to seize a state what care is there for a wife?—that was not capricious breach of ritual.

manualTranslations.zh: 今先主無權事之偪，而引前失以為譬，非導其君以堯、舜之道者。
manualTranslations.literal: Now the First Lord had no coercion of expedient affairs, yet cited a past fault as precedent—this is not guiding one's lord by the Way of Yao and Shun.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Liu Bei faced no such coercion, yet Fa Zheng cited an old lapse as precedent—this was not guiding a ruler along the path of Yao and Shun.

manualTranslations.zh: 先主從之，過矣。
manualTranslations.literal: The First Lord followed it—an error.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Liu Bei took the advice—a mistake, in Xi Zaochi's view.

manualTranslations.zh: 建安二十四年，立為漢中王后。
manualTranslations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year of Jian'an she was established as queen of Hanzhong.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Jian'an 24 she was made queen of Hanzhong.

manualTranslations.zh: 章武元年夏五月，策曰：「朕承天命，奉至尊，臨萬國。
manualTranslations.literal: In the fifth month of summer in the first year of Zhangwu the patent read, "We receive Heaven's mandate, hold the supreme dignity, and face the myriad states.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Zhangwu 1 an edict ran: "I receive Heaven's mandate, hold supreme dignity, and rule the myriad states.

manualTranslations.zh: 今以后為皇后，遣使持節丞相亮授璽綬，承宗廟，母天下，皇后其敬之哉！」
manualTranslations.literal: Now We make the empress queen, dispatch envoys bearing the tally for Chancellor Liang to confer seals and ribbons, to receive the ancestral temples and mother the realm—may the empress revere this charge!"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I now make the empress queen, send envoys with the imperial baton for Chancellor Zhuge Liang to confer her seals and cords, that she may receive the ancestral shrines and mother the realm—revere this charge, O empress!"

manualTranslations.zh: 建興元年223年五月，後主即位，尊后為皇太后，稱長樂宮。
manualTranslations.literal: In the fifth month of the first year of Jianxing (223 CE) the Later Lord ascended the throne and honored the empress as empress dowager, with her residence called Changle Palace.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Jianxing 1 (223 CE) Liu Shan succeeded and raised her to empress dowager of Changle Palace.

manualTranslations.zh: 壹官至車騎將軍，封縣侯。
manualTranslations.literal: Yi rose to General of Chariots and Cavalry and was enfeoffed as a district marquis.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wu Yi rose to general of chariots and cavalry and received a district marquisate.

manualTranslations.zh: 延熙八年，后薨，合葬惠陵。
manualTranslations.literal: In the eighth year of Yanxi the empress died and was buried with the First Lord at Huiling.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Yanxi 8 she died and was interred with Liu Bei at Huiling.

manualTranslations.zh: 孫盛《蜀世譜》曰：壹孫喬，沒李雄中三十年，不為雄屈也。
manualTranslations.literal: Sun Sheng's Genealogy of Shu states: Yi's grandson Qiao, captured among Li Xiong's forces for thirty years, would not submit to Xiong.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sun Sheng's Shu genealogy notes that Wu Yi's grandson Qiao, held among Li Xiong's forces for thirty years, never bowed to Xiong.

sourceRange.text: 後主張皇后，前后敬哀之妹也。建興十五年237年，入為貴人。延熙元年238年春正月，策曰：「朕統承大業，君臨天下，奉郊廟社稷。今以貴人為皇后，使行丞相事左將軍向朗持節授璽綬。勉脩中饋，恪肅禋祀，皇后其敬之哉！」咸熙元年，隨後主遷於洛陽。《漢晉春秋》曰：魏以蜀宮人賜諸將之無妻者，李昭儀曰：「我不能二三屈辱。」乃自殺。劉永字公壽，先主子，後主庶弟也。章武元年六月，使司徒靖立永為魯王，策曰：「小子永，受茲青土。朕承天序，繼統大業，遵脩稽古，建爾國家，封於東土，奄有龜蒙，世為籓輔。嗚呼，恭朕之詔！惟彼魯邦，一變適道，風化存焉。人之好德，世茲懿美。王其秉心率禮，綏爾士民，是饗是宜，其戒之哉！」建興八年230年，改封為甘陵王。初，永憎宦人黃皓，皓既信任用事，譖構永於後主，後主稍疏外永，至不得朝見者十餘年。咸熙元年，永東遷洛陽，拜奉車都尉，封為鄉侯。

manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the first month of Yanxi 1 (238 CE) an edict ran: "I inherit the great enterprise, rule the realm, and serve the suburban altars and state shrines.

manualTranslations.idiomatic: Cultivate the inner household and reverently keep the state sacrifices—revere this charge, O empress!"

manualTranslations.zh: 《漢晉春秋》曰：魏以蜀宮人賜諸將之無妻者，李昭儀曰：「我不能二三屈辱。」
manualTranslations.literal: The Spring and Autumn of Han and Jin states: Wei gave Shu palace women to generals without wives; Lady Li, imperial lady of splendid deportment, said, "I cannot endure repeated humiliation."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn of Han and Jin says Wei gave Shu palace women to generals without wives. Lady Li, an imperial lady of splendid deportment, said, "I cannot endure repeated humiliation."

manualTranslations.zh: 乃自殺。
manualTranslations.literal: Thereupon she killed herself.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: She then took her own life.

manualTranslations.zh: 劉永字公壽，先主子，後主庶弟也。
manualTranslations.literal: Liu Yong, courtesy Gongshou, was a son of the First Lord and a younger half-brother of the Later Lord.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Liu Yong, styled Gongshou, was Liu Bei's son and Liu Shan's younger half-brother.

manualTranslations.zh: 章武元年六月，使司徒靖立永為魯王，策曰：「小子永，受茲青土。
manualTranslations.literal: In the sixth month of the first year of Zhangwu the emperor ordered Minister of Education Xu Jing to invest Yong as Prince of Lu; the patent read, "Young Yong, receive this azure soil.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Zhangwu 1 Liu Bei ordered Xu Jing, minister of education, to enfeoff Liu Yong as prince of Lu. The edict ran: "Young Liu Yong, receive this azure soil.

manualTranslations.zh: 朕承天序，繼統大業，遵脩稽古，建爾國家，封於東土，奄有龜蒙，世為籓輔。
manualTranslations.literal: We inherit Heaven's sequence, continue the great enterprise, observe and restore antiquity, establish your state and house, enfeoff you in the eastern lands, embrace Gui and Meng, and make you a feudal bulwark for generations.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I carry on Heaven's line, continue the great enterprise, observe antiquity, establish your state, enfeoff you in the east, embrace Gui and Meng, and make you a feudal shield for generations.

manualTranslations.zh: 嗚呼，恭朕之詔！
manualTranslations.literal: Alas, revere Our edict!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Revere this charge of mine!

manualTranslations.zh: 惟彼魯邦，一變適道，風化存焉。
manualTranslations.literal: That state of Lu, once transformed, was fit for the Way; civilizing transformation abides there.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Lu, once transformed, was fit for the Way; civilizing rule endures there.

manualTranslations.zh: 人之好德，世茲懿美。
manualTranslations.literal: Men's love of virtue there is ever this excellent beauty.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Its people's love of virtue is a lasting excellence.

manualTranslations.zh: 王其秉心率禮，綏爾士民，是饗是宜，其戒之哉！」
manualTranslations.literal: May you, my prince, hold your heart and lead by ritual, pacify your officers and people, receive and keep what is fitting—revere this charge!"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Hold your heart to ritual, pacify your officers and people, receive what is fitting—revere this charge, my prince!"

manualTranslations.zh: 建興八年230年，改封為甘陵王。
manualTranslations.literal: In the eighth year of Jianxing (230 CE) his fief was changed to Prince of Ganling.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Jianxing 8 (230 CE) his title was changed to prince of Ganling.

manualTranslations.zh: 初，永憎宦人黃皓，皓既信任用事，譖構永於後主，後主稍疏外永，至不得朝見者十餘年。
manualTranslations.literal: At first Yong detested the eunuch Huang Hao; once Hao gained trust and wielded power he slandered Yong to the Later Lord, and the Later Lord gradually kept Yong at a distance until for more than ten years he could not attend court audiences.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Liu Yong hated the eunuch Huang Hao. Once Huang Hao gained power he slandered Liu Yong to Liu Shan, who gradually kept him at arm's length until for more than ten years he could not attend court.

manualTranslations.zh: 咸熙元年，永東遷洛陽，拜奉車都尉，封為鄉侯。
manualTranslations.literal: In the first year of Xianxi Yong moved east to Luoyang, was appointed Commandant of the Imperial Carriage, and enfeoffed as a village marquis.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Xianxi 1 Liu Yong went east to Luoyang, became commandant of the imperial carriage, and received a village marquisate.

sourceRange.text: 建興元年223年，封亮武鄉侯，開府治事。頃之，又領益州牧。政事無巨細，咸決於亮。南中諸郡，并皆叛亂，亮以新遭大喪，故未便加兵，且遣使聘吳，因結和親，遂為與國。亮集曰：是歲，魏司徒華歆、司空王朗、尚書令陳群、太史令許芝、謁者僕射諸葛璋各有書與亮，陳天命人事，欲使舉國稱籓。亮遂不報書，作正議曰：「昔在項羽，起不由德，雖處華夏，秉帝者之勢，卒就湯鑊，為後永戒。魏不審鑒，今次之矣；免身為幸，戒在子孫。而二三子各以耆艾之齒，承偽指而進書，有若崇、竦稱莽之功，亦將偪於元禍苟免者邪！昔世祖之創跡舊基，奮羸卒數千，摧莽彊旅四十餘萬於昆陽之郊。夫據道討淫，不在眾寡。及至孟德，以其譎勝之力，舉數十萬之師，救張郃於陽平，勢窮慮悔，僅能自脫，辱其鋒銳之眾，遂喪漢中之地，深知神器不可妄獲，旋還未至，感毒而死。子桓淫逸，繼之以篡。縱使二三子多逞蘇、張詭靡之說，奉進驩兜滔天之辭，欲以誣毀唐帝，諷解禹、稷，所謂徒喪文藻煩勞翰墨者矣。夫大人君子之所不為也。又軍誡曰：『萬人必死，橫行天下。』昔軒轅氏整卒數萬，制四方，定海內，況以數十萬之眾，據正道而臨有罪，可得干擬者哉！」三年春，亮率眾南征，詔賜亮金鈇鉞一具，曲蓋一，前後羽葆鼓吹各一部，虎賁六十人。

manualTranslations.zh: 建興元年223年，封亮武鄉侯，開府治事。
manualTranslations.literal: In the first year of Jianxing (223 CE), Liang was enfeoffed as Marquis of Wuxiang and opened a chancellor's office to handle affairs.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Jianxing 1 (223 CE), Zhuge Liang was enfeoffed as Marquis of Wuxiang and opened a chancellor's office to conduct government.

manualTranslations.zh: 頃之，又領益州牧。
manualTranslations.literal: Before long he also took charge as Governor of Yizhou.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he also assumed the governorship of Yizhou.

manualTranslations.zh: 政事無巨細，咸決於亮。
manualTranslations.literal: Whether the business of government was great or small, all was decided by Liang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Whether state business was great or small, all was decided by Liang.

manualTranslations.zh: 南中諸郡，并皆叛亂，亮以新遭大喪，故未便加兵，且遣使聘吳，因結和親，遂為與國。
manualTranslations.literal: All the commanderies of the southern midlands rebelled at once; because Liang had newly suffered the great bereavement, he was not yet able to send troops, and instead dispatched envoys to court Wu, thereby forming a marriage alliance and becoming a friendly state.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Every commandery in the southern midlands rose in revolt. Because Liang had just suffered the great bereavement, he could not yet march in force; instead he sent envoys to Wu, secured a marriage alliance, and made Shu a friendly state.

manualTranslations.zh: 亮集曰：是歲，魏司徒華歆、司空王朗、尚書令陳群、太史令許芝、謁者僕射諸葛璋各有書與亮，陳天命人事，欲使舉國稱籓。
manualTranslations.literal: Liang's collected writings say: That year, Hua Xin, Minister of Works of Wei, Wang Lang, Minister of Works, Chen Qun, Director of the Masters of Writing, Xu Zhi, Director of Astronomy, and Zhuge Zhang, Master of Ceremonies, each sent Liang a letter expounding Heaven's mandate and human affairs, wishing to make the whole state submit as a vassal.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Liang's collected writings record that year Hua Xin, Wang Lang, Chen Qun, Xu Zhi, and Zhuge Zhang each wrote to him urging submission to Wei on grounds of Heaven's mandate and human affairs, wishing the whole state to declare itself a vassal.

manualTranslations.zh: 亮遂不報書，作正議曰：「昔在項羽，起不由德，雖處華夏，秉帝者之勢，卒就湯鑊，為後永戒。
manualTranslations.literal: Liang did not reply to the letters but composed a Proper Discourse, stating: "In the time of Xiang Yu, he rose without virtue; though he occupied the heartland of China and wielded an emperor's power, he ended in the boiling cauldron, an eternal warning to later ages.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Liang sent no reply but composed a Proper Discourse: "In the time of Xiang Yu, he rose without virtue; though he held the heartland and wielded an emperor's power, he ended in the boiling cauldron—a warning for all later ages.

manualTranslations.zh: 魏不審鑒，今次之矣；
manualTranslations.literal: Wei has failed to take warning and now ranks next.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wei has failed to take warning and now stands next in line.

manualTranslations.zh: 免身為幸，戒在子孫。
manualTranslations.literal: That one escaped with life was fortune; the warning lies with one's descendants.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: To escape with one's life was fortune enough; the warning rests with one's descendants.

manualTranslations.zh: 而二三子各以耆艾之齒，承偽指而進書，有若崇、竦稱莽之功，亦將偪於元禍苟免者邪！
manualTranslations.literal: Yet these two or three men, each with the white hairs of age, carry out false orders in submitting their letters—as if Chong and Song praised Wang Mang's merits—would they too be driven by imminent calamity to seek mere survival?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yet these elders, each with white hair, carry out false orders in their letters—as if Chong and Song praised Wang Mang—are they too driven by imminent calamity to seek bare survival?

manualTranslations.zh: 昔世祖之創跡舊基，奮羸卒數千，摧莽彊旅四十餘萬於昆陽之郊。
manualTranslations.literal: Formerly the Founder Emperor laid his founding trace upon the old foundation, roused a few thousand weary soldiers, and shattered Wang Mang's strong armies of more than four hundred thousand at the outskirts of Kunyang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Formerly the Founder Emperor began from the old foundation, roused a few thousand weary soldiers, and shattered Wang Mang's armies of more than four hundred thousand at Kunyang.

manualTranslations.zh: 夫據道討淫，不在眾寡。
manualTranslations.literal: To hold to the Way and punish wickedness does not depend on numbers.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: To uphold the Way and punish wickedness does not depend on numbers.

manualTranslations.zh: 及至孟德，以其譎勝之力，舉數十萬之師，救張郃於陽平，勢窮慮悔，僅能自脫，辱其鋒銳之眾，遂喪漢中之地，深知神器不可妄獲，旋還未至，感毒而死。
manualTranslations.literal: When it came to Lord Meng, with his power of cunning triumph he raised an army of several hundred thousand to rescue Zhang He at Yangping; his strength exhausted and regret setting in, he barely escaped himself, disgracing his sharp-edged multitudes and losing the territory of Hanzhong; deeply knowing the imperial regalia could not be rashly seized, he turned back but died from poison before arriving.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When it came to Lord Mengde, with his power of cunning he raised hundreds of thousands of troops to rescue Zhang He at Yangping; exhausted and repentant, he barely escaped, disgraced his sharp hosts, and lost Hanzhong; knowing the imperial regalia could not be seized rashly, he turned back but died of poison before arriving.

manualTranslations.zh: 子桓淫逸，繼之以篡。
manualTranslations.literal: Son Huan was dissolute and followed with usurpation.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His son Huan was dissolute and followed with usurpation.

manualTranslations.zh: 縱使二三子多逞蘇、張詭靡之說，奉進驩兜滔天之辭，欲以誣毀唐帝，諷解禹、稷，所謂徒喪文藻煩勞翰墨者矣。
manualTranslations.literal: Even if these two or three men fully deployed the deceitful flattery of Su and Zhang, presenting the sky-filling words of Gun and Dou, wishing thereby to slander the Emperor of Tang and mock Yu and Ji—it is what is called merely wasting literary ornament and wearying the brush.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Even if these men deployed all the deceitful flattery of Su Qin and Zhang Yi, offering the sky-filling words of Gun and Dou to slander the Emperor of Tang and mock Yu and Ji—that is merely wasting ornament and wearying the brush.

manualTranslations.zh: 夫大人君子之所不為也。
manualTranslations.literal: Such things great men and gentlemen do not do.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Such things great men and gentlemen do not do.

manualTranslations.zh: 又軍誡曰：『萬人必死，橫行天下。』
manualTranslations.literal: Moreover the military admonition says: "Ten thousand men resolved on death will march across the realm."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Moreover the military admonition says: "Ten thousand men resolved on death will march across the realm."

manualTranslations.zh: 昔軒轅氏整卒數萬，制四方，定海內，況以數十萬之眾，據正道而臨有罪，可得干擬者哉！」
manualTranslations.literal: Formerly the Yellow Emperor arrayed tens of thousands of soldiers, controlled the four quarters, and settled the realm within the seas—how much more with hundreds of thousands holding the righteous path and confronting the guilty could one be resisted!"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Formerly the Yellow Emperor arrayed tens of thousands of soldiers, controlled the four quarters, and settled the realm within the seas—how much more, with hundreds of thousands holding the righteous path against the guilty, could one be resisted!"

manualTranslations.zh: 三年春，亮率眾南征，詔賜亮金鈇鉞一具，曲蓋一，前後羽葆鼓吹各一部，虎賁六十人。
manualTranslations.literal: In the third year, spring, Liang led the host on a southern expedition; an edict granted Liang one set of golden axes and halberds, one curved canopy, one front and one rear escort with feathered banners, drums, and wind instruments, and sixty tiger guards.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the third year, spring, Liang led the host south on campaign; an edict granted him gilded axes and halberds, a curved canopy, paired bands of feathered banners, drums, and wind instruments, and sixty tiger guards.

sourceRange.text: 瞻字思遠。建興十二年234年，亮出武功，與瑾書曰：「瞻今已八歲，聰慧可愛，嫌其早成，恐不為重器耳。」年十七，尚公主，拜騎都尉。其明年為羽林中郎將，屢遷射聲校尉、侍中、尚書僕射，加軍師將軍。瞻工書畫，強識念，蜀人追思亮，咸愛其才敏。每朝廷有一善政佳事，雖非瞻所建倡，百姓皆傳相告曰：「葛侯之所為也。」是以美聲溢譽，有過其實。景耀四年，為行都護衛將軍，與輔國大將軍南鄉侯董厥并平尚書事。六年冬，魏征西將軍鄧艾伐蜀，自陰平由景谷道旁入。瞻督諸軍至涪停住，前鋒破，退還，住綿竹。艾遣書誘瞻曰：「若降者，必表為琅邪王。」瞻怒，斬艾使。遂戰，大敗，臨陣死，時年三十七。眾皆離散，艾長驅至成都。瞻長子尚，與瞻俱沒。干寶曰：瞻雖智不足以扶危，勇不足以拒敵，而能外不負國，內不改父之志，忠孝存焉。《華陽國志》曰：尚嘆曰：「父子荷國重恩，不早斬黃皓，以致傾敗，用生何為！」乃馳赴魏軍而死。次子京及攀子顯等，咸熙元年內移河東。案《諸葛氏譜》云：京字行宗。《晉泰始起居注》載詔曰：「諸葛亮在蜀，盡其心力，其子瞻臨難而死義，天下之善一也。」其孫京，隨才署吏，後為郿令。尚書僕射山濤《啟事》曰：「郿令諸葛京，祖父亮，遇漢亂分隔，父子在蜀，雖不達天命，要為盡心所事。京治郿自復有稱，臣以為宜以補東宮舍人，以明事人之理，副梁、益之論。」京位至江州刺史。

manualTranslations.literal: Zhan's style name was Siyuan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhuge Zhan, courtesy name Siyuan.

manualTranslations.zh: 建興十二年234年，亮出武功，與瑾書曰：「瞻今已八歲，聰慧可愛，嫌其早成，恐不為重器耳。」
manualTranslations.literal: In the twelfth year of Jianxing (234 CE), when Liang marched from Wugong, he wrote to Jin: "Zhan is now eight years old, clever and lovable; I fear his early maturity and worry he may not become a great vessel."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Jianxing 12 (234 CE), when Liang marched from Wugong, he wrote to Jin: "Zhan is now eight years old, clever and lovable; I fear his early maturity and worry he may not become a great vessel."

manualTranslations.zh: 年十七，尚公主，拜騎都尉。
manualTranslations.literal: At age seventeen he married a princess and was appointed Cavalry Commandant.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At seventeen he married an imperial princess and was appointed cavalry commandant.

manualTranslations.zh: 其明年為羽林中郎將，屢遷射聲校尉、侍中、尚書僕射，加軍師將軍。
manualTranslations.literal: The next year he became Colonel of the Feathered Forest Guard; he was repeatedly transferred to Commandant of the Archers' Guard, Palace Attendant, Vice-Director of the Masters of Writing, and was given the additional title General of the Army.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The next year he became a colonel of the feathered forest guard, then rose through commandant of the archers' guard, palace attendant, and vice-director of the masters of writing, with the additional title army general.

manualTranslations.zh: 瞻工書畫，強識念，蜀人追思亮，咸愛其才敏。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhan was skilled in calligraphy and painting and had a powerful memory; the people of Shu, recalling Liang, all loved his quick talent.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhan excelled at calligraphy and painting and had a powerful memory; the people of Shu, remembering Liang, all loved his quick wit.

manualTranslations.zh: 每朝廷有一善政佳事，雖非瞻所建倡，百姓皆傳相告曰：「葛侯之所為也。」
manualTranslations.literal: Whenever the court had a good policy or fine deed, even if Zhan had not initiated it, the common people would pass word to one another, saying, "This is what Lord Ge did."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Whenever the court enacted a good policy, even if Zhan had not initiated it, the people would tell one another, "This is what Lord Ge did."

manualTranslations.zh: 是以美聲溢譽，有過其實。
manualTranslations.literal: Thus his fine reputation overflowed with praise beyond what was real.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Thus praise for him ran beyond the facts.

manualTranslations.zh: 景耀四年，為行都護衛將軍，與輔國大將軍南鄉侯董厥并平尚書事。
manualTranslations.literal: In the fourth year of Jingyao he became Acting General Who Guards and Protects the Capital and jointly balanced the affairs of the Masters of Writing with Dong Jue, General Who Assists the State and Marquis of Nanxiang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Jingyao 4 he became acting general who guards and protects the capital and jointly handled the masters of writing with Dong Jue, general who assists the state and Marquis of Nanxiang.

manualTranslations.zh: 六年冬，魏征西將軍鄧艾伐蜀，自陰平由景谷道旁入。
manualTranslations.literal: In the winter of the sixth year, Deng Ai, General Who Conquers the West of Wei, attacked Shu, entering by way of Yinping along a side path through Jinggu.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the winter of the sixth year, Deng Ai, Wei's general who conquers the west, attacked Shu, entering from Yinping by a side path through Jinggu.

manualTranslations.zh: 瞻督諸軍至涪停住，前鋒破，退還，住綿竹。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhan directed the armies to Fu and halted; the vanguard was broken, and he withdrew and encamped at Mianzhu.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhan led the armies to Fu and halted; when the vanguard was broken he fell back to Mianzhu.

manualTranslations.zh: 艾遣書誘瞻曰：「若降者，必表為琅邪王。」
manualTranslations.literal: Ai sent a letter to entice Zhan, saying, "If you surrender, I will surely memorialize to make you King of Langye."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Ai sent a letter tempting Zhan: "If you surrender, I will memorialize to make you King of Langye."

manualTranslations.zh: 瞻怒，斬艾使。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhan was enraged and executed Ai's envoy.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhan was enraged and executed Ai's envoy.

manualTranslations.zh: 遂戰，大敗，臨陣死，時年三十七。
manualTranslations.literal: Then they fought; he was utterly defeated and died on the battlefield, aged thirty-seven.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: They fought; he was utterly defeated and died on the field, aged thirty-seven.

manualTranslations.zh: 眾皆離散，艾長驅至成都。
manualTranslations.literal: The host all scattered, and Ai drove straight through to Chengdu.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The armies scattered, and Ai drove straight to Chengdu.

manualTranslations.zh: 瞻長子尚，與瞻俱沒。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhan's eldest son Shang perished together with Zhan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhan's eldest son Shang died with him.

manualTranslations.zh: 干寶曰：瞻雖智不足以扶危，勇不足以拒敵，而能外不負國，內不改父之志，忠孝存焉。
manualTranslations.literal: Gan Bao says: Although Zhan's wisdom was insufficient to rescue the crisis and his courage insufficient to repel the enemy, he could outwardly not betray the state and inwardly not alter his father's resolve—loyalty and filial piety remained in him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Gan Bao writes: Though Zhan's wisdom could not save the crisis and his courage could not repel the enemy, he did not betray the state outwardly or abandon his father's resolve inwardly—loyalty and filial piety remained.

manualTranslations.zh: 《華陽國志》曰：尚嘆曰：「父子荷國重恩，不早斬黃皓，以致傾敗，用生何為！」
manualTranslations.literal: The Huayang Guozhi says: Shang sighed and said, "Father and son bore the state's heavy grace; by not executing Huang Hao early we brought ruin—what use is life!"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Huayang Guozhi records that Shang sighed: "Father and son bore the state's heavy grace; by not executing Huang Hao early we brought ruin—what use is life!"

manualTranslations.zh: 乃馳赴魏軍而死。
manualTranslations.literal: Thereupon he galloped to the Wei army and died.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He then galloped to the Wei army and died.

manualTranslations.zh: 次子京及攀子顯等，咸熙元年內移河東。
manualTranslations.literal: The second son Jing and Pan's son Xian and others were moved inland to Hedong in the first year of Xianxi.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The second son Jing and Pan's son Xian and others were moved inland to Hedong in Xianxi 1.

manualTranslations.zh: 案《諸葛氏譜》云：京字行宗。
manualTranslations.literal: According to the Zhuge clan genealogy: Jing's style name was Xingzong.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Zhuge clan genealogy records that Jing's courtesy name was Xingzong.

manualTranslations.zh: 《晉泰始起居注》載詔曰：「諸葛亮在蜀，盡其心力，其子瞻臨難而死義，天下之善一也。」
manualTranslations.literal: The Jin Daily Notes of Taishi record an edict: "Zhuge Liang in Shu exhausted his heart and strength; his son Zhan faced hardship and died in righteousness—one of the realm's goods."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Jin Daily Notes of Taishi record an edict: "Zhuge Liang in Shu gave his whole heart and strength; his son Zhan faced hardship and died in righteousness—one of the realm's goods."

manualTranslations.zh: 其孫京，隨才署吏，後為郿令。
manualTranslations.literal: His grandson Jing, according to his talent, was appointed an official and later became magistrate of Mei.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His grandson Jing was appointed an official according to his talent and later became magistrate of Mei.

manualTranslations.zh: 尚書僕射山濤《啟事》曰：「郿令諸葛京，祖父亮，遇漢亂分隔，父子在蜀，雖不達天命，要為盡心所事。
manualTranslations.literal: Shan Tao, Vice-Director of the Masters of Writing, in a memorial states: "Zhuge Jing, magistrate of Mei—his grandfather was Liang; encountering Han disorder and separation, father and son were in Shu; though they did not attain Heaven's mandate, they gave their utmost in service.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Shan Tao, vice-director of the masters of writing, wrote in a memorial: "Zhuge Jing, magistrate of Mei—his grandfather was Liang; when Han disorder separated the realm, father and son were in Shu; though they did not attain Heaven's mandate, they gave their utmost in service.

manualTranslations.zh: 京治郿自復有稱，臣以為宜以補東宮舍人，以明事人之理，副梁、益之論。」
manualTranslations.literal: Jing's administration of Mei has won praise on its own; your servant thinks he should be appointed Eastern Palace Attendant to make clear the principle of serving others and accord with the discourse on Liang and Yi."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Jing's administration of Mei has won praise; I think he should be appointed eastern palace attendant to make clear the principle of serving others and accord with the discourse on Liang and Yi."

manualTranslations.zh: 京位至江州刺史。
manualTranslations.literal: Jing rose to the post of Inspector of Jiangzhou.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Jing rose to inspector of Jiangzhou.

sourceRange.text: 先主自葭萌還攻劉璋，召諸葛亮。亮率雲與張飛等俱溯江西上，平定郡縣。至江州，分遣雲從外水上江陽，與亮會於成都。成都既定，以雲為翊軍將軍。雲別傳曰：益州既定，時議欲以成都中屋舍及城外園地桑田分賜諸將。雲駮之曰：「霍去病以匈奴未滅，無用家為，令國賊非但匈奴，未可求安也。須天下都定，各反桑梓，歸耕本土，乃其宜耳。益州人民，初罹兵革，田宅皆可歸還，今安居複業，然後可役調，得其歡心。」先主即從之。夏侯淵敗，曹公爭漢中地，運米北山下，數千萬囊。黃忠以為可取，雲兵隨忠取米。忠過期不還，雲將數十騎輕行出圍，迎視忠等。值曹公揚兵大出，雲為公前鋒所擊，方戰，其大眾至，勢偪，遂前突其陳，且鬥且卻。公軍散，已復合，雲陷敵，還趣圍。將張著被創，雲復馳馬還營迎著。公軍追至圍，此時沔陽長張翼在雲圍內，翼欲閉門拒守，而雲入營，更大開門，偃旗息鼓。公軍疑雲有伏兵，引去。雲雷鼓震天，惟以戎弩於後射公軍，公軍驚駭，自相蹂踐，墮漢水中死者甚多。先主明旦自來至雲營圍視昨戰處，曰：「子龍一身都是膽也。」作樂飲宴至暝，軍中號雲為虎威將軍。孫權襲荊州，先主大怒，欲討權。雲諫曰：「國賊是曹操，非孫權也，且先滅魏，則吳自服。操身雖斃，子丕篡盜，當因眾心，早圖關中，居河、渭上流以討凶逆，關東義士必裹糧策馬以迎王師。不應置魏，先與吳戰；兵勢一交，不得卒解。」先主不聽，遂東征，留雲督江州。先主失利於秭歸，雲進兵至永安，吳軍已退。建興元年223年，為中護軍、征南將軍，封永昌亭侯，遷鎮東將軍。五年，隨諸葛亮駐漢中。明年，亮出軍，揚聲由斜谷道，曹真遣大眾當之。亮令雲與鄧芝往拒，而身攻祁山。雲、芝兵弱敵強，失利於箕谷，然斂眾固守，不至大敗。軍退，貶為鎮軍將軍。雲別傳曰：亮曰：「街亭軍退，兵將不復相錄，箕穀軍退，兵將初不相失，何故？」芝答曰：「雲身自斷後，軍資什物，略無所棄，兵將無緣相失。」雲有軍資餘絹，亮使分賜將士，雲曰：「軍事無利，何為有賜？其物請悉入赤岸府庫，須十月為冬賜。」亮大善之。

context.afterSource: 七年卒，追諡順平侯。

manualTranslations.zh: 先主自葭萌還攻劉璋，召諸葛亮。
manualTranslations.literal: The First Lord returned from Jiameng to attack Liu Zhang and summoned Zhuge Liang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The First Lord marched back from Jiameng against Liu Zhang and called up Zhuge Liang.

manualTranslations.zh: 亮率雲與張飛等俱溯江西上，平定郡縣。
manualTranslations.literal: Liang led Yun together with Zhang Fei and others alike upriver west, pacifying commanderies and districts.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang took Zhao Yun, Zhang Fei, and the rest up the river westward, reducing counties as they went.

manualTranslations.zh: 至江州，分遣雲從外水上江陽，與亮會於成都。
manualTranslations.literal: Reaching Jiangzhou, he separately dispatched Yun from the outer waters up to Jiangyang to meet Liang at Chengdu.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At Jiangzhou he detached Zhao Yun up the outer water route to Jiangyang to rendezvous with Zhuge Liang at Chengdu.

manualTranslations.zh: 成都既定，以雲為翊軍將軍。
manualTranslations.literal: When Chengdu was settled, he made Yun General Who Aids the Army.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Once Chengdu was secure, he named Zhao Yun General Who Aids the Army.

manualTranslations.zh: 雲別傳曰：益州既定，時議欲以成都中屋舍及城外園地桑田分賜諸將。
manualTranslations.literal: The Zhao Yun biezhuan states: When Yizhou was settled, at the time there was discussion of wanting to divide and grant to the various generals the houses within Chengdu and the garden lands and mulberry fields outside the walls.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Zhao Yun biezhuan records that after Yizhou was pacified, some proposed dividing Chengdu houses and suburban gardens and mulberry fields among the generals.

manualTranslations.zh: 雲駮之曰：「霍去病以匈奴未滅，無用家為，令國賊非但匈奴，未可求安也。
manualTranslations.literal: Yun rebutted, saying, "Huo Qubing, because the Xiongnu were not yet destroyed, had no use for a home; now the state's enemy is not only the Xiongnu—one cannot seek ease.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhao Yun objected: "Huo Qubing said that while the Xiongnu still lived, a man had no business building a home; our state's foe is not the Xiongnu alone—we cannot settle into comfort yet.

manualTranslations.zh: 須天下都定，各反桑梓，歸耕本土，乃其宜耳。
manualTranslations.literal: Only when all under Heaven is fully settled should each return to his native place and go back to farm his homeland—that is fitting.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Only when the realm is wholly at peace should each man return home and till his own fields—that is the proper course."

manualTranslations.zh: 益州人民，初罹兵革，田宅皆可歸還，今安居複業，然後可役調，得其歡心。」
manualTranslations.literal: The people of Yizhou had just suffered war; fields and dwellings can all be returned; now let them settle and resume their occupations, and only then can levies and corvée be imposed to win their hearts."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The people of Yizhou have only just endured war; their fields and homes should be restored. Let them settle and resume their livelihoods first—only then levy service and taxes and win their goodwill."

manualTranslations.zh: 先主即從之。
manualTranslations.literal: The First Lord at once followed this advice.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The First Lord accepted the advice at once.

manualTranslations.zh: 夏侯淵敗，曹公爭漢中地，運米北山下，數千萬囊。
manualTranslations.literal: Xiahou Yuan was defeated; Lord Cao contested Hanzhong territory and transported grain to the foot of North Mountain—tens of millions of sacks.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After Xiahou Yuan's defeat, Lord Cao fought for Hanzhong and hauled grain in tens of millions of sacks to the foot of North Mountain.

manualTranslations.zh: 黃忠以為可取，雲兵隨忠取米。
manualTranslations.literal: Huang Zhong thought it could be taken; Yun's troops followed Zhong to seize the grain.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Huang Zhong judged the stores ripe for the taking, and Zhao Yun's men went with him to seize the grain.

manualTranslations.zh: 忠過期不還，雲將數十騎輕行出圍，迎視忠等。
manualTranslations.literal: When Zhong passed the deadline and did not return, Yun led several dozen horsemen on a light sortie out of the encampment to meet and look in on Zhong and the others.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Huang Zhong failed to return on time, Zhao Yun took a few dozen horsemen on a swift ride out of camp to find him.

manualTranslations.zh: 值曹公揚兵大出，雲為公前鋒所擊，方戰，其大眾至，勢偪，遂前突其陳，且鬥且卻。
manualTranslations.literal: He encountered Lord Cao raising troops and coming out in force; Yun was struck by the Lord's vanguard. As he was fighting, the enemy's main force arrived; the situation pressed hard, so he charged forward into their formation, fighting as he retreated.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Lord Cao marched out in strength; Zhao Yun collided with the vanguard and, as the main host closed in, drove into the enemy line while fighting his way back.

manualTranslations.zh: 公軍散，已復合，雲陷敵，還趣圍。
manualTranslations.literal: The Lord's army scattered, then rallied again; Yun was cut off among the enemy and turned back toward the encampment.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Wei ranks broke, then re-formed; Zhao Yun was trapped among the enemy and wheeled back toward his camp.

manualTranslations.zh: 將張著被創，雲復馳馬還營迎著。
manualTranslations.literal: General Zhang Zhu was wounded; Yun again galloped back to camp to receive Zhu.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: General Zhang Zhu was wounded, and Zhao Yun galloped back into camp to bring him out.

manualTranslations.zh: 公軍追至圍，此時沔陽長張翼在雲圍內，翼欲閉門拒守，而雲入營，更大開門，偃旗息鼓。
manualTranslations.literal: The Lord's army pursued to the encampment. At that time Zhang Yi, magistrate of Mianyang, was inside Yun's encampment and wished to close the gate and hold in defense; but Yun entered the camp and instead opened the gate wide, lowered the banners, and silenced the drums.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wei troops pressed to the stockade. Zhang Yi, magistrate of Mianyang, was inside and meant to shut the gates; Zhao Yun entered, threw the gates wide, lowered the banners, and silenced the drums.

manualTranslations.zh: 公軍疑雲有伏兵，引去。
manualTranslations.literal: The Lord's army suspected Yun had ambush troops and withdrew.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Wei army suspected an ambush and withdrew.

manualTranslations.zh: 雲雷鼓震天，惟以戎弩於後射公軍，公軍驚駭，自相蹂踐，墮漢水中死者甚多。
manualTranslations.literal: Yun thundered the drums to shake heaven and with crossbows alone shot at the Lord's army from behind; the Lord's army was shocked and terrified, trampled one another, and many fell into the Han River and died.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhao Yun rolled the drums to heaven and raked the retreating Wei ranks with crossbows from the rear; panic broke their lines, and many drowned in the Han River.

manualTranslations.zh: 先主明旦自來至雲營圍視昨戰處，曰：「子龍一身都是膽也。」
manualTranslations.literal: The next morning the First Lord came in person to Yun's encampment to view yesterday's battlefield and said, "Zilong's whole body is courage."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The next morning the First Lord came in person to Zhao Yun's camp to see the field of battle and said, "Zilong is courage from head to foot."

manualTranslations.zh: 作樂飲宴至暝，軍中號雲為虎威將軍。
manualTranslations.literal: Music was made and a banquet held until dusk; in the army Yun was styled General Who Displays Tiger Might.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: There was music and feasting until dusk, and the army styled Zhao Yun General Who Displays Tiger Might.

manualTranslations.zh: 孫權襲荊州，先主大怒，欲討權。
manualTranslations.literal: Sun Quan raided Jing Province; the First Lord was greatly enraged and wished to campaign against Quan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Sun Quan seized Jing Province, the First Lord was furious and meant to march against him.

manualTranslations.zh: 雲諫曰：「國賊是曹操，非孫權也，且先滅魏，則吳自服。
manualTranslations.literal: Yun remonstrated, saying, "The state's enemy is Cao Cao, not Sun Quan; moreover, if Wei is destroyed first, then Wu will submit of itself.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhao Yun remonstrated: "The state's enemy is Cao Cao, not Sun Quan. Destroy Wei first and Wu will submit of itself.

manualTranslations.zh: 操身雖斃，子丕篡盜，當因眾心，早圖關中，居河、渭上流以討凶逆，關東義士必裹糧策馬以迎王師。
manualTranslations.literal: Though Cao's person has perished, his son Pi usurped and stole the throne; one should follow the people's hearts, plan early for Guanzhong, hold the upper reaches of the He and Wei rivers to campaign against the traitors, and the righteous men east of the Pass will surely wrap grain and spur their horses to welcome the royal army.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Though Cao Cao is dead, his son Pi has usurped the throne. Seize the people's will, take Guanzhong early, hold the upper He and Wei, and march against the traitors—the righteous east of the Pass will saddle up with grain to welcome the royal army.

manualTranslations.zh: 不應置魏，先與吳戰；
manualTranslations.literal: One should not set Wei aside and fight Wu first;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Do not set Wei aside to fight Wu first;

manualTranslations.zh: 兵勢一交，不得卒解。」
manualTranslations.literal: once military momentum is joined, it cannot be quickly resolved."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: once arms are joined, the war cannot quickly be ended."

manualTranslations.zh: 先主不聽，遂東征，留雲督江州。
manualTranslations.literal: The First Lord did not heed this and thereupon campaigned east, leaving Yun to oversee Jiangzhou.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The First Lord would not listen and marched east, leaving Zhao Yun to oversee Jiangzhou.

manualTranslations.zh: 先主失利於秭歸，雲進兵至永安，吳軍已退。
manualTranslations.literal: The First Lord met defeat at Zigui; Yun advanced to Yong'an and the Wu army had already withdrawn.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After the First Lord's defeat at Zigui, Zhao Yun advanced to Yong'an and found the Wu army already gone.

manualTranslations.zh: 建興元年，為中護軍、征南將軍，封永昌亭侯，遷鎮東將軍。
manualTranslations.literal: In the first year of Jianxing he became Central Protector of the Army and General Who Conquers the South, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yongchang precinct, and was transferred to General Who Guards the East.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Jianxing 1 (223) he became central protector of the army and general who conquers the south, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yongchang precinct, and rose to general who guards the east.

manualTranslations.zh: 五年，隨諸葛亮駐漢中。
manualTranslations.literal: In the fifth year he followed Zhuge Liang in garrisoning Hanzhong.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he followed Zhuge Liang to garrison Hanzhong.

manualTranslations.zh: 明年，亮出軍，揚聲由斜谷道，曹真遣大眾當之。
manualTranslations.literal: The next year Liang marched out, publicly declaring he would take the Xie Valley route; Cao Zhen sent a large force to oppose him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The next year Zhuge Liang marched out, loudly declaring the Xie Valley route; Cao Zhen sent a great host to meet him.

manualTranslations.zh: 亮令雲與鄧芝往拒，而身攻祁山。
manualTranslations.literal: Liang ordered Yun and Deng Zhi to go resist while he himself attacked Mount Qi.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang sent Zhao Yun and Deng Zhi to hold the line while he struck Qishan himself.

manualTranslations.zh: 雲、芝兵弱敵強，失利於箕谷，然斂眾固守，不至大敗。
manualTranslations.literal: Yun and Zhi's troops were weak and the enemy strong; they met defeat at Jigu, yet gathered the force and held firm without suffering great defeat.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhao Yun and Deng Zhi were outmatched and lost at Jigu, yet gathered their men, held firm, and escaped catastrophe.

manualTranslations.zh: 軍退，貶為鎮軍將軍。
manualTranslations.literal: When the army withdrew, he was demoted to General Who Guards the Army.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After the withdrawal he was demoted to general who guards the army.

manualTranslations.zh: 雲別傳曰：亮曰：「街亭軍退，兵將不復相錄，箕穀軍退，兵將初不相失，何故？」
manualTranslations.literal: The Zhao Yun biezhuan states: Liang said, "When the Jieting army withdrew, soldiers and generals could no longer find one another; when the Jigu army withdrew, soldiers and generals at first did not lose one another—why?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Zhao Yun biezhuan records Zhuge Liang saying, "At Jieting the army broke and officers and men could not find one another; at Jigu the army withdrew yet officers and men never lost one another—why?"

manualTranslations.zh: 芝答曰：「雲身自斷後，軍資什物，略無所棄，兵將無緣相失。」
manualTranslations.literal: Zhi answered, "Yun personally covered the retreat; army supplies and goods were almost nothing abandoned—soldiers and generals had no occasion to lose one another."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Deng Zhi answered, "Zhao Yun covered the retreat himself; stores and gear were scarcely abandoned—officers and men had no chance to lose one another."

manualTranslations.zh: 雲有軍資餘絹，亮使分賜將士，雲曰：「軍事無利，何為有賜？
manualTranslations.literal: Yun had surplus silk from army supplies; Liang had it divided and granted to officers and soldiers. Yun said, "The military campaign brought no gain—why should there be gifts?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhao Yun still held surplus army silk; Zhuge Liang had it divided among the officers and soldiers. Zhao Yun said, "The campaign brought no gain—why grant gifts?

manualTranslations.zh: 其物請悉入赤岸府庫，須十月為冬賜。」
manualTranslations.literal: Please put all these goods into the Chian office storehouses and wait until the tenth month for the winter grant."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Put it all in the Chian treasury and hold it for the winter grant in the tenth month."

manualTranslations.zh: 亮大善之。
manualTranslations.literal: Liang greatly approved of this.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang greatly approved.

items.acceptedSourceText: 先主自葭萌還攻劉璋，召諸葛亮。亮率雲與張飛等俱溯江西上，平定郡縣。至江州，分遣雲從外水上江陽，與亮會於成都。成都既定，以雲為翊軍將軍。雲別傳曰：益州既定，時議欲以成都中屋舍及城外園地桑田分賜諸將。雲駮之曰：「霍去病以匈奴未滅，無用家為，令國賊非但匈奴，未可求安也。須天下都定，各反桑梓，歸耕本土，乃其宜耳。益州人民，初罹兵革，田宅皆可歸還，今安居複業，然後可役調，得其歡心。」先主即從之。夏侯淵敗，曹公爭漢中地，運米北山下，數千萬囊。黃忠以為可取，雲兵隨忠取米。忠過期不還，雲將數十騎輕行出圍，迎視忠等。值曹公揚兵大出，雲為公前鋒所擊，方戰，其大眾至，勢偪，遂前突其陳，且鬥且卻。公軍散，已復合，雲陷敵，還趣圍。將張著被創，雲復馳馬還營迎著。公軍追至圍，此時沔陽長張翼在雲圍內，翼欲閉門拒守，而雲入營，更大開門，偃旗息鼓。公軍疑雲有伏兵，引去。雲雷鼓震天，惟以戎弩於後射公軍，公軍驚駭，自相蹂踐，墮漢水中死者甚多。先主明旦自來至雲營圍視昨戰處，曰：「子龍一身都是膽也。」作樂飲宴至暝，軍中號雲為虎威將軍。孫權襲荊州，先主大怒，欲討權。雲諫曰：「國賊是曹操，非孫權也，且先滅魏，則吳自服。操身雖斃，子丕篡盜，當因眾心，早圖關中，居河、渭上流以討凶逆，關東義士必裹糧策馬以迎王師。不應置魏，先與吳戰；兵勢一交，不得卒解。」先主不聽，遂東征，留雲督江州。先主失利於秭歸，雲進兵至永安，吳軍已退。建興元年，為中護軍、征南將軍，封永昌亭侯，遷鎮東將軍。五年，隨諸葛亮駐漢中。明年，亮出軍，揚聲由斜谷道，曹真遣大眾當之。亮令雲與鄧芝往拒，而身攻祁山。雲、芝兵弱敵強，失利於箕谷，然斂眾固守，不至大敗。軍退，貶為鎮軍將軍。雲別傳曰：亮曰：「街亭軍退，兵將不復相錄，箕穀軍退，兵將初不相失，何故？」芝答曰：「雲身自斷後，軍資什物，略無所棄，兵將無緣相失。」雲有軍資餘絹，亮使分賜將士，雲曰：「軍事無利，何為有賜？其物請悉入赤岸府庫，須十月為冬賜。」亮大善之。

sourceRange.text: 曹公破張魯，留夏侯淵、張郃守漢川。郃別督諸軍下巴西，欲徙其民於漢中，進軍宕渠、蒙頭、蕩石，與飛相拒五十餘日。飛率精卒萬餘人，從他道邀郃軍交戰，山道迮狹，前後不得相救，飛遂破郃。郃棄馬緣山，獨與麾下十餘人從間道退，引軍還南鄭，巴土獲安。先主為漢中王，拜飛為右將軍、假節。章武元年，遷車騎將軍，領司隸校尉，進封西鄉侯，策曰：「朕承天序，嗣奉洪業，除殘靖亂，未燭厥理。今寇虜作害，民被荼毒，思漢之士，延頸鶴望。朕用怛然，坐不安席，食不甘味，整軍誥誓，將行天罰。以君忠毅，侔蹤召、虎，名宣遐邇，故特顯命，高墉進爵，兼司於京。其誕將天威，柔服以德，伐叛以刑，稱朕意焉。詩不云乎，『匪疚匪棘，王國來極。肇敏戎功，用錫爾祉』。可不勉歟！

items.acceptedSourceText: 曹公破張魯，留夏侯淵、張郃守漢川。郃別督諸軍下巴西，欲徙其民於漢中，進軍宕渠、蒙頭、蕩石，與飛相拒五十餘日。飛率精卒萬餘人，從他道邀郃軍交戰，山道迮狹，前後不得相救，飛遂破郃。郃棄馬緣山，獨與麾下十餘人從間道退，引軍還南鄭，巴土獲安。先主為漢中王，拜飛為右將軍、假節。章武元年，遷車騎將軍，領司隸校尉，進封西鄉侯，策曰：「朕承天序，嗣奉洪業，除殘靖亂，未燭厥理。今寇虜作害，民被荼毒，思漢之士，延頸鶴望。朕用怛然，坐不安席，食不甘味，整軍誥誓，將行天罰。以君忠毅，侔蹤召、虎，名宣遐邇，故特顯命，高墉進爵，兼司於京。其誕將天威，柔服以德，伐叛以刑，稱朕意焉。詩不云乎，『匪疚匪棘，王國來極。肇敏戎功，用錫爾祉』。可不勉歟！」

sourceRange.text: 」靖雖年逾七十，愛樂人物，誘納后進，清談不倦。丞相諸葛亮皆為之拜。章武二年卒。子欽，先靖夭沒。欽子游，景耀中為尚書。始靖兄事颍川陳紀，與陳郡袁渙、平原華歆、東海王朗等親善，歆、朗及紀子群，魏初為公輔大臣，咸與靖書，申陳舊好，情義款至，文多故不載。《魏略》：王朗與文休書曰：「文休足下：消息平安，甚善甚善。豈意脫別三十餘年而無相見之緣乎！詩人比一日之別於歲月，豈況悠悠歷累紀之年者哉！自與子別，若沒而復浮，若絕而復連者數矣。而今而後，居昇平之京師，攀附於飛龍之聖主；儕輩略盡，幸得老與足下併為遺種之叟，而相去數千里，加有邅蹇之隔，時聞消息於風聲，託舊情於思想，眇眇異處，與異世無以異也。往者隨軍到荊州，見鄧子孝、桓元將，粗聞足下動靜，云夫子既在益州，執職領郡，德素規矩，老而不墮。是時侍宿武皇帝於江陵劉景升聽事之上，共道足下於通夜，拳拳饑渴，誠無已也。自天子在東宮，及即位之後，每會群賢，論天下髦雋之見在者，豈獨人盡易為英，士鮮易取最，故乃猥以原壤之朽質，感夫子之情聽；每敘足下，以為謀首，豈其注意，乃復過於前世，書曰『人惟求舊』，易稱『同聲相應，同氣相求』，劉將軍之與大魏，兼而兩之，總此二義。前世邂逅，以同為睽，非武皇帝之旨；頃者蹉跌，其泰而否，亦非足下之意也。深思書、易之義，利結分於宿好，故遣降者送吳所獻致名馬、貂、罽，得因無嫌。道初開通，展敘舊情，以達聲問。久闊情慉，非夫筆墨所能寫陳，亦想足下同其志念。今者，親生男女凡有幾人？年並幾何？僕連失一男一女，今有二男：大兒名肅，年二十九，生於會稽；小兒裁歲餘。臨書愴悢，有懷緬然。」又曰：「過聞『受終於文祖』之言於尚書。又聞『曆數在躬，允執其中』之文於論語。豈自意得於老耄之齒，正值天命受於聖主之會，親見三讓之弘辭，觀眾瑞之總集，睹升堂穆穆之盛禮，瞻燔燎焜曜之青煙；於時忽自以為處唐、虞之運，際於紫微之天庭也。徒慨不得攜子之手，共列於（世）有二子之數，以聽有唐『欽哉』之命也。子雖在裔土，想亦極目而回望，側耳而遐聽，延頸而鶴立也。昔汝南陳公初拜，不依故常，讓上卿於李元禮。以此推之，吾宜退身以避子位也。苟得避子以竊讓名，然後（綬）帶委質，游談於平、勃之間，與子共陳往時避地之艱辛，樂酒酣宴，高談大噱，亦足遺憂而忘老。捉筆陳情，隨以喜笑。」又曰：「前夏有書而未達，今重有書，而並致前問。皇帝既深悼劉將軍之早世，又愍其孤之不易，又惜使足下孔明等士人氣類之徒，遂沈溺於羌夷異種之間，永與華夏乖絕，而無朝聘中國之期緣，瞻睎故土桑梓之望也，故復運慈念而勞仁心，重下明詔以發德音，申敕朗等，使重為書與足下等。以足下聰明，揆殷勤之聖意，亦足悟海岱之所常在，知百川之所宜注矣。昔伊尹去夏而就殷，陳平違楚而歸漢，猶曜德於阿衡，著功於宰相。若足下能弼人之遺孤，定人之猶豫，去非常之偽號，事受命之大魏，客主兼不世之榮名，上下蒙不朽之常耀，功與事並，聲與勛著，考績效，足以超越伊、呂矣。既承詔（直），且服舊之情，情不能已。若不言足下之所能，陳足下之所見，則無以宣明詔命，弘光大之恩，敘宿昔夢想之思。若天啟眾心，子導蜀意，誠此意有攜手之期。若險路未夷，子謀不從，則懼聲問或否，復面何由！前後二書，言每及斯，希不切然有動於懷。足下周游江湖，以暨南海，歷觀夷俗，可謂遍矣；想子之心，結思華夏，可謂深矣。為身擇居，猶原中土；為主擇（居）安，豈可以不系意於京師，而持疑於荒裔乎？詳思愚言，速示還報也。」麋竺字子仲，東海朐人也。祖世貨殖，僮客萬人，貲產鉅億。《搜神記》曰：竺嘗從洛歸，未達家數十里，路傍見一婦人，從竺求寄載。行可數里，婦謝去，謂竺曰：「我天使也，當往燒東海麋竺家，感君見載，故以相語。」竺因私請之，婦曰：「不可得不燒。如此，君可馳去，我當緩行，日中火當發。」竺乃還家，遽出財物，日中而火大發。后徐州牧陶謙辟為別駕從事。謙卒，竺奉謙遺命，迎先主于小沛。建安元年，呂布乘先主之出拒袁術，襲下邳，虜先主妻子。先主轉軍廣陵海西，竺于是進妹于先主為夫人，奴客二千，金銀貨幣以助軍資，于時困匱，賴此複振。后曹公表竺領嬴郡太守，曹公集載公表曰：「泰山郡界廣遠，舊多輕悍，權時之宜，可分五縣為嬴郡，揀選清廉以為守將。偏將軍麋竺，素履忠貞，文武昭烈，請以竺領嬴郡太守，撫慰吏民。」竺弟芳為彭城相，皆去官，隨先主周旋。先主將適荊州，遣竺先與劉表相聞，以竺為左將軍從事中郎。益州既平，拜為安漢將軍，班在軍師將軍之右。竺雍容敦雅，而干翮非所長。是以待之以上賓之禮，未嘗有所統御。然賞賜優寵，無與為比。
