manualTranslations.zh: 馬忠字德信，巴西閬中人也。
manualTranslations.literal: Ma Zhong, courtesy name Dexin, was a man of Langzhong in Ba-Xi.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Ma Zhong, styled Dexin, came from Langzhong in Ba-Xi Commandery.

manualTranslations.zh: 少養外家，姓狐，名篤，後乃復姓，改名忠。
manualTranslations.literal: In youth he was raised by his maternal family, surnamed Hu and named Du; later he restored his surname and changed his name to Zhong.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Raised in his mother's Hu clan under the name Du, he later resumed the surname Ma and took the name Zhong.

manualTranslations.zh: 為郡吏，建安末舉孝廉，除漢昌長。
manualTranslations.literal: He was a commandery clerk; at the end of the Jian'an era he was recommended as filial and incorrupt and appointed chief of Hanchang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He served as a commandery clerk and, at the end of Jian'an, was recommended as filial and incorrupt and made chief of Hanchang.

manualTranslations.zh: 先主東征，敗績猇亭，巴西太守閻芝發諸縣兵五千人以補遣闕，遣忠送往。
manualTranslations.literal: When the First Sovereign campaigned east and was defeated at Xiaoting, Ba-Xi Administrator Yan Zhi mobilized five thousand troops from the various counties to fill shortages and losses and sent Zhong to deliver them.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After Liu Bei's defeat at Xiaoting, Ba-Xi administrator Yan Zhi raised five thousand county troops to fill the army's losses and sent Ma Zhong with them.

manualTranslations.zh: 先主已還永安，見忠與語，謂尚書令劉巴曰：「雖亡黃權，復得狐篤，此為世不乏賢也。」
manualTranslations.literal: The First Sovereign had already returned to Yong'an. Seeing Zhong and speaking with him, he said to Masters-of-Writing Director Liu Ba: "Though I have lost Huang Quan, I have again gained Hu Du—this shows the age is never short of worthy men."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Liu Bei had already returned to Yong'an. After meeting Ma Zhong he told Masters-of-Writing Director Liu Ba, "Though I lost Huang Quan, I have gained Hu Du—the world never lacks talent."

manualTranslations.zh: 建興元年223年，丞相亮開府，以忠為下督。
manualTranslations.literal: In the first year of Jianxing [223], Chancellor Liang opened his bureau and appointed Zhong lower supervisor.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Jianxing 1 Zhuge Liang opened his chancellor's bureau and named Ma Zhong lower supervisor.

manualTranslations.zh: 三年，亮入南，拜忠牂牁太守。
manualTranslations.literal: In the third year, when Liang entered the south, he appointed Zhong Administrator of Zangke.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Jianxing 3, when Zhuge Liang marched south, he made Ma Zhong administrator of Zangke.

manualTranslations.zh: 郡丞朱褒反。
manualTranslations.literal: Assistant Administrator Zhu Bao rebelled.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Assistant administrator Zhu Bao rebelled.

manualTranslations.zh: 叛亂之後，忠撫育卹理，甚有威惠。
manualTranslations.literal: After the rebellion, Zhong nurtured and comforted the people and governed them; he had great authority and grace.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After the rebellion Ma Zhong nursed the people back to order with both sternness and kindness.

manualTranslations.zh: 八年，召為丞相參軍，副長史蔣琬署留府事。
manualTranslations.literal: In the eighth year he was summoned as army adviser to the chancellor, assisting Chief Clerk Jiang Wan in administering rear headquarters affairs.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Jianxing 8 he was recalled as the chancellor's army adviser, assisting chief clerk Jiang Wan in running the rear headquarters.

manualTranslations.zh: 又領州治中從事。
manualTranslations.literal: He also concurrently served as director of the headquarters staff of the province.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He also served concurrently as director of the provincial headquarters staff.

manualTranslations.zh: 明年，亮出祁山，忠詣亮所，經營戌事。
manualTranslations.literal: The next year, when Liang marched out to Qishan, Zhong went to Liang's headquarters and managed garrison affairs.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The next year, when Zhuge Liang marched to Qishan, Ma Zhong joined his headquarters to manage garrison affairs.

manualTranslations.zh: 軍還，督將軍張嶷等討汶山郡叛羌。
manualTranslations.literal: When the army returned, he supervised Generals Zhang Ni and others in punishing the rebel Qiang of Wenshan Commandery.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After the campaign he directed Zhang Ni and others against rebel Qiang in Wenshan Commandery.

manualTranslations.zh: 十一年，南夷豪帥劉冑反，擾亂諸郡。
manualTranslations.literal: In the eleventh year the southern Yi chieftain Liu Zhou rebelled and disturbed the various commanderies.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Jianxing 11 the southern chieftain Liu Zhou rebelled and threw several commanderies into turmoil.

manualTranslations.zh: 徵庲降都督張冀還，以忠代冀。
manualTranslations.literal: Area Commander of Laixiang Zhang Ji was recalled and Zhong replaced Ji.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Laixiang area commander Zhang Ji was recalled and Ma Zhong replaced him.

manualTranslations.zh: 忠遂斬冑，平南土。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhong thereupon beheaded Zhou and pacified the southern lands.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Ma Zhong beheaded Liu Zhou and pacified the south.

manualTranslations.zh: 加忠監軍、奮威將軍，封博陽亭侯。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhong was additionally made army supervisor and General Who Displays Might, and enfeoffed as village marquis of Boyang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He was promoted to army supervisor and general who displays might and enfeoffed as village marquis of Boyang.

manualTranslations.zh: 初，建寧郡殺太守正昂，縛太守張裔於吳，故都督常駐平夷縣。
manualTranslations.literal: At first Jianning Commandery killed Administrator Zheng Ang and bound Administrator Zhang Yi in Wu; therefore area commanders had regularly been stationed at Pingyi County.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Earlier Jianning had killed Administrator Zheng Ang and sent Administrator Zhang Yi bound to Wu, so area commanders had long been stationed at Pingyi County.

manualTranslations.zh: 至忠，乃移治味縣，處民夷之間。
manualTranslations.literal: When Zhong took office, he moved the seat to Wei County, placing it among Han and tribal peoples.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Under Ma Zhong the seat moved to Wei County, among Han and tribal settlements.

manualTranslations.zh: 又越嶲郡亦久失土地，忠率將太守張嶷開复舊郡，由此就加安南將軍，進封彭鄉亭侯。
manualTranslations.literal: Moreover Yuexi Commandery had long lost territory; Zhong led Administrator Zhang Ni to reopen and recover the old commandery; thereby he was promoted to General Who Pacifies the South and advanced to village marquis of Pengxiang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He also led Zhang Ni to recover long-lost Yuexi territory and was promoted to general who pacifies the south and advanced to village marquis of Pengxiang.

manualTranslations.zh: 延熙五年還朝，因至漢中，見大司馬蔣琬，宣傳詔旨，加拜鎮南大將軍。
manualTranslations.literal: In the fifth year of Yanxi he returned to court, and on the way to Hanzhong he saw Grand Marshal Jiang Wan, proclaimed the imperial edict, and was additionally appointed Grand General Who Guards the South.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Yanxi 5 he returned to court, stopped at Hanzhong to see Grand Marshal Jiang Wan, delivered the imperial edict, and was promoted to grand general who guards the south.

manualTranslations.zh: 七年春，大將軍費韋北禦魏敵，留忠成都，平尚書事。
manualTranslations.literal: In the spring of the seventh year, Grand General Fei Yi marched north to resist Wei enemies and left Zhong at Chengdu to balance Masters-of-Writing affairs.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the spring of Yanxi 7 Grand General Fei Yi marched north against Wei and left Ma Zhong at Chengdu to balance masters-of-writing affairs.

manualTranslations.zh: 禕還，忠乃歸南。
manualTranslations.literal: When Yi returned, Zhong then returned south.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Fei Yi returned, Ma Zhong went back south.

manualTranslations.zh: 十二年卒，子脩嗣。
manualTranslations.literal: In the twelfth year he died; his son Xiu succeeded.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He died in Jianxing 12; his son Ma Xiu inherited the title.

manualTranslations.zh: 脩弟恢。
manualTranslations.literal: Xiu's younger brother was Hui.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Ma Xiu's younger brother was Hui.

manualTranslations.zh: 恢子義，晉建寧太守。
manualTranslations.literal: Hui's son Yi was Administrator of Jianning under Jin.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Hui's son Yi served Jin as administrator of Jianning.

manualTranslations.zh: 忠為人寬濟有度量，但恢啁大笑，忿怒不形於色。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhong as a man was generous and relieving, with breadth of measure; only when cheerful he laughed loudly, and anger did not show on his face.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Ma Zhong was generous and broad-minded, laughed loudly when pleased, and never let anger show.

manualTranslations.zh: 然處事能斷，威思並立，是以蠻夷畏而愛之。
manualTranslations.literal: Yet in handling affairs he could decide; authority and kindness stood together—therefore the tribes both feared and loved him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yet he decided firmly, pairing authority with kindness, so the tribes both feared and loved him.

manualTranslations.zh: 及卒，莫不自致喪庭，流涕盡哀，為之立廟祀，迄今猶在。
manualTranslations.literal: When he died, none failed to come in person to the mourning hall, weeping with full grief; they built temples to sacrifice to him, which remain to this day.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At his death tribesmen came in person to mourn, weeping fully, and built shrines to him that still stand.

manualTranslations.zh: 張表，時名士，清望逾忠。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhang Biao was a famed gentleman of the time; his pure reputation surpassed Zhong's.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhang Biao was a celebrated gentleman whose repute outshone Ma Zhong's.

manualTranslations.zh: 閻宇宿有功幹，於事精勤。
manualTranslations.literal: Yan Yu for long had merit and capability and was meticulous and diligent in affairs.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yan Yu had long shown ability and handled affairs with care.

manualTranslations.zh: 繼踵在忠後，其威風稱績，皆不及忠。
manualTranslations.literal: Those who followed in Zhong's footsteps—their authority, reputation, and achievements all did not reach Zhong's.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Successors who followed Ma Zhong never matched his authority or record.

manualTranslations.zh: 《益部耆舊傳》曰：張表，肅子也。
manualTranslations.literal: The Traditions of Former Worthies of Yibu states: Zhang Biao was the son of Su.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Yibu tradition says Zhang Biao was Su's son.

manualTranslations.zh: 《華陽國志》云：表，張松子，未詳。
manualTranslations.literal: The Huayang guo zhi says: Biao was Zhang Songzi—uncertain.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Huayang guo zhi calls him Zhang Songzi, which is uncertain.

manualTranslations.zh: 閻宇字文平，南郡人也。
manualTranslations.literal: Yan Yu, courtesy name Wenping, was a man of Nan Commandery.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yan Yu, styled Wenping, came from Nan Commandery.

sourceRange.text: 先主薨於永安。先是，吳王孫權請和，先主累遣宋瑋、費禕等與相報答。丞相諸葛亮深慮權聞先主殂隕，恐有異計，未知所如。芝見亮曰：「今主上幼弱，初在位，宜遣大使重申吳好。」亮答之曰：「吾思之久矣，未得其人耳，今日始得之。」芝問其人為誰？亮曰：「即使君也。」乃遣芝脩好於權。權果狐疑，不時見芝，芝乃自表請見權曰：「臣今來亦欲為吳，非但為蜀也。」權乃見之，語芝曰：「孤誠原與蜀和親，然恐蜀主幼弱，國小勢偪，為魏所乘，不自保全，以此猶豫耳。」芝對曰：「吳、蜀二國四州之地，大王命世之英，諸葛亮亦一時之傑也。蜀有重險之固，吳有三江之阻，合此二長，共為脣齒，進可並兼天下，退可鼎足而立，此理之自然也。大王今若委質於魏，魏必上望大王之入朝，下求太子之內侍，若不從命，則奉辭伐叛，蜀必順流見可而進，如此，江南之地非複大王之有也。」權默然良久曰：「君言是也。」遂自絕魏，與蜀連和，遣張溫報聘於蜀。蜀復令芝重往，權謂芝曰：「若天下太平，二主分治，不亦樂乎！」芝對曰：「夫天無二日，土無二王，如並魏之後，大王未深識天命者也，君各茂其德，臣各盡其忠，將提枹鼓，則戰爭方始耳。」權大笑曰：「君之誠款，乃當爾邪！」權與亮書曰：「丁厷掞張，掞音夷念反，或作艷。臣松之案《漢書禮樂志》曰「長離前掞光耀明」。左思《蜀都賦》「摛藻掞天庭」。孫權蓋謂丁厷之言多浮艷也。陰化不盡；和合二國，唯有鄧芝。」及亮北住漢中，以芝為中監軍、揚武將軍。亮卒，遷前軍師前將軍，領袞州刺史，封陽武亭侯，頃之為督江州。權數與芝相聞，饋遺優渥。

manualTranslations.zh: 丞相諸葛亮深慮權聞先主殂隕，恐有異計，未知所如。
manualTranslations.literal: Chancellor Zhuge Liang deeply feared that when Quan heard the First Sovereign had passed away he might form a different plan, and did not know what to do.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Chancellor Zhuge Liang deeply feared that Sun Quan, hearing of the First Sovereign’s death, might change course, and he did not know what to do.

manualTranslations.zh: 芝見亮曰：「今主上幼弱，初在位，宜遣大使重申吳好。」
manualTranslations.literal: Zhi saw Liang and said, "Now the sovereign is young and weak, having just taken the throne; it is fitting to send a great envoy to reaffirm friendship with Wu."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Deng Zhi saw Liang and said, "The throne is young and newly filled; we should send a senior envoy to renew our bond with Wu."

manualTranslations.zh: 亮答之曰：「吾思之久矣，未得其人耳，今日始得之。」
manualTranslations.literal: Liang answered him, saying, "I have thought on this long, but had not found the man; today I have found him."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Liang answered: "I have sought the right man a long while; today I have found him."

manualTranslations.zh: 芝問其人為誰？
manualTranslations.literal: Zhi asked who the man was.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Deng Zhi asked who he was.

manualTranslations.zh: 亮曰：「即使君也。」
manualTranslations.literal: Liang said, "It is you, sir."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Liang said, "You, sir."

manualTranslations.zh: 乃遣芝脩好於權。
manualTranslations.literal: He then sent Zhi to renew friendship with Quan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He then sent Deng Zhi to treat with Sun Quan.

manualTranslations.zh: 權果狐疑，不時見芝，芝乃自表請見權曰：「臣今來亦欲為吳，非但為蜀也。」
manualTranslations.literal: Quan indeed was hesitant and did not receive Zhi promptly; Zhi thereupon submitted a memorial requesting audience and said to Quan, "Your servant has come now also wishing to act for Wu, not only for Shu."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sun Quan hesitated and delayed the audience; Deng Zhi petitioned to be received and said, "I come now to serve Wu’s interest as much as Shu’s."

manualTranslations.zh: 權乃見之，語芝曰：「孤誠原與蜀和親，然恐蜀主幼弱，國小勢偪，為魏所乘，不自保全，以此猶豫耳。」
manualTranslations.literal: Quan then received him and said to Zhi, "I truly wish kinship with Shu, yet I fear the Shu sovereign is young and weak, the state small and pressed by circumstance, and will be ridden by Wei and unable to preserve itself—therefore I hesitate."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sun Quan received him and said, "I truly wish kinship with Shu, yet I fear your young ruler, your small state pressed by power, will be overrun by Wei and cannot stand alone—that is why I hesitate."

manualTranslations.zh: 芝對曰：「吳、蜀二國四州之地，大王命世之英，諸葛亮亦一時之傑也。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhi replied, saying, "Wu and Shu are two states spanning four provinces; Great King is a hero of the age, and Zhuge Liang is also an outstanding man of the time.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Deng Zhi answered: "Wu and Shu hold four provinces between them; Your Majesty is a hero of the age, and Zhuge Liang is a genius of his time.

manualTranslations.zh: 蜀有重險之固，吳有三江之阻，合此二長，共為脣齒，進可並兼天下，退可鼎足而立，此理之自然也。
manualTranslations.literal: Shu has the security of layered peril, Wu has the barrier of the three rivers; join these two strengths and become lip and teeth together—advancing, you can unite and take all under Heaven; retreating, you can stand as a tripod of three legs. This is the natural reason of things.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Shu has its mountain fastnesses; Wu its three rivers. Join those strengths and you are lip to teeth: advance and you may unite the realm; retreat and you still stand as one leg of a tripod. That is nature’s logic.

manualTranslations.zh: 大王今若委質於魏，魏必上望大王之入朝，下求太子之內侍，若不從命，則奉辭伐叛，蜀必順流見可而進，如此，江南之地非複大王之有也。」
manualTranslations.literal: If Great King now submits quality to Wei, Wei will above expect Great King to enter court and below demand the heir as inner attendant; if you do not follow the command, they will offer words to attack rebellion, and Shu also will go with the current and advance when it sees opportunity—thus the lands south of the river will no longer belong to Great King."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If you now submit to Wei, they will demand your court attendance and your heir as hostage; refuse, and they march south under a punitive banner while Shu follows the river wherever chance opens. Then the lands south of the Yangzi will no longer be yours."

manualTranslations.zh: 權默然良久曰：「君言是也。」
manualTranslations.literal: Quan was silent a long while and said, "Your words are right."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sun Quan was silent a long while, then said, "You are right."

manualTranslations.zh: 遂自絕魏，與蜀連和，遣張溫報聘於蜀。
manualTranslations.literal: He then broke with Wei on his own, allied with Shu, and sent Zhang Wen on a return mission of courtesy to Shu.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He broke with Wei and allied with Shu, and sent Zhang Wen as envoy to Shu.

manualTranslations.zh: 蜀復令芝重往，權謂芝曰：「若天下太平，二主分治，不亦樂乎！」
manualTranslations.literal: Shu again had Zhi go once more; Quan said to Zhi, "If all under Heaven were at peace and the two rulers divided governance, would that not also be joy!"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Shu sent Deng Zhi again. Sun Quan said to him, "If the realm were at peace and our two thrones shared rule, would that not be pleasant!"

manualTranslations.zh: 芝對曰：「夫天無二日，土無二王，如並魏之後，大王未深識天命者也，君各茂其德，臣各盡其忠，將提枹鼓，則戰爭方始耳。」
manualTranslations.literal: Zhi replied, saying, "Heaven has no two suns; earth has no two kings. After uniting with Wei, if Great King has not deeply recognized Heaven’s Mandate, and each ruler cultivates his virtue while each minister exhausts his loyalty, and they raise drum and mallet—then war has only just begun."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Deng Zhi answered: "Heaven admits but one sun; earth but one king. Once Wei is gone, if you have not read Heaven’s Mandate aright, and each throne and each minister plays his part to the full, then the drums of war will sound and the fighting begin anew."

manualTranslations.zh: 權大笑曰：「君之誠款，乃當爾邪！」
manualTranslations.literal: Quan laughed greatly and said, "Your honest sincerity is truly thus!"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sun Quan laughed aloud: "Your candor is exactly what I hoped for!"

manualTranslations.zh: 權與亮書曰：「丁厷掞張，掞音夷念反，或作艷。
manualTranslations.literal: Quan wrote to Liang, saying, "Ding Gong’s words are florid and spread wide; shan is fanqie yi plus nian, or written as yan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sun Quan wrote Liang: "Ding Gong’s words are florid and spread wide; shan is fanqie yi plus nian, or written yan.

manualTranslations.zh: 臣松之案《漢書禮樂志》曰「長離前掞光耀明」。
manualTranslations.literal: Your servant Songzhi examines the Han shu "Treatise on Rites and Music," which states, "Changli in front spreads radiance and brightness."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi notes the Han shu "Treatise on Rites and Music," which says, "Changli in front spreads radiance and brightness."

manualTranslations.zh: 左思《蜀都賦》「摛藻掞天庭」。
manualTranslations.literal: Zuo Si’s "Rhapsody on the Shu Capital" has, "Wielding ornament, he spreads it through the court of Heaven."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zuo Si’s "Rhapsody on the Shu Capital" has, "Wielding ornament, he spreads it through the court of Heaven."

manualTranslations.zh: 孫權蓋謂丁厷之言多浮艷也。
manualTranslations.literal: Sun Quan probably meant that Ding Gong’s words were mostly floating and florid.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sun Quan probably meant that Ding Gong’s words were mostly florid and showy.

manualTranslations.zh: 陰化不盡；
manualTranslations.literal: Yin Hua did not exhaust his task;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yin Hua did not finish the task;

manualTranslations.zh: 和合二國，唯有鄧芝。」
manualTranslations.literal: to unite the two states there was only Deng Zhi."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: only Deng Zhi could unite the two states."

manualTranslations.zh: 及亮北住漢中，以芝為中監軍、揚武將軍。
manualTranslations.literal: When Liang camped north at Hanzhong, he made Zhi Central Army Supervisor and General Who Displays Might.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Liang took up his northern post at Hanzhong, he made Deng Zhi central army supervisor and general who displays might.

manualTranslations.zh: 亮卒，遷前軍師前將軍，領袞州刺史，封陽武亭侯，頃之為督江州。
manualTranslations.literal: When Liang died, Zhi was moved up to Former Army Adviser and Former General, concurrently Inspector of Yan Province, enfeoffed as Marquis of Yangwu village, and soon afterward was made supervisor of Jiangzhou.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After Liang died Deng Zhi became former army adviser and former general, inspector of Yan Province, marquis of Yangwu village, and soon supervisor of Jiangzhou.

manualTranslations.zh: 權數與芝相聞，饋遺優渥。
manualTranslations.literal: Quan repeatedly exchanged messages with Zhi and sent gifts that were generous and lavish.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sun Quan exchanged messages with Deng Zhi often and sent lavish gifts.

sourceRange.text: 建興九年231年，為庲降都督、綏南中郎將。

sourceRange.text: 延熙十年，為屯騎校尉。時車騎將軍鄧芝自江州還，來朝，謂預曰：「禮，六十不服戎，而卿甫受兵，何也？」預答曰：「卿七十不還兵，我六十何為不受邪？」臣松之以為芝以年啁預，是不自顧。然預之此答，觸人所忌。載之記牒，近為煩文。芝性驕傲，自大將軍費禕等皆避下之，而預獨不為屈。預復東聘吳，孫權捉預手，涕泣而別曰：「君每銜命結二國之好。今君年長，孤亦衰老，恐不復相見！」遺預大珠一斛，吳歷曰：預臨別，謂孫權曰：「蜀土僻小，雖云鄰國，東西相賴，吳不可無蜀，蜀不可無吳，君臣憑恃，唯陛下重垂神慮。」又自說「年老多病，恐不復得奉聖顏」。孫盛曰：夫帝王之保，唯道與義，道義既建，雖小可大，殷、周是也。苟任詐力，雖強必敗，秦、項是也。況乎居偏鄙之城，恃山水之固，而欲連橫萬里，永相資賴哉？昔九國建合從之計，而秦人卒並六合；囂、述營輔車之謀，而光武終兼隴、蜀。夫以九國之強，隴、漢之大，莫能相救，坐觀屠覆。何者？道德之基不固，而強弱之心難一故也。而云「吳不可無蜀，蜀不可無吳」，豈不諂哉！乃還。遷後將軍，督永安，就拜征西大將軍，賜爵關內侯。景耀元年，以疾徵還成都。後為鎮軍大將軍，領兗州刺史。時都護諸葛瞻初統朝事，廖化過預，欲與預共詣瞻許。預曰：「吾等年逾七十，所竊已過，但少一死耳，何求於年少輩而屑屑造門邪？」遂不往。廖化字元儉，本名淳，襄陽人也。為前將軍關羽主簿，羽敗，屬吳。思歸先主，乃詐死，時人謂為信然，因攜持老母晝夜西行。會先主東征，遇於秭歸。先主大悅，以化為宜都太守。先主薨，為丞相參軍，後為督廣武，稍遷至右車騎將軍，假節，領并州刺史，封中鄉侯，以果烈稱。官位與張翼齊，而在宗預之右。《漢晉春秋》曰：景耀五年，姜維率眾出狄道，廖化曰：「‘兵不戢，必自焚’，伯約之謂也。智不出敵，而力少於寇，用之無厭，何以能立？詩云‘不自我先，不自我後’，今日之事也。

manualTranslations.zh: 延熙十年，為屯騎校尉。
manualTranslations.literal: In the tenth year of Yanxi he became Commandant of Escort Cavalry.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Yanxi 10 he became commandant of escort cavalry.

manualTranslations.zh: 時車騎將軍鄧芝自江州還，來朝，謂預曰：「禮，六十不服戎，而卿甫受兵，何也？」
manualTranslations.literal: At the time General of Chariots and Cavalry Deng Zhi returned from Jiangzhou and came to court; he said to Yu, "By ritual, at sixty one does not bear arms—yet you have just received command of troops. Why?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When General of Chariots and Cavalry Deng Zhi returned from Jiangzhou and came to court, he said to Zong Yu, "By ritual, at sixty one does not bear arms—yet you have just taken command. Why?"

manualTranslations.zh: 預答曰：「卿七十不還兵，我六十何為不受邪？」
manualTranslations.literal: Yu replied, saying, "You at seventy have not returned your troops—why should I at sixty not receive them?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zong Yu answered, "You at seventy have not returned your troops—why should I at sixty not accept them?"

manualTranslations.zh: 臣松之以為芝以年啁預，是不自顧。
manualTranslations.literal: Your servant Songzhi considers that Zhi used age to mock Yu and did not look to himself.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi considers that Deng Zhi mocked Zong Yu by age and did not look to himself.

manualTranslations.zh: 然預之此答，觸人所忌。
manualTranslations.literal: Yet Yu’s reply here touched what people resent.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yet Zong Yu’s reply touched what people resent.

manualTranslations.zh: 載之記牒，近為煩文。
manualTranslations.literal: Recording it in the annals comes close to superfluous writing.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Recording it in the annals comes close to superfluous writing.

manualTranslations.zh: 芝性驕傲，自大將軍費禕等皆避下之，而預獨不為屈。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhi by nature was proud and arrogant; from Grand General Fei Yi downward all yielded before him, yet Yu alone would not bow.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Deng Zhi was proud by nature; from Grand General Fei Yi downward all yielded before him, yet Zong Yu alone would not bow.

manualTranslations.zh: 預復東聘吳，孫權捉預手，涕泣而別曰：「君每銜命結二國之好。
manualTranslations.literal: Yu again went east on a mission of courtesy to Wu; Sun Quan took Yu’s hand, wept as they parted, and said, "You, sir, have repeatedly borne orders to bind the friendship of the two states.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zong Yu went east again on a mission to Wu; Sun Quan took his hand, wept as they parted, and said, "You have repeatedly borne orders to bind our two states in friendship.

manualTranslations.zh: 今君年長，孤亦衰老，恐不復相見！」
manualTranslations.literal: Now you, sir, are advanced in years, and I too am aging—I fear we shall not meet again!"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Now you are advanced in years, and I too am aging—I fear we shall not meet again!"

manualTranslations.zh: 遺預大珠一斛，吳歷曰：預臨別，謂孫權曰：「蜀土僻小，雖云鄰國，東西相賴，吳不可無蜀，蜀不可無吳，君臣憑恃，唯陛下重垂神慮。」
manualTranslations.literal: He bestowed on Yu a hu of great pearls. Wu Li states: As Yu was about to part, he said to Sun Quan, "Shu’s land is remote and small; though called a neighboring state, east and west rely on each other—Wu cannot be without Shu, Shu cannot be without Wu; ruler and ministers depend on one another; may Your Majesty deeply bestow your divine consideration."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He gave Zong Yu a hu of great pearls. Wu Li states that on parting Zong Yu told Sun Quan, "Shu is remote and small; though we are neighbors, east and west rely on each other—Wu cannot be without Shu, Shu cannot be without Wu. Ruler and ministers depend on one another; may Your Majesty weigh this carefully."

manualTranslations.zh: 又自說「年老多病，恐不復得奉聖顏」。
manualTranslations.literal: He also said of himself, "I am old and often ill, and fear I shall not again behold the sacred countenance."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He also said he was old and often ill and feared he would not again behold the sacred countenance.

manualTranslations.zh: 孫盛曰：夫帝王之保，唯道與義，道義既建，雖小可大，殷、周是也。
manualTranslations.literal: Sun Sheng says: The preservation of emperors and kings rests only on the Way and righteousness; once the Way and righteousness are established, though small one may become great—Yin and Zhou were thus.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sun Sheng says: emperors and kings endure only through the Way and righteousness; once those are established, the small may become great, as with Yin and Zhou.

manualTranslations.zh: 苟任詐力，雖強必敗，秦、項是也。
manualTranslations.literal: If one relies on deceit and force, though strong one must fail—Qin and Xiang Yu were thus.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If one relies on deceit and force, though strong one must fail, as with Qin and Xiang Yu.

manualTranslations.zh: 況乎居偏鄙之城，恃山水之固，而欲連橫萬里，永相資賴哉？
manualTranslations.literal: How much more when dwelling in remote and humble cities, relying on the security of mountains and rivers, yet wishing to join in alliance across ten thousand li and rely on each other forever!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: How much less when dwelling in remote cities, relying on mountains and rivers, yet wishing to ally across ten thousand li and rely on each other forever!

manualTranslations.zh: 昔九國建合從之計，而秦人卒並六合；
manualTranslations.literal: Formerly the nine states formed the plan of the Vertical Alliance, yet the men of Qin in the end united the six directions;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Formerly the nine states formed the Vertical Alliance, yet Qin in the end united the six directions;

manualTranslations.zh: 囂、述營輔車之謀，而光武終兼隴、蜀。
manualTranslations.literal: Xiao and Shu plotted the chariot-and-outrigger alliance, yet Guangwu in the end combined Long and Shu.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Xiao and Shu plotted mutual support, yet Guangwu in the end combined Long and Shu.

manualTranslations.zh: 夫以九國之強，隴、漢之大，莫能相救，坐觀屠覆。
manualTranslations.literal: With the strength of nine states and the vastness of Long and Han, none could rescue one another and sat watching slaughter and ruin.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: With the strength of nine states and the vastness of Long and Han, none could rescue one another and sat watching slaughter and ruin.

manualTranslations.zh: 何者？
manualTranslations.literal: Why?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Why?

manualTranslations.zh: 道德之基不固，而強弱之心難一故也。
manualTranslations.literal: Because the foundation of virtue and the Way was not firm, and hearts of strong and weak were hard to unify.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Because the foundation of virtue and the Way was not firm, and hearts of strong and weak were hard to unify.

manualTranslations.zh: 而云「吳不可無蜀，蜀不可無吳」，豈不諂哉！
manualTranslations.literal: Yet to say "Wu cannot be without Shu, Shu cannot be without Wu"—is this not flattery!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yet to say "Wu cannot be without Shu, Shu cannot be without Wu"—is this not flattery!

manualTranslations.zh: 乃還。
manualTranslations.literal: He then returned.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He then returned.

manualTranslations.zh: 遷後將軍，督永安，就拜征西大將軍，賜爵關內侯。
manualTranslations.literal: He was moved up to General of the Rear, supervised Yong’an, and on the spot was appointed Grand General Who Conquers the West and granted the rank of secondary marquis within the passes.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He was promoted to general of the rear, supervised Yong’an, and was appointed grand general who conquers the west with the rank of secondary marquis within the passes.

manualTranslations.zh: 景耀元年，以疾徵還成都。
manualTranslations.literal: In the first year of Jingyao he was summoned back to Chengdu on account of illness.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Jingyao 1 he was recalled to Chengdu on account of illness.

manualTranslations.zh: 後為鎮軍大將軍，領兗州刺史。
manualTranslations.literal: Later he became Grand General Who Stabilizes the Army and concurrently held the post of Inspector of Yan Province.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Later he became grand general who stabilizes the army and inspector of Yan Province.

manualTranslations.zh: 時都護諸葛瞻初統朝事，廖化過預，欲與預共詣瞻許。
manualTranslations.literal: At the time Protector-General Zhuge Zhan had just taken charge of court affairs; Liao Hua passed by Yu and wished to go with Yu together to visit Zhan’s residence.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Protector-General Zhuge Zhan had just taken charge of court affairs, Liao Hua visited Zong Yu and wished to go with him to call on Zhan.

manualTranslations.zh: 預曰：「吾等年逾七十，所竊已過，但少一死耳，何求於年少輩而屑屑造門邪？」
manualTranslations.literal: Yu said, "We are past seventy; what we have stolen is already more than enough—we lack only death. Why seek anything from younger men and fuss about calling at doors?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zong Yu said, "We are past seventy; what we have taken is already more than enough—we lack only death. Why fuss about calling on younger men?"

manualTranslations.zh: 遂不往。
manualTranslations.literal: He thereupon did not go.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He did not go.

manualTranslations.zh: 廖化字元儉，本名淳，襄陽人也。
manualTranslations.literal: Liao Hua, courtesy name Yuanjian, original name Chun, was a man of Xiangyang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Liao Hua, styled Yuanjian, originally named Chun, came from Xiangyang.

manualTranslations.zh: 為前將軍關羽主簿，羽敗，屬吳。
manualTranslations.literal: He was chief clerk to Former General Guan Yu; when Yu was defeated he came under Wu.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He was chief clerk to Former General Guan Yu; when Yu was defeated he came under Wu.

manualTranslations.zh: 思歸先主，乃詐死，時人謂為信然，因攜持老母晝夜西行。
manualTranslations.literal: Wishing to return to the First Sovereign, he feigned death; people of the time took it as true, and he therefore carried his old mother and traveled west day and night.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wishing to return to the First Sovereign, he feigned death; people believed it, and he carried his old mother west day and night.

manualTranslations.zh: 會先主東征，遇於秭歸。
manualTranslations.literal: He happened to meet the First Sovereign on the eastern campaign at Zigui.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He met the First Sovereign on the eastern campaign at Zigui.

manualTranslations.zh: 先主大悅，以化為宜都太守。
manualTranslations.literal: The First Sovereign was greatly pleased and made Hua Administrator of Yidu.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The First Sovereign was greatly pleased and made Liao Hua Administrator of Yidu.

manualTranslations.zh: 先主薨，為丞相參軍，後為督廣武，稍遷至右車騎將軍，假節，領并州刺史，封中鄉侯，以果烈稱。
manualTranslations.literal: When the First Sovereign died, he became army adviser to the chancellor, later supervised Guangwu, was gradually moved up to General of Chariots and Cavalry of the Right, granted the staff of authority, concurrently held the post of Inspector of Bing Province, enfeoffed as Marquis of Zhong village, and was famed for decisiveness and fierceness.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After the First Sovereign died he became the chancellor’s army adviser, later supervised Guangwu, rose to general of chariots and cavalry of the right with the credential staff, inspector of Bing Province, and marquis of Zhong village, famed for decisiveness and fierceness.

manualTranslations.zh: 官位與張翼齊，而在宗預之右。
manualTranslations.literal: His offices were equal to Zhang Yi’s, yet he ranked above Zong Yu.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His rank equaled Zhang Yi’s, yet he stood above Zong Yu.

manualTranslations.zh: 《漢晉春秋》曰：景耀五年，姜維率眾出狄道，廖化曰：「'兵不戢，必自焚'，伯約之謂也。
manualTranslations.literal: The Han Jin Chunqiu states: In the fifth year of Jingyao Jiang Wei led the host out toward Didao; Liao Hua said, "'If troops are not kept in check, they will burn themselves'—this is what Boyue means.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Han Jin Chunqiu states: In Jingyao 5 Jiang Wei led troops toward Didao; Liao Hua said, "'If troops are not kept in check, they will burn themselves'—that is Boyue’s point.

manualTranslations.zh: 智不出敵，而力少於寇，用之無厭，何以能立？
manualTranslations.literal: Wisdom does not surpass the enemy, yet strength is less than the foe; using them without satiety—how can one stand?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His wisdom does not surpass the enemy, yet his strength is less than the foe; using them without satiety—how can he stand?

manualTranslations.zh: 詩云'不自我先，不自我後'，今日之事也。」
manualTranslations.literal: The Odes say, "Neither before me nor after me"—today’s affair is thus."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Odes say, "Neither before me nor after me"—today’s affair is thus."

sourceRange.text: 伷字子緒，亦閬中人。先主定益州後，為功曹書佐。建興元年223年，為廣漢太守。丞相亮北駐漢中，闢為掾。並進文武之士，亮稱曰：「忠益者莫大於進人，進人者各務其所尚；今姚掾並存剛柔，以廣文武之用，可謂博雅矣，原諸掾各希此事，以屬其望。」遷為參軍。亮卒，稍遷為尚書僕射。時人服其真誠篤粹。延熙五年卒，在作讚之後。

manualTranslations.literal: Zhou, courtesy name Zixu, was also a man of Langzhong.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yao Zhou, styled Zixu, also came from Langzhong.

manualTranslations.zh: 先主定益州後，為功曹書佐。
manualTranslations.literal: After the First Sovereign settled Yizhou, he served as clerical aide in the merit office.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After the First Sovereign took Yizhou, he served as a merit-office clerical aide.

manualTranslations.zh: 建興元年，為廣漢太守。
manualTranslations.literal: In the first year of Jianxing he became Administrator of Guanghan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Jianxing 1 he was made Administrator of Guanghan.

manualTranslations.zh: 丞相亮北駐漢中，闢為掾。
manualTranslations.literal: When Chancellor Liang camped north at Hanzhong, he recruited him as a clerk.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Chancellor Liang took up his northern post at Hanzhong, he recruited Yao Zhou as a clerk.

manualTranslations.zh: 並進文武之士，亮稱曰：「忠益者莫大於進人，進人者各務其所尚；
manualTranslations.literal: Together he recommended men of civil and military talent, and Liang praised him, saying, "Nothing benefits loyalty more than recommending men; those who recommend men each pursue what they esteem;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He also recommended both civil and military men, and Liang praised him: "Nothing serves loyalty better than recommending talent, and each recommender pursues what he most values;

manualTranslations.zh: 今姚掾並存剛柔，以廣文武之用，可謂博雅矣，原諸掾各希此事，以屬其望。
manualTranslations.literal: Now Clerk Yao preserves both firmness and flexibility to broaden use of civil and military men—this may be called broadly learned; I wish all clerks would each aspire to this matter to fulfill their hopes.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Clerk Yao now keeps both firm and flexible men in view and broadens the use of civil and military talent. That may truly be called breadth of learning. I hope every clerk will aspire to the same and live up to what is expected of him.

manualTranslations.zh: 遷為參軍。
manualTranslations.literal: He was moved up to Army Advisor.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He was promoted to army adviser.

manualTranslations.zh: 亮卒，稍遷為尚書僕射。
manualTranslations.literal: When Liang died, he was gradually moved up to Vice Director of the Secretariat.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After Liang died he rose to vice director of the secretariat.

manualTranslations.zh: 時人服其真誠篤粹。
manualTranslations.literal: People of the time admired his sincerity and pure integrity.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Contemporaries respected his sincerity and unmixed integrity.

manualTranslations.zh: 延熙五年卒，在作讚之後。
manualTranslations.literal: In the fifth year of Yanxi he died, after the encomium was composed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He died in Yanxi 5, after the encomium had been written.

sourceRange.text: 永南名邵，廣漢郪人也。先主定蜀後，為州書佐部從事。建興元年223年，丞相亮闢為西曹掾。亮南征，留邵為治中從事，是歲卒。《華陽國志》曰：邵兄邈，字漢南，劉璋時為牛鞞長。先主領牧，為從事，正旦命行酒，得進見，讓先主曰：「振威以將軍宗室肺腑，委以討賊，元功未效，先寇而滅；邈以將軍之取鄙州，甚為不宜也。」先主曰：「知其不宜，何以不助之？」邈曰：「匪不敢也，力不足耳。」有司將殺之，諸葛亮為請，得免。久之，為犍為太守、丞相參軍、安漢將軍。建興六年228年，亮西征。馬謖在前敗績，亮將殺之，邈諫以「秦赦孟明，用伯西戎，楚誅子玉，二世不競」，失亮意，還蜀。十二年，亮卒，後主素服發哀三日，邈上疏曰：「呂祿、霍禹未必懷反叛之心，孝宣不好為殺臣之君，直以臣懼其偪，主畏其威，故姦萌生。亮身杖強兵，狼顧虎視，五大不在邊，臣常危之。今亮殞沒，蓋宗族得全，西戎靜息，大小為慶。」後主怒，下獄誅之。

context.beforeSource: 子祐，有父風，官至尚書右選郎。
context.afterSource: 盛衡名勳，承伯名齊，皆巴西閬中人也。

manualTranslations.zh: 永南名邵，廣漢郪人也。
manualTranslations.literal: Yongnan’s given name was Shao; he was a man of Qi in Guanghan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Li Shao, styled Yongnan, came from Qi in Guanghan.

manualTranslations.zh: 先主定蜀後，為州書佐部從事。
manualTranslations.literal: After the First Sovereign settled Shu, he was a provincial clerical aide and department attendant.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After the First Sovereign took Shu he served as provincial clerical aide and department attendant.

manualTranslations.zh: 建興元年，丞相亮闢為西曹掾。
manualTranslations.literal: In the first year of Jianxing Chancellor Liang recruited him as clerk of the western bureau.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Jianxing 1 Chancellor Liang recruited him as a western-bureau clerk.

manualTranslations.zh: 亮南征，留邵為治中從事，是歲卒。
manualTranslations.literal: When Liang campaigned south, he left Li Shao as managing attendant; that year Li Shao died.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On the southern campaign Liang left Li Shao as managing attendant; Li Shao died that year.

manualTranslations.zh: 〈《華陽國志》曰：邵兄邈，字漢南，劉璋時為牛鞞長。
manualTranslations.literal: 〈The Huayang Guozhi states: Li Shao’s elder brother Miao, courtesy name Hannan, in Liu Zhang’s time was chief of Niubi.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: 〈The Huayang Guozhi states that Li Shao’s elder brother Li Miao, styled Hannan, was chief of Niubi under Liu Zhang.

manualTranslations.zh: 先主領牧，為從事，正旦命行酒，得進見，讓先主曰：「振威以將軍宗室肺腑，委以討賊，元功未效，先寇而滅；
manualTranslations.literal: When the First Sovereign held the shepherdcy, Miao was an attendant; on New Year’s Day he was ordered to pass wine, gained audience, and reproached the First Sovereign, saying, "Zhenwei, as a general of the imperial clan and close as heart and lungs, was entrusted to strike the bandits; the great achievement had not yet succeeded when the enemy came first and he was destroyed;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When the First Sovereign held the shepherd’s staff, Li Miao served as an attendant. On New Year’s Day he was told to pass wine, gained audience, and reproached the First Sovereign: "Zhenwei, a kinsman of the imperial house entrusted to strike the rebels, had not yet won the great victory when the enemy came first and destroyed him;

manualTranslations.zh: 邈以將軍之取鄙州，甚為不宜也。」
manualTranslations.literal: Miao considered the general’s taking this humble province very improper."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Li Miao held that your taking this province was very improper."

manualTranslations.zh: 先主曰：「知其不宜，何以不助之？」
manualTranslations.literal: The First Sovereign said, "Knowing it was improper, why did you not assist him?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The First Sovereign said, "If you knew it was improper, why did you not help him?"

manualTranslations.zh: 邈曰：「匪不敢也，力不足耳。」
manualTranslations.literal: Miao said, "It was not that I did not dare; my strength was insufficient."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Li Miao said, "Not that I did not dare—I lacked the strength."

manualTranslations.zh: 有司將殺之，諸葛亮為請，得免。
manualTranslations.literal: The officials were about to execute him; Zhuge Liang pleaded for him, and he was spared.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The officials were about to execute him; Zhuge Liang interceded and he was spared.

manualTranslations.zh: 久之，為犍為太守、丞相參軍、安漢將軍。
manualTranslations.literal: After a long while he became Administrator of Qianwei, army adviser to the chancellor, and General Who Pacifies Han.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In time he became Administrator of Qianwei, the chancellor’s army adviser, and general who pacifies Han.

manualTranslations.zh: 建興六年，亮西征。
manualTranslations.literal: In the sixth year of Jianxing Liang campaigned west.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Jianxing 6 Liang marched west.

manualTranslations.zh: 馬謖在前敗績，亮將殺之，邈諫以「秦赦孟明，用伯西戎，楚誅子玉，二世不競」，失亮意，還蜀。
manualTranslations.literal: Ma Su suffered defeat in the van; Liang was about to execute him, and Miao remonstrated with the examples "Qin pardoned Meng Ming and used him to dominate the Western Rong; Chu executed Ziyu and did not compete for two generations," lost Liang’s favor, and returned to Shu.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Ma Su was routed in the van; Liang meant to execute him, and Li Miao cited the precedents "Qin pardoned Meng Ming and used him against the Western Rong; Chu executed Ziyu and lost two generations of competition," lost Liang’s favor, and returned to Shu.

manualTranslations.zh: 十二年，亮卒，後主素服發哀三日，邈上疏曰：「呂祿、霍禹未必懷反叛之心，孝宣不好為殺臣之君，直以臣懼其偪，主畏其威，故姦萌生。
manualTranslations.literal: In the twelfth year Liang died; the Later Lord wore plain robes and proclaimed mourning for three days. Miao submitted a memorial saying, "Lü Lu and Huo Yu did not necessarily harbor rebellious intent; Emperor Xiao of Han did not wish to be a ruler who killed his ministers—it was simply that ministers feared their pressure and the sovereign feared their power, and so treachery arose.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year Liang died; the Later Lord wore mourning for three days. Li Miao memorialized: "Lü Lu and Huo Yu did not necessarily mean rebellion; Emperor Xuan of Han did not wish to be a ruler who killed ministers—it was only that ministers feared their pressure and the sovereign feared their power, and treachery arose.

manualTranslations.zh: 亮身杖強兵，狼顧虎視，五大不在邊，臣常危之。
manualTranslations.literal: Liang himself wielded strong troops, looked back like a wolf and glared like a tiger; the Five Great were not at the frontier, and your servant often feared this.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Liang himself wielded strong armies, looked back like a wolf and glared like a tiger; the Five Great were not on the frontier, and I often feared it.

manualTranslations.zh: 今亮殞沒，蓋宗族得全，西戎靜息，大小為慶。」
manualTranslations.literal: Now that Liang has fallen, perhaps the clans may be preserved whole, the Western Rong quieted, and great and small may rejoice."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Now that Liang is gone, perhaps the clans may be preserved, the western frontier quieted, and all may rejoice."

manualTranslations.zh: 後主怒，下獄誅之。〉
manualTranslations.literal: The Later Lord was enraged and had him imprisoned and executed.〉
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Later Lord was enraged, imprisoned him, and had him executed.〉

sourceRange.text: 建安五年，曹公與袁紹相拒於官渡，策陰欲襲許。迎漢帝，呉録曰：「時有高岱者，隱於餘姚，策命出，使會稽丞陸昭逆之，策虛己候焉。聞其善左傳，乃自玩讀，欲與論講。或謂之曰：『高岱以將軍但英武而已，無文學之才，若與論傳而或云不知者，則某言符矣。』又謂岱曰：『孫將軍爲人，惡勝己者，若每問，當言不知，乃合意耳。如皆辨義，此必危殆。』岱以爲然，及與論傳，或答不知。策果怒，以爲輕己，乃囚之。知交及時人皆露坐爲請。策登樓，望見數里中塡滿。策惡其收衆心，遂殺之。岱字孔文，呉郡人也。受性聰達，輕財貴義。其友士拔奇，取於未顯，所友八人，皆世之英偉也。太守盛憲以爲上計，舉孝廉。許貢來領郡，岱將憲避難於許昭家，求救於陶謙。謙未卽救，岱憔悴泣血，水漿不入口。謙感其忠壯，有申包胥之義，許爲出軍，以書與貢。岱得謙書以還，而貢已囚其母。呉人大小皆爲危竦，以貢宿忿，往必見害。岱言在君則爲君，且母在牢獄，期於當往，若得入見，事自當解。遂通書自白，貢卽與相見。才辭敏捷，好自陳謝，貢登時出其母。岱將見貢，語友人張允、沈䁕令豫具船，以貢必悔，當追逐之。出便將母乘船易道而逃。貢須臾遣人追之，令追者若及於船，江上便殺之，已過則止。使與岱錯道，遂免。被誅時，年三十餘。」《江表傳》曰：「時有道士琅邪于吉，先寓居東方，往來呉會，立精舍，燒香讀道書，製作符水以治病，呉會人多事之。策嘗於郡城門樓上，集會諸將賓客，吉乃盛服杖小函，漆畫之，名爲仙人鏵，趨度門下。諸將賓客三分之二下樓迎拜之，掌賓者禁呵不能止。策卽令收之。諸事之者，悉使婦女入見策母，請救之。母謂策曰：『于先生亦助軍作福，醫護將士，不可殺之。』策曰：『此子妖妄，能幻惑衆心，遠使諸將不復相顧君臣之禮，盡委策下樓拜之，不可不除也。』諸將復連名通白事陳乞之，策曰：『昔南陽張津爲交州刺史，舍前聖典訓，廢漢家法律，嘗著絳帕頭，鼓琴燒香，讀邪俗道書，云以助化，卒爲南夷所殺。此甚無益，諸君但未悟耳。今此子已在鬼籙，勿復費紙筆也。』卽催斬之，縣首於巿。諸事之者，尙不謂其死而云屍解焉，復祭祀求福。」志林曰：『初順帝時，琅邪宮崇詣闕上師于吉所得神書於曲陽泉水上，白素朱界，號太平靑領道，凡百餘卷。順帝至建安中，五六十歳，于吉是時近已百年，年在耄悼，禮不加刑。又天子巡狩，問百年者，就而見之，敬齒以親愛，聖王之至教也。吉罪不及死，而暴加酷刑，是乃謬誅，非所以爲美也。喜推考桓王之薨，建安五年四月四日。是時曹袁相攻，未有勝負。案夏侯元讓與石威則書，袁紹破後也。」此爲桓王於前亡，張津於後死，不得相讓，譬言津之死意矣。』臣松之案：「太康八年，廣州大中正王範上交廣二州春秋。建安六年，張津猶爲交州牧。江表傳之虛如志林所云。搜神記曰：『』策欲渡江襲許，與吉俱行。時大旱，所在熇厲。策催諸將士使速引船，或身自早出督切，見將吏多在吉許，策因此激怒，言：「我爲不如于吉邪，而先趨務之？」便使收吉。至，呵問之曰：「天旱不雨，道塗艱澀，不時得過，故自早出，而卿不同憂戚，安坐船中作鬼物態，敗吾部伍，今當相除。」令人縛置地上暴之，使請雨，若能感天日中雨者，當原赦，不爾行誅。俄而雲氣上蒸，膚寸而合，比至日中，大雨總至，溪澗盈溢。將士喜悅，以爲吉必見原，並往慶慰。策遂殺之。將士哀惜，共藏其屍。天夜，忽更興雲覆之；明旦往視，不知所在。案江表傳、搜神記于吉事不同，未詳孰是。」密治兵，部署諸將。未發，會爲故呉郡太守許貢客所殺。

sourceRange.text: 」徐州牧陶謙深忌策。策舅呉景，時爲丹楊太守，策乃載母徙曲阿，與呂範，孫河俱就景。因緣召募得數百人。興平元年194年，從袁術。術甚奇之，以堅部曲還策。呉暦曰：「初策在江都時，張紘有母喪。策數詣紘，咨以世務，曰：『方今漢祚中微，天下擾攘，英雄俊傑各擁衆營私，未有能扶危濟亂者也。先君與袁氏共破董卓，功業未遂，卒爲黃祖所害。策雖暗稚，竊有微志，欲從袁揚州求先君餘兵，就舅氏於丹楊，收合流散，東據呉會，報讎雪恥，爲朝廷外籓。君以爲何如？』紘答曰：『旣素空劣，方居衰絰之中，無以奉贊盛略。』策曰：『君高名播越，遠近懷歸。今日事計，決之於君，何得不紆慮啓告，副其高山之望？若微志得展，血讎得報，此乃君之勛力，策心所望也。』因涕泣橫流，顔色不變。紘見策忠壯內發，辭令慷慨，感其志言，乃答曰：『昔周道陵遲，齊晉並興；王室已寧，諸侯貢職。今君紹先侯之軌，有驍武之名，若投丹楊，收兵呉會，則荆揚可一，讎敵可報。據長江，奮威德，誅除群穢，匡輔漢室，功業侔於桓文，豈徒外籓而已哉？方今世亂多難，若功成事立，當與同好俱南濟也。』策曰：『一與君同符合契，（同）有永固之分，今便行矣，以老母弱弟委付於君，策無復回顧之憂。』」江表傳曰：「策徑到壽春見袁術，涕泣而言曰：『亡父昔從長沙入討董卓，與明使君會於南陽，同盟結好；不幸遇難，勛業不終。策感惟先人舊恩，欲自憑結，原明使君垂察其誠。』術甚貴異之，然未肯還其父兵。術謂策曰：『孤始用貴舅爲丹楊太守，賢從伯陽爲都尉，彼精兵之地，可還依召募。』策遂詣丹楊依舅，得數百人，而爲涇縣大帥祖郎所襲，幾至危殆。於是復往見術，術以堅餘兵千餘人還策。」太傅馬日磾杖節安集關東，在壽春以禮辟策，表拜懷義校尉，術大將喬蕤、張勳皆傾心敬焉。術常歎曰：「使術有子如孫郎，死復何恨！」策騎士有罪，逃入術營，隱於內廄。策指使人就斬之，訖，詣術謝。術曰：「兵人好叛，當共疾之，何爲謝也？」由是軍中益畏憚之。術初許策爲九江太守，已而更用丹楊陳紀。後術欲攻徐州，從廬江太守陸康求米三萬斛。康不與，術大怒。策昔曾詣康，康不見，使主簿接之。策常銜恨。術遣策攻康，謂曰：「前錯用陳紀，每恨本意不遂。今若得康，廬江眞卿有也。」策攻康，拔之。術復用其故吏劉勳爲太守，策益失望。先是，劉繇爲揚州刺史，州舊治壽春。

sourceRange.text: 」中平元年，黃巾賊師張角起於魏郡。託有神靈，遣八使以善道教化天下，而潛相連結，自稱黃天泰平。三月甲子，三十六（萬）一旦俱發，天下響應，燔燒郡縣，殺害長吏。獻帝春秋曰：「角稱天公將軍，角弟寶稱地公將軍，寶弟梁稱人公將軍。」漢朝遣車騎將軍皇甫崧、中郎將朱儁將兵討擊之。儁表請堅爲佐軍司馬，鄕里少年隨在下邳者皆願從。堅又募諸商旅及淮泗精兵，合千許人，與儁並力奮擊，所向無前。呉書曰：「堅乘勝深入，於西華失利。堅被創墮馬，臥草中。軍衆分散，不知堅所在。堅所騎驄馬馳還營，踣地呼鳴，將士隨馬於草中得堅。堅還營十數日，創少愈，乃復出戰。」汝穎賊困迫，走保宛城。堅身當一面，登城先入，衆乃蟻附，遂大破之。儁具以狀聞上，拜堅別部司馬。續漢書曰：「儁字公偉，會稽人，少好學，爲郡功曹，察孝廉，舉進士。漢朝以討黃巾功拜車騎將軍，累遷河南尹。董卓見儁，外甚親納，而心忌之，儁亦陰備焉。關東兵起，卓議移都，儁輒止卓。卓雖憚儁，然貪其名重，乃表拜太僕以自副。儁被召不肯受拜，因進曰：「國不宜遷，必孤天下望，成山東之結，臣不見其可也。」有司詰曰：「召君受拜而君拒之，不問徙事而君陳之，何也？」儁曰：「副相國，非臣所堪也。遷都非計，臣之所急也。辭所不堪，進臣所急，臣之所宜也。」有司曰：「遷都之事，初無此計也，就有，未露，何所受聞？」儁曰：「相國董卓爲臣説之，臣聞之於相國。」有司不能屈，朝廷稱服焉。後爲太尉。李傕、郭汜相攻，劫質天子公卿，儁性剛，卽發病而卒。

sourceRange.text: 臣松之以爲張昭雖名重，然不如紘之文也，此書必紘所作。曹公表策爲討逆將軍，封爲呉侯。江表傳曰：「建安二年夏，漢朝遣議郎王誧奉戊辰詔書曰：『董卓逆亂，凶國害民。先將軍堅念在平討，雅意未遂，厥美著聞。策遵善道，求福不回。今以策爲騎都尉，襲爵烏程侯，領會稽太守。』又詔敕曰：『故左將軍袁術不顧朝恩，坐創凶逆，造合虛僞，欲因兵亂，詭詐百姓，聞其言以爲不然。定得使持節、平東將軍、領徐州牧、温侯布上術所造惑衆妖妄，知術鴟梟之性，遂其無道，修治王宮，署置公卿，郊天祀地，殘民害物，爲禍深酷。布前後上策乃心本朝，欲還討術，爲國效節，乞加顯異。夫縣賞俟功，惟勤是與，故便寵授，承襲前邑，重以大郡，榮耀兼至，是策輸力竭命之秋也。其亟與布及行呉郡太守、安東將軍陳瑀戮力一心，同時赴討。』策自以統領兵馬，但以騎都尉領郡爲輕，欲得將軍號，（及）使人諷誧，誧便承制假策明漢將軍。是時，陳瑀屯海西，策奉詔治嚴，當與布瑀參同形勢。行到錢塘，瑀陰圖襲策，遣都尉萬演等密渡江，使持印傳三十餘紐與賊丹楊、宣城、涇、陵陽、始安、黟、歙諸險縣大帥祖郎、焦已及呉郡烏程嚴白虎等，使爲內應，伺策軍發，欲攻取諸郡。策覺之，遣呂範、徐逸攻瑀於海西，大破瑀，獲其吏士妻子四千人。山陽公載記曰：『瑀單騎走冀州，自歸袁紹，紹以爲故安都尉。』呉録載策上表謝曰：『臣以固陋，孤持邊陲。陛下廣播高澤，不遺細節，以臣襲爵，兼典名郡。仰榮顧寵，所不克堪。興平二年十二月二十日，於呉郡曲阿得袁術所呈表，以臣行殄寇將軍；至被詔書，乃知詐擅。雖輒捐廢，猶用悚悸。臣年十七，喪失所怙，懼有不任堂構之鄙，以忝析薪之戒，誠無去病十八建功，世祖列將弱冠佐命。臣初領兵，年未弱冠，雖駑懦不武，然思竭微命。惟術狂惑，爲惡深重。臣憑威靈，奉辭罰罪，庶必獻捷，以報所授。』臣松之案：本傳云孫堅以初平三年卒，策以建安五年卒，策死時年二十六，計堅之亡，策應十八，而此表云十七，則爲不符。張璠張璠後漢紀漢紀及呉歷並以堅初平二年死，此爲是而本傳誤也。江表傳曰：『建安三年，策又遣使貢方物，倍於元年所獻。其年，制書轉拜討逆將軍，改封呉侯。

sourceRange.text: 偕乃報勛，具説形狀，使勛來襲取之。勛得偕書，使潛軍到海昏邑下。宗帥知之，空壁逃匿，勛了無所得。時策西討黃祖，行及石城，聞勛輕身詣海昏，便分遣從兄賁、輔率八千人於彭澤待勛，自與周瑜率二萬人歩襲皖城，卽克之，得術百工及鼓吹部曲三萬餘人，並術勛妻子。賁、輔又於彭澤破勛。勛走入楚江，從尋陽歩上到置馬亭，聞策等已克皖，乃投西塞。至沂，築壘自守，告急於劉表，求救於黃祖。祖遣太子射船軍五千人助勛。策復就攻，大破勛。勛與偕北歸曹公，射亦遁走。策收得勛兵二千餘人，船千艘，遂前進夏口攻黃祖。時劉表遣從子虎、南陽韓晞將長矛五千，來爲黃祖前鋒。

sourceRange.text: 臣松之按《禮記》曾子問子夏曰：『三年之喪，金革之事無避也者，禮與？初有司與？』孔子曰：『吾聞諸老摐曰，昔者魯公伯禽有爲爲之也。』鄭玄注曰：『周人卒哭而致事。時有徐戎作難，伯禽卒哭而徵之，急王事也。』昭所云『伯禽不師』，蓋謂此也。況今奸宄競逐，豺狼滿道，乃欲哀親戚，顧禮制，是猶開門而揖盜，未可以爲仁也。

sourceRange.text: 」壬申，王濬最先到，於是受皓之降，解縛焚櫬，延請相見。《晉陽秋》曰：濬收其圖籍，領州四，郡四十三，縣三百一十三，戶五十二萬三千，吏三萬二千，兵二十三萬，男女口二百三十萬，米穀二百八十萬斛，舟船五千餘艘，後宮五千餘人。伷以皓致印綬於己，遣使送皓。皓舉家西遷，以太康元年五月丁亥集于京邑。四月甲申，詔曰：「孫皓窮迫歸降，前詔待之以不死，今皓垂至，意猶愍之，其賜號爲歸命侯。進給衣服車乘，田三十頃，歲給穀五千斛，錢五十萬，絹五百匹，緜五百斤。」皓太子瑾拜中郎，諸子爲王者，拜郎中。《搜神記》曰：吳以草創之國，信不堅固，邊屯守將皆質其妻子，名曰保質。童子少年，以類相與嬉游者，日有十數。永安二年259年三月，有一異兒，長四尺餘，年可六七歲，衣青衣，來從羣兒戲，諸兒莫之識也。皆問曰：「爾誰家小兒，今日忽來？」荅曰：「見爾羣戲樂，故來耳。」詳而視之，眼有光芒，爚爚外射。諸兒畏之，重問其故。兒乃荅曰：「爾惡我乎？我非人也，乃熒惑星也。將有以告爾：三公鉏，司馬如。」諸兒大驚，或走告大人，大人馳往觀之。兒曰：「舍爾去乎！」竦身而躍，即以化矣。仰而視之，若引一匹練以登天。大人來者，猶及見焉，飄飄漸高，有頃而沒。時吳政峻急，莫敢宣也。後五年而蜀亡，六年而晉興，至是而吳滅，司馬如矣。干寶《晉紀》曰：王濬治船於蜀，吳彥取其流柹以呈孫皓，曰：「晉必有攻吳之計，宜增建平兵。建平不下，終不敢渡江。」皓弗從。陸抗之克步闡，皓意張大，乃使尚廣筮并天下，遇同人之頤，對曰：「吉。庚子歲，青蓋當入洛陽。」故皓不脩其政，而恒有窺上國之志。是歲也，實在庚子。五年，皓死于洛陽。《吳錄》曰：皓以四年十二月死，時年四十二，葬河南縣界。

sourceRange.text: 鳳皇元年272年秋八月，徵西陵督步闡。闡不應，據城降晉。遣樂鄉都督陸抗圍取闡，闡衆悉降。闡及同計數十人皆夷三族。大赦。是歲右丞相萬彧被譴憂死，徙其子弟於廬陵。《江表傳》曰：初皓游華里，彧與丁奉、留平密謀曰：「此行不急，若至華里不歸，社稷事重，不得不自還。」此語頗泄。皓聞知，以彧等舊臣，且以計忍而陰銜之。後因會，以毒酒飲彧，傳酒人私減之。又飲留平，平覺之，服他藥以解，得不死。彧自殺。平憂懣，月餘亦死。何定姦穢發聞，伏誅。皓以其惡似張布，追改定名爲布。《江表傳》曰：定，汝南人，本孫權給使也，後出補吏。定佞邪僭媚，自表先帝舊人，求還內侍，皓以爲樓下都尉，典知酤糴事，專爲威福。而皓信任，委以衆事。定爲子求少府李勗女，不許。定挾忿譖勗於皓，皓尺口誅之，焚其尸。定又使諸將各上好犬，皆千里遠求，一犬至直數千匹。御犬率具纓，直錢一萬。一犬一兵，養以捕兎供厨。所獲無幾。吳人皆歸罪於定，而皓以爲忠勤，賜爵列侯。《吳歷》曰：中書郎奚熙譖宛陵令賀惠。惠，劭弟也。遣使者徐粲訊治，熙又譖粲顧護不即決斷。皓遣使就宛陵斬粲，收惠付獄。會赦得免。

sourceRange.text: 元興元年264年八月，以上大將軍施績、大將軍丁奉爲左右大司馬，張布爲驃騎將軍，加侍中，諸增位班賞，一皆如舊。九月，貶太后爲景皇后，追謚父和曰文皇帝，尊母何爲太后。十月，封休太子𩅦爲豫章王，次子汝南王，次子梁王，次子陳王，立皇后滕氏。《江表傳》曰：皓初立，發優詔，恤士民，開倉廩，振貧乏，科出宮女以配無妻，禽獸擾於苑者皆放之。當時翕然稱爲明主。皓旣得志，麤暴驕盈，多忌諱，好酒色，大小失望。興、布竊悔之。或以譖皓，十一月，誅興、布。十二月，孫休葬定陵。封后父滕牧爲高密侯，《吳歷》曰：牧本名密，避丁密，改名牧，丁密避牧，改名爲固。舅何洪等三人皆列侯。是歲，魏置交阯太守之郡。晉文帝爲魏相國，遣昔吳壽春城降將徐紹、孫彧銜命齎書，陳事勢利害，以申喻皓。《漢晉春秋》載晉文王與皓書曰：「聖人稱有君臣然後有上下禮義，是故大必字小，小必事大，然後上下安服，羣生獲所。逮至末塗，純德旣毀，勦民之命，以爭彊於天下，違禮順之至理，則仁者弗由也。方今主上聖明，覆帱無外，僕備位宰輔，屬當國重。唯華夏乖殊，方隅圮裂，六十餘載，金革亟動，無年不戰，暴骸喪元，困悴罔定，每用悼心，坐以待旦。將欲止戈興仁，爲百姓請命，故分命偏師，平定蜀漢，役未經年，全軍獨克。于時猛將謀夫，朝臣庶士，咸以奉天時之宜，就旣征之軍，藉吞敵之勢，宜遂回旗東指，以臨吳境。舟師汎江，順流而下，陸軍南轅，取徑四郡，兼成都之械，漕巴漢之粟，然後以中軍整旅，三方雲會，未及浹辰，可使江表厎平，南夏順軌。然國朝深惟伐蜀之舉，雖有靜難之功，亦悼蜀民獨罹其害，戰於緜竹者，自元帥以下並受斬戮，伏尸蔽地，血流丹野。一之於前，猶追恨不忍，況重之於後乎？是故旋師案甲，思與南邦共全百姓之命。夫料力忖勢，度資量險，遠考古昔廢興之理，近鑒西蜀安危之効，隆德保祚，去危即順，屈己以寧四海者，仁哲之高致也；履危偷安，隕德覆祚，而不稱於後世者，非智者之所居也。今朝廷遣徐紹、孫彧獻書喻懷，若書御於前，必少留意，回慮革筭，結歡弭兵，共爲一家，惠矜吳會，施及中土，豈不泰哉！此昭心之大願也，敢不承受。若不獲命，則普天率土，期於大同，雖重干戈，固不獲已也。」甘露元年265年三月，皓遣使隨紹、彧報書曰：「知以高世之才，處宰輔之任，漸導之功，勤亦至矣。孤以不德，階承統緒，思與賢良共濟世道，而以壅隔未有所緣，嘉意允著，深用依依。今遣光祿大夫紀陟、五官中郎將弘璆宣明至懷。」《江表傳》曰：皓書兩頭言白，稱名言而不著姓。《吳錄》曰：陟字子上，丹楊人。初爲中書郎，孫峻使詰南陽王和，令其引分。陟密使令正辭自理，峻怒。陟懼，閉門不出。孫休時，父亮爲尚書令，而陟爲中書令，每朝會，詔以屏風隔其座。出爲豫章太守。干寶《晉紀》曰：陟、璆奉使如魏，入境而問諱，入國而問俗。壽春將王布示之馬射，旣而問之曰：「吳之君子亦能斯乎？」陟曰：「此軍人騎士肄業所及，士大夫君子未有爲之者矣。」布大慙。旣至，魏帝見之，使儐問曰：「來時吳王何如？」陟對曰：「來時皇帝臨軒，百寮陪位，御膳無恙。」晉文王饗之，百寮畢會，使儐者告曰：「某者安樂公也，某者匈奴單于也。」陟曰：「西主失土，爲君王所禮，位同三代，莫不感義，匈奴邊塞難羈之國，君王懷之，親在坐席，此誠威恩遠著。」又問：「吳之戍備幾何？」對曰：「自西陵以至江都，五千七百里。」又問曰：「道里甚遠，難爲堅固？」對曰：「疆界雖遠，而其險要必爭之地，不過數四，猶人雖有八尺之軀靡不受患，其護風寒亦數處耳。」文王善之，厚爲之禮。臣松之以爲人有八尺之體靡不受患，防護風寒豈唯數處？取譬若此，未足稱能。若曰譬如金城萬雉，所急防者四門而已。方陟此對，不猶愈乎！《吳錄》曰：皓以諸父與和相連及者，家屬皆徙東冶，唯陟以有密旨，特封子孚都亭侯。孚弟瞻，字思遠，入仕晉驃騎將軍。弘璆，曲阿人，弘咨之孫，權外甥也。璆後至中書令、太子少傅。紹行到濡須，召還殺之，徙其家屬建安，始有白紹稱美中國者故也。夏四月，蔣陵言甘露降，於是改年大赦。秋七月，皓逼殺景后朱氏，亡不在正殿，於苑中小屋治喪，衆知其非疾病，莫不痛切。又送休四子於吳小城，尋復追殺大者二人。九月，從西陵督步闡表，徙都武昌，御史大夫丁固、右將軍諸葛靚鎮建業。陟、璆至洛，遇晉文帝崩，十一月，乃遣還。皓至武昌，又大赦。以零陵南部爲始安郡，桂陽南部爲始興郡。十二月，晉受禪。寶鼎元年正月，遣大鴻臚張儼、五官中郎將丁忠弔祭晉文帝。及還，儼道病死。《吳錄》曰：儼字子節，吳人也。弱冠知名，歷顯位，以博聞多識，拜大鴻臚。使于晉，皓謂儼曰：「今南北通好，以君爲有出境之才，故相屈行。」對曰：「皇皇者華，蒙其榮耀，無古人延譽之美，磨厲鋒鍔，思不辱命。」旣至，車騎將軍賈充、尚書令裴秀、侍中荀勗等欲傲以所不知而不能屈。尚書僕射羊祜、尚書何楨並結縞帶之好。忠說皓曰：「北方守戰之具不設，弋陽可襲而取。」皓訪羣臣，鎮西大將軍陸凱曰：「夫兵不得已而用之耳，且三國鼎立已來，更相侵伐，無歲寧居。今彊敵新并巴蜀，有兼土之實，而遣使求親，欲息兵役，不可謂其求援於我。今敵形勢方彊，而欲徼幸求勝，未見其利也。」車騎將軍劉纂曰：「天生五才，誰能去兵？譎詐相雄，有自來矣。若其有闕，庸可棄乎？宜遣閒諜，以觀其勢。」皓陰納纂言，且以蜀新平，故不行，然遂自絕。八月，所在言得大鼎，於是改年，大赦。以陸凱爲左丞相，常侍萬彧爲右丞相。冬十月，永安山賊施但等聚衆數千人，《吳錄》曰：永安今武康縣也。劫皓庶弟永安侯謙出烏程，取孫和陵上鼓吹曲蓋。比至建業，衆萬餘人。丁固、諸葛靚逆之於牛屯，大戰，但等敗走。獲謙，謙自殺。《漢晉春秋》曰：初望氣者云荊州有王氣破揚州而建業宮不利，故皓徙武昌，遣使者發民掘荊州界大臣名家冢與山岡連者以厭之。旣聞但反，自以爲徙土得計也。使數百人鼓譟入建業，殺但妻子，云天子使荊州兵來破揚州賊，以厭前氣。分會稽爲東陽郡，分吳、丹楊爲吳興郡。皓詔曰：「古者分土建國，所以襃賞賢能，廣樹藩屏。秦毀五等爲三十六郡，漢室初興，闓立乃至百五，因事制宜，蓋無常數也。今吳郡陽羨、永安、餘杭、臨水及丹楊故鄣、安吉、原鄉、於潛諸縣，地勢水流之便，悉注烏程，旣宜立郡以鎮山越，且以藩衞明陵，奉承大祭，不亦可乎！其亟分此九縣爲吳興郡，治烏程。」以零陵北部爲邵陵郡。十二月，皓還都建業，衞將軍滕牧留鎮武昌。

sourceRange.text: 四年夏五月，大雨，水泉涌溢。秋八月，遣光祿大夫周弈、石偉巡行風俗，察將吏清濁，民所疾苦，爲黜陟之詔。《楚國先賢傳》曰：石偉字公操，南郡人。少好學，脩節不怠，介然獨立，有不可奪之志。舉茂才、賢良方正，皆不就。孫休即位，特徵偉，累遷至光祿勳。及皓即位，朝政昏亂，偉乃辭老耄痼疾乞身，就拜光祿大夫。吳平，建威將軍王戎親詣偉。太康二年，詔曰：「吳故光祿大夫石偉，秉志清白，皓首不渝，難處危亂，廉節可紀。年已過邁，不堪遠涉，其以偉爲議郎，加二千石秩，以終厥世。」偉遂陽狂及盲，不受晉爵。年八十三，太熙元年卒。九月，布山言白龍見。是歲，安吳民陳焦死，埋之，六日更生，穿土中出。

sourceRange.text: 天璽元年276年，吳郡言臨平湖自漢末草穢壅塞，今更開通。長老相傳，此湖塞，天下亂，此湖開，天下平。又於湖邊得石函，中有小石，青白色，長四寸，廣二寸餘，刻上作皇帝字，於是改年，大赦。會稽太守車浚、湘東太守張詠不出筭緡，就在所斬之，徇首諸郡。《江表傳》曰：浚在公清忠，值郡荒旱，民無資糧，表求振貸。皓謂浚欲樹私恩，遣人梟首。又尚書熊睦見皓酷虐，微有所諫，皓使人以刀環撞殺之，身無完肌。秋八月，京下督孫楷降晉。鄱陽言歷陽山石文理成字，凡二十，云「楚九州渚，吳九州都，揚州士，作天子，四世治，太平始」。《江表傳》曰：歷陽縣有石山臨水，高百丈，其三十丈所，有七穿駢羅，穿中色黃赤，不與本體相似，俗相傳謂之石印。又云，石印封發，天下當太平。下有祠屋，巫祝言石印神有三郎。時歷陽長表上言石印發，皓遣使以太牢祭歷山。巫言，石印三郎說「天下方太平」。使者作高梯，上看印文，詐以朱書石作二十字，還以啟皓。皓大喜曰：「吳當爲九州作都、渚乎！從大皇帝逮孤四世矣，太平之主，非孤復誰？」重遣使，以印綬拜三郎爲王，又刻石立銘，襃贊靈德，以荅休祥。又吳興陽羨山有空石，長十餘丈，名曰石室，在所表爲大瑞。乃遣兼司徒董朝、兼太常周處至陽羨縣，封襌國山。明年改元，大赦，以恊石文。

sourceRange.text: 詔曰：「」二年春正月，震電。三月，備九卿官，詔曰：「」三年春三月，西陵言赤烏見。

localRange.text: 詔曰：「古者建國，教學爲先，所以道世治性，爲時養器也。自建興以來，時事多故，吏民頗以目前趨務，去本就末，不循古道。夫所尚不惇，則傷化敗俗。其案古置學官，立五經博士，核取應選，加其寵祿，科見吏之中及將吏子弟有志好者，各令就業。一歲課試，差其品第，加以位賞。使見之者樂其榮，聞之者羨其譽。以敦王化，以隆風俗。二年春正月，震電。三月，備九卿官，詔曰：「朕以不德，託于王公之上，夙夜戰戰，忘寢與食。今欲偃武脩文，以崇大化。推此之道，當由士民之贍，必須農桑。管子有言：『倉廩實，知禮節；衣食足，知榮辱。夫一夫不耕，有受其饑，一婦不織，有受其寒；饑寒並至而民不爲非者，未之有也。自頃年已來，州郡吏民及諸營兵，多違此業，皆浮船長江，賈作上下，良田漸廢，見穀日少，欲求大定，豈可得哉？亦由租入過重，農人利薄，使之然乎！今欲廣開田業，輕其賦稅，差科彊羸，課其田畝，務令優均，官私得所，使家給戶贍，足相供養，則愛身重命，不犯科法，然後刑罰不用，風俗可整。以羣僚之忠賢，若盡心於時，雖太古盛化，未可卒致，漢文升平，庶幾可及。及之則臣主俱榮，不及則損削侵辱，何可從容俯仰而已？諸卿尚書，可共咨度，務取便佳。田桑已至，不可後時。事定施行，稱朕意焉。三年春三月，西陵言赤烏見。

sourceRange.text: 孫休字子烈，權第六子。年十三，從中書郎射慈、郎中盛冲受學。太元二年252年正月，封琅邪王，居虎林。四月，權薨，休弟亮承統，諸葛恪秉政，不欲諸王在濵江兵馬之地，徙休於丹楊郡。太守李衡數以事侵休，休上書乞徙他郡，詔徙會稽。居數歲，夢乘龍上天，顧不見尾，覺而異之。孫亮廢，己未，孫綝使宗正孫楷與中書郎董朝迎休。休初聞問，意疑，楷、朝具述綝等所以奉迎本意，留一日二夜，遂發。十月戊寅，行至曲阿，有老公干休叩頭曰：「事乆變生，天下喁喁，願陛下速行。」休善之，是日進及布塞亭。武衞將軍恩行丞相事，率百僚以乘輿法駕迎於永昌亭，築宮，以武帳爲便殿，設御座。己卯，休至，望便殿止住，使孫楷先見恩。楷還，休乘輦進，羣臣再拜稱臣。休升便殿，謙不即御坐，止東廂。戶曹尚書前即階下讚奏，丞相奉璽符。休三讓，羣臣三請。休曰：「將相諸侯咸推寡人，寡人敢不承受璽符。」羣臣以次奉引，休就乘輿，百官陪位，綝以兵千人迎於半野，拜于道側，休下車荅拜。即日，御正殿，大赦，改元。是歲，於魏甘露三年258年也。永安元年258年冬十月壬午，詔曰：「夫襃德賞功，古今通義。其以大將軍綝爲丞相、荊州牧，增食五縣。武衞將軍恩爲御史大夫、衞將軍、中軍督，封縣侯。威遠將軍授爲右將軍、縣侯。偏將軍幹雜號將軍、亭侯。長水校尉張布輔導勤勞，以布爲輔義將軍，封永康侯。董朝親迎，封爲鄉侯。」又詔曰：「丹陽太守李衡，以往事之嫌，自拘有司。夫射鉤斬袪，在君爲君，遣衡還郡，勿令自疑。」《襄陽記》曰：衡字叔平，本襄陽卒家子也，漢末入吳爲武昌庶民。聞羊衜有人物之鑒，往干之，衜曰：「多事之世，尚書劇曹郎才也。」是時校事呂壹操弄權柄，大臣畏偪，莫有敢言，衜曰：「非李衡無能困之者。」遂共薦爲郎。權引見，衡口陳壹姦短數千言，權有愧色。數月，壹被誅，而衡大見顯擢。後常爲諸葛恪司馬，幹恪府事。恪被誅，求爲丹楊太守。時孫休在郡治，衡數以法繩之。妻習氏每諫衡，衡不從。會休立，衡憂懼，謂妻曰：「不用卿言，以至於此。」遂欲奔魏。妻曰：「不可。君本庶民耳，先帝相拔過重，旣數作無禮，而復逆自猜嫌，逃叛求活，以此北歸，何面見中國人乎？」衡曰：「計何所出？」妻曰：「琅邪王素好善慕名，方欲自顯於天下，終不以私嫌殺君明矣。可自囚詣獄，表列前失，顯求受罪。如此，乃當逆見優饒，非但直活而已。」衡從之，果得無患，又加威遠將軍，援以棨戟。衡每欲治家，妻輙不聽，後密遣客十人於武陵龍陽汎洲上作宅，種甘橘千株。臨死，勑兒曰：「汝母惡我治家，故窮如是。然吾州里有千頭木奴，不責汝衣食，歲上一匹絹，亦可足用耳。」衡亡後二十餘日，兒以白母，母曰：「此當是種甘橘也，汝家失十戶客來七八年，必汝父遣爲宅。汝父恒稱太史公言，『江陵千樹橘，當封君家』。吾荅曰：『且人患無德義，不患不富，若貴而能貧，方好耳，用此何爲！』」吳末，衡甘橘成，歲得絹數千匹，家道殷足。晉咸康中，其宅止枯樹猶在。己丑，封孫皓爲烏程侯，皓弟德錢唐侯，謙永安侯。《江表傳》曰：羣臣奏立皇后、太子，詔曰：「朕以寡德，奉承洪業，莅事日淺，恩澤未敷，加后妃之號，嗣子之位，非所急也。」有司又固請，休謙虛不許。

localRange.text: 〈《吳錄》載休詔曰：「人之有名，以相紀別，長爲作字，憚其名耳。禮，名子欲令難犯易避，五十稱伯仲，古或一字。今人競作好名好字，又令相配，所行不副，此瞽字伯明者也，孤常哂之。或師友父兄所作，或自己爲；師友尚可，父兄猶非，自爲最不謙。孤今爲四男作名字：太子名𩅦，𩅦音如『湖水灣澳』之灣，字莔，莔音如『迄今』之迄；次子名𩃙，𩃙音如『兕觥』之觥，字𧟨，𧟨音如『玄礥首』之礥；次子名壾，壾音如『草莽』之莽，字昷，昷音如『舉物』之舉；次子名𠅬，𠅬音如『襃衣下寬大』之襃，字㷏，㷏音如『有所擁持』之擁。此都不與世所用者同，故鈔舊文會合作之。夫書八體損益，因事而生，今造此名字，旣不相配，又字但一，庶易棄避，其普告天下，使咸聞知。臣松之以爲傳稱「名以制義，義以出禮，禮以體政，政以正民。

context.afterSource: 是以政成而民聽，易則生亂」。

sourceRange.text: 孫休朱夫人，朱據女，休姊公主所生也。臣松之以為休妻其甥，事同漢惠。荀悅譏之已當，故不復廣言。赤烏末，權為休納以為妃。休為琅邪王，隨居丹楊。建興中，孫峻專政，公族皆患之。全尚妻即峻姊。故惟全主祐焉。初，孫和為太子時，全主譖害王夫人，欲廢太子，立魯王，朱主不聽，由是有隙。五鳳中，孫儀謀殺峻，事覺被誅。全主因言朱主與儀同謀，峻枉殺朱主。休懼，遣夫人還建業，執手泣別。既至，峻遣還休。太平中，孫亮知朱主為全主所害，問朱主死意？全主懼曰：「我實不知，皆據二子熊、損所白。」亮殺熊、損。損妻是峻妹也，孫綝益忌亮，遂廢亮，立休。永安五年262年，立夫人為皇后。休卒，群臣尊夫人為皇太后，孫皓即位月餘，貶為景皇后。稱安定宮。甘露元年265年七月，見逼薨，合葬定陵。《搜神記》曰：孫峻殺朱主，埋於石子岡。歸命即位，將欲改葬之。塚墓相亞，不可識別，而宮人頗識主亡時所著衣服，乃使兩巫各住一處以伺其靈，使察鑑之，不得相近。久時，二人俱白：見一女人年可三十餘，上著青錦束頭，紫白袷裳，丹綈絲履，從石子岡上半岡，而以手抑膝長太息，小住須臾，進一塚上便住，徘徊良久，奄然不見。二人之言，不謀而同，於是開塚，衣服如之。孫和何姬，丹楊句容人也。父遂，本騎士。孫權嘗遊幸諸營，而姬觀於道中，權望見異之，命宦者召入，以賜子和。生男，權喜。名之曰彭祖，即皓也。太子和既廢，後為南陽王，居長沙。孫亮即位，孫峻輔政。峻素媚事全主，全主與和母有隙，遂勸峻徙和居新都，遣使賜死，嫡妃張氏亦自殺。何姬曰：「若皆從死，誰當養孤？」遂拊育皓及其三弟。皓即位，尊和為昭獻皇帝，《吳錄》曰：皓初尊和為昭獻皇帝，俄改曰文皇帝。何姬為昭獻皇后，稱昇平宮，月餘，進為皇太后。封弟洪永平侯，蔣溧陽侯，植宣城侯。洪卒，子邈嗣，為武陵監軍，為晉所殺。植官至大司徒。吳末昏亂，何氏驕僭，子弟橫放，百姓患之。故民訛言「皓久死，立者何氏子」云。《江表傳》曰：皓以張布女為美人，有寵，皓問曰：「汝父所在？」答曰：「賊以殺之。」皓大怒，棒殺之。後思其顏色，使巧工刻木作美人形象，恆置座側。問左右：「布復有女否？」答曰：「布大女適故衛尉馮朝子純。」即奪純妻入宮，大有寵，拜為左夫人，晝夜與夫人房宴，不聽朝政，使尚方以金作華燧、步搖、假髻以千數。令宮人著以相撲，朝成夕敗，輒出更作，工匠因緣偷盜，府藏為空。會夫人死，皓哀愍思念，葬於苑中，大作塚，使工匠刻柏作木人，內塚中以為兵衛，以金銀珍玩之物送葬，不可稱計。已葬之後，皓治喪於內，半年不出。國人見葬太奢麗，皆謂皓已死，所葬者是也。皓舅子何都顏狀似皓，云都代立。臨海太守奚熙信訛言，舉兵欲還誅都，都叔父植時為備海督，擊殺熙，夷三族，訛言乃息，而人心猶疑。孫皓滕夫人，故太常胤之族女也。胤夷滅，夫人父牧，以疏遠徙邊郡。孫休即位，大赦，得還，以牧為五官中郎。皓既封烏程侯，聘牧女為妃。皓即位，立為皇后，封牧高密侯，拜衛將軍，錄尚書事。後朝士以牧尊戚，頗推令諫爭。而夫人寵漸衰，皓滋不悅，皓母何恆左右之。又太史言，於運歷，后不可易，皓信巫覡，故得不廢，常供養昇平宮。牧見遣居蒼梧郡，雖爵位不奪，其實裔也，遂道路憂死。長秋官僚，備員而已，受朝賀表疏如故。而皓內諸寵姬，佩皇后璽紱者多矣。《江表傳》曰：皓又使黃門備行州郡，科取將吏家女。其二千石大臣子女，皆當歲歲言名，年十五六一簡閱，簡閱不中，乃得出嫁。后宮千數，而採擇無已。天紀四年，隨皓遷於洛陽。

localRange.text: 朱夫人滕夫人【評】

manualTranslations.zh: 孫休朱夫人，朱據女，休姊公主所生也。
manualTranslations.literal: Sun Xiu's Lady Zhu was the daughter of Zhu Ju, born to Xiu's elder sister the princess.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sun Xiu's consort Lady Zhu was Zhu Ju's daughter, born to Xiu's elder sister the princess.

manualTranslations.zh: 臣松之以為休妻其甥，事同漢惠。
manualTranslations.literal: Your servant Songzhi considers that Xiu married his nephew's daughter, the case being the same as Emperor Hui of Han.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi notes that Sun Xiu married his niece—parallel to Emperor Hui of Han.

manualTranslations.zh: 荀悅譏之已當，故不復廣言。
manualTranslations.literal: Xun Yue's censure was already apt; therefore I do not expand further.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Xun Yue's censure was apt enough, so I say no more.

manualTranslations.zh: 赤烏末，權為休納以為妃。
manualTranslations.literal: At the end of Chiwu, Quan took her in marriage for Xiu to be consort.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Late in the Chiwu era Sun Quan betrothed her to Sun Xiu as consort.

manualTranslations.zh: 休為琅邪王，隨居丹楊。
manualTranslations.literal: Xiu was Prince of Langye and dwelt accordingly in Danyang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sun Xiu was Prince of Langye and lived with her in Danyang.

manualTranslations.zh: 建興中，孫峻專政，公族皆患之。
manualTranslations.literal: In the Jianxing period Sun Jun monopolized government; the imperial clan all feared it.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: During Jianxing Sun Jun seized power, and every member of the imperial house feared him.

manualTranslations.zh: 全尚妻即峻姊。
manualTranslations.literal: Quan Shang's wife was Jun's elder sister.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Quan Shang had married Jun's elder sister.

manualTranslations.zh: 故惟全主祐焉。
manualTranslations.literal: Therefore only the Princess of Quan protected her.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Only Princess Quan (Sun Luban) therefore shielded Lady Zhu.

manualTranslations.zh: 初，孫和為太子時，全主譖害王夫人，欲廢太子，立魯王，朱主不聽，由是有隙。
manualTranslations.literal: At first, when Sun He was heir apparent, the Princess of Quan slandered Lady Wang, wishing to depose the heir and establish the Prince of Lu; Lady Zhu would not listen, and from this there was a rift.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Sun He was crown prince, Princess Quan slandered Lady Wang to depose the heir and elevate the Prince of Lu; Lady Zhu refused to go along, and a feud opened between them.

manualTranslations.zh: 五鳳中，孫儀謀殺峻，事覺被誅。
manualTranslations.literal: In the Wufeng period Sun Yi plotted to kill Jun; the affair was discovered and he was executed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Wufeng Sun Yi plotted to kill Sun Jun; the plot was exposed and he was executed.

manualTranslations.zh: 全主因言朱主與儀同謀，峻枉殺朱主。
manualTranslations.literal: The Princess of Quan thereupon said Lady Zhu had conspired with Yi; Jun wrongly killed Lady Zhu.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Princess Quan then claimed Lady Zhu had conspired with Sun Yi, and Jun had Lady Zhu executed on false grounds.

manualTranslations.zh: 休懼，遣夫人還建業，執手泣別。
manualTranslations.literal: Xiu was afraid and sent the lady back to Jianye, clasping hands and weeping in parting.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Terrified, Sun Xiu sent Lady Zhu back to Jianye, weeping as they clasped hands in farewell.

manualTranslations.zh: 既至，峻遣還休。
manualTranslations.literal: When she arrived, Jun sent her back to Xiu.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Once she reached the capital, Jun sent her back to Sun Xiu.

manualTranslations.zh: 太平中，孫亮知朱主為全主所害，問朱主死意？
manualTranslations.literal: In the Taiping period Sun Liang learned Lady Zhu had been harmed by the Princess of Quan and asked about the circumstances of Lady Zhu's death.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Taiping Sun Liang learned Princess Quan had engineered Lady Zhu's death and questioned her about it.

manualTranslations.zh: 全主懼曰：「我實不知，皆據二子熊、損所白。」
manualTranslations.literal: The Princess of Quan, afraid, said, "I truly did not know; it was all reported by Ju's two sons Xiong and Sun."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Princess Quan, terrified, said, "I truly knew nothing—it all came from Zhu Ju's sons Xiong and Sun."

manualTranslations.zh: 亮殺熊、損。
manualTranslations.literal: Liang killed Xiong and Sun.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sun Liang had Zhu Xiong and Zhu Sun executed.

manualTranslations.zh: 損妻是峻妹也，孫綝益忌亮，遂廢亮，立休。
manualTranslations.literal: Sun's wife was Jun's younger sister; Sun Chen grew ever more jealous of Liang, then deposed Liang and established Xiu.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhu Sun's wife was Jun's sister; Sun Chen, ever more hostile to Sun Liang, deposed him and raised Sun Xiu to the throne.

manualTranslations.zh: 永安五年262年，立夫人為皇后。
manualTranslations.literal: In the fifth year of Yong'an (262 CE), he established the lady as empress.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Yong'an 5 (262) he made Lady Zhu empress.

manualTranslations.zh: 休卒，群臣尊夫人為皇太后，孫皓即位月餘，貶為景皇后。
manualTranslations.literal: When Xiu died, the host of ministers honored the lady as empress dowager; a little more than a month after Sun Hao succeeded, she was demoted to Empress Jing.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At Sun Xiu's death the court hailed her as empress dowager; a month after Sun Hao took the throne she was reduced to Empress Jing.

manualTranslations.zh: 稱安定宮。
manualTranslations.literal: She was styled the Palace of Anding.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: She was given the title Palace of Anding.

manualTranslations.zh: 甘露元年265年七月，見逼薨，合葬定陵。
manualTranslations.literal: In the seventh month of the first year of Ganlu (265 CE), she was forced and died; joint burial at Ding Mausoleum.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Ganlu 1 (265) she was driven to her death and was buried with Sun Xiu at Ding Mausoleum.

manualTranslations.zh: 《搜神記》曰：孫峻殺朱主，埋於石子岡。
manualTranslations.literal: The Soushen ji states: Sun Jun killed Lady Zhu and buried her at Shizi Hill.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Soushen ji says Sun Jun killed Lady Zhu and buried her on Shizi Hill.

manualTranslations.zh: 歸命即位，將欲改葬之。
manualTranslations.literal: When the Lord Who Surrenders succeeded, he was about to rebury her.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Sun Hao took the throne as Lord Who Surrenders, he meant to give her a proper reburial.

manualTranslations.zh: 塚墓相亞，不可識別，而宮人頗識主亡時所著衣服，乃使兩巫各住一處以伺其靈，使察鑑之，不得相近。
manualTranslations.literal: Tombs and graves pressed close together and could not be distinguished; yet palace women fairly well knew the clothes the lady wore at death; therefore he sent two shamans each to dwell in one place to watch for her spirit and have them identify it, not allowing them to approach each other.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The graves lay too close to tell apart, but palace women remembered the clothes Lady Zhu wore at death; Sun Hao posted two shamans at separate spots to watch for her spirit and identify the grave, forbidding them to compare notes.

manualTranslations.zh: 久時，二人俱白：見一女人年可三十餘，上著青錦束頭，紫白袷裳，丹綈絲履，從石子岡上半岡，而以手抑膝長太息，小住須臾，進一塚上便住，徘徊良久，奄然不見。
manualTranslations.literal: After a long while both reported: they saw a woman of perhaps thirty-odd years, wearing green brocade head-binding, purple-and-white lined robe, and red silk shoes; from halfway up Shizi Hill she came, pressing her knee with her hand and sighing long; pausing briefly, she advanced to one grave and stopped, pacing for a long while, then suddenly vanished.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After a long wait both reported the same vision: a woman of about thirty in green brocade head-wrap, purple-and-white lined robe, and red silk shoes climbed halfway up Shizi Hill, pressed her knee, sighed, paused at one mound, wandered awhile, and vanished.

manualTranslations.zh: 二人之言，不謀而同，於是開塚，衣服如之。
manualTranslations.literal: The two men's words matched without prior agreement; thereupon they opened the grave, and the clothes were as described.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Their accounts matched without collusion; they opened the grave and found the clothes just as described.

manualTranslations.zh: 孫和何姬，丹楊句容人也。
manualTranslations.literal: Sun He's Lady He was a native of Jurong in Danyang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sun He's consort Lady He came from Jurong in Danyang.

manualTranslations.zh: 父遂，本騎士。
manualTranslations.literal: Her father Sui was originally a mounted soldier.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Her father He Sui had been a cavalryman.

manualTranslations.zh: 孫權嘗遊幸諸營，而姬觀於道中，權望見異之，命宦者召入，以賜子和。
manualTranslations.literal: Sun Quan once toured the various camps, and the lady watched from the road; Quan saw her from afar and thought her unusual, ordered a eunuch to summon her in, and bestowed her on He.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sun Quan once inspected the camps; Lady He stood watching from the road. Struck by her looks, he had a eunuch bring her in and gave her to Sun He.

manualTranslations.zh: 生男，權喜。
manualTranslations.literal: She bore a son; Quan was pleased.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: She bore a son, to Sun Quan's delight.

manualTranslations.zh: 名之曰彭祖，即皓也。
manualTranslations.literal: He named him Pengzu—that is, Hao.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sun Quan named the boy Pengzu—later Sun Hao.

manualTranslations.zh: 太子和既廢，後為南陽王，居長沙。
manualTranslations.literal: After the heir He was deposed, he later became Prince of Nanyang and dwelt at Changsha.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After Sun He lost the heirship he was made Prince of Nanyang and sent to Changsha.

manualTranslations.zh: 孫亮即位，孫峻輔政。
manualTranslations.literal: When Sun Liang succeeded, Sun Jun assisted in government.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Sun Liang took the throne, Sun Jun served as regent.

manualTranslations.zh: 峻素媚事全主，全主與和母有隙，遂勸峻徙和居新都，遣使賜死，嫡妃張氏亦自殺。
manualTranslations.literal: Jun had long flattered and served the Princess of Quan; the princess and He's mother were at odds, so she urged Jun to move He to Xindu, sent envoys to grant death, and the principal consort Lady Zhang also killed herself.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Jun had long curried favor with Princess Quan, who feuded with Sun He's mother; she talked Jun into exiling Sun He to Xindu and sending orders for his death, and Lady Zhang, his principal consort, killed herself as well.

manualTranslations.zh: 何姬曰：「若皆從死，誰當養孤？」
manualTranslations.literal: Lady He said, "If all follow in death, who will raise the orphan?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Lady He said, "If we all die with him, who will raise these children?"

manualTranslations.zh: 遂拊育皓及其三弟。
manualTranslations.literal: Thereupon she nurtured and raised Hao and his three younger brothers.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: She then raised Sun Hao and his three younger brothers.

manualTranslations.zh: 皓即位，尊和為昭獻皇帝，《吳錄》曰：皓初尊和為昭獻皇帝，俄改曰文皇帝。
manualTranslations.literal: When Hao succeeded, he honored He as Emperor Zhaoxian; the Wu lu states: at first Hao honored He as Emperor Zhaoxian, soon changing it to Emperor Wen.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Sun Hao succeeded he canonized Sun He as Emperor Zhaoxian; the Wu lu adds that he soon changed the title to Emperor Wen.

manualTranslations.zh: 何姬為昭獻皇后，稱昇平宮，月餘，進為皇太后。
manualTranslations.literal: Lady He was Empress Zhaoxian, styled the Palace of Shengping; after a little more than a month she was advanced to empress dowager.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Lady He became Empress Zhaoxian with the title Palace of Shengping, and a month later was raised to empress dowager.

manualTranslations.zh: 封弟洪永平侯，蔣溧陽侯，植宣城侯。
manualTranslations.literal: He enfeoffed younger brothers Hong as Marquis of Yongping, Jiang as Marquis of Liyang, and Zhi as Marquis of Xuancheng.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He enfeoffed her brothers He Hong as Marquis of Yongping, Jiang as Marquis of Liyang, and Zhi as Marquis of Xuancheng.

manualTranslations.zh: 洪卒，子邈嗣，為武陵監軍，為晉所殺。
manualTranslations.literal: When Hong died, his son Miao succeeded, served as military inspector of Wuling, and was killed by Jin.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Hong died; his heir Miao became inspector of Wuling and was killed by Jin.

manualTranslations.zh: 植官至大司徒。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhi reached office as Grand Minister of Works.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhi rose to Grand Minister of Works.

manualTranslations.zh: 吳末昏亂，何氏驕僭，子弟橫放，百姓患之。
manualTranslations.literal: At the end of Wu there was confusion and disorder; the He clan was arrogant and overbearing, sons and younger brothers ran wild, and the common people suffered from it.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Wu's final years the He clan grew arrogant and their sons ran riot, to the people's misery.

manualTranslations.zh: 故民訛言「皓久死，立者何氏子」云。
manualTranslations.literal: Therefore the people spread the saying, "Hao has long been dead; the one enthroned is a son of the He clan."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Hence the rumor that "Sun Hao died long ago—the man on the throne is a He clansman."

manualTranslations.zh: 《江表傳》曰：皓以張布女為美人，有寵，皓問曰：「汝父所在？」
manualTranslations.literal: The Jiang biao zhuan states: Hao took Zhang Bu's daughter as a Beauty and favored her; Hao asked, "Where is your father?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Jiang biao zhuan says Sun Hao favored Zhang Bu's daughter as a palace lady and asked her, "Where is your father?"

manualTranslations.zh: 答曰：「賊以殺之。」
manualTranslations.literal: She answered, "The rebels killed him."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: She replied, "The rebels killed him."

manualTranslations.zh: 皓大怒，棒殺之。
manualTranslations.literal: Hao was greatly enraged and clubbed her to death.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sun Hao flew into a rage and beat her to death.

manualTranslations.zh: 後思其顏色，使巧工刻木作美人形象，恆置座側。
manualTranslations.literal: Later, thinking of her looks, he had skilled craftsmen carve wood into a likeness of the beauty and always placed it beside his seat.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Missing her face, he had artisans carve a wooden likeness and kept it at his side.

manualTranslations.zh: 問左右：「布復有女否？」
manualTranslations.literal: He asked those at hand, "Does Bu have another daughter?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He asked his attendants, "Does Zhang Bu have another daughter?"

manualTranslations.zh: 答曰：「布大女適故衛尉馮朝子純。」
manualTranslations.literal: They answered, "Bu's elder daughter is married to Chun, son of the former Commandant of the Guards Feng Chao."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: They said Zhang Bu's elder daughter had married Chun, son of former Commandant of the Guards Feng Chao.

manualTranslations.zh: 即奪純妻入宮，大有寵，拜為左夫人，晝夜與夫人房宴，不聽朝政，使尚方以金作華燧、步搖、假髻以千數。
manualTranslations.literal: He immediately seized Chun's wife into the palace, greatly favored her, appointed her Left Lady, day and night feasted with the lady in the inner chamber, did not attend to court affairs, and had the Directorate of Imperial Manufactures make gold flame-torches, step-shakers, and false coiffures by the thousands.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He seized Chun's wife for the harem, made her Left Lady, and spent day and night feasting with her while neglecting court; he ordered thousands of gold torches, step-shakers, and false coiffures from the imperial workshops.

manualTranslations.zh: 令宮人著以相撲，朝成夕敗，輒出更作，工匠因緣偷盜，府藏為空。
manualTranslations.literal: He ordered palace women to wear them in sumo contests; made in the morning and broken by evening, they were constantly replaced; craftsmen took opportunity to steal, and the treasury stores were emptied.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Palace women wore them in mock wrestling bouts that ruined them by evening, so new ones were made constantly while craftsmen stole until the treasury stood empty.

manualTranslations.zh: 會夫人死，皓哀愍思念，葬於苑中，大作塚，使工匠刻柏作木人，內塚中以為兵衛，以金銀珍玩之物送葬，不可稱計。
manualTranslations.literal: When the lady died, Hao mourned and longed for her, buried her in the park, built a great tomb, had craftsmen carve cypress into wooden men placed inside the tomb as military guards, and sent gold, silver, and precious curios to the burial beyond counting.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When she died Sun Hao mourned extravagantly, burying her in the park with a huge mound, cypress wood soldiers inside the tomb, and incalculable gold, silver, and treasures.

manualTranslations.zh: 已葬之後，皓治喪於內，半年不出。
manualTranslations.literal: After the burial, Hao observed mourning within and for half a year did not go out.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After the funeral he kept mourning seclusion for half a year without leaving the palace.

manualTranslations.zh: 國人見葬太奢麗，皆謂皓已死，所葬者是也。
manualTranslations.literal: The people of the state, seeing the burial too lavish, all said Hao was already dead and that the one buried was he.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The people, seeing the lavish funeral, decided Sun Hao was dead and someone else had been buried in his place.

manualTranslations.zh: 皓舅子何都顏狀似皓，云都代立。
manualTranslations.literal: Hao's maternal nephew He Du resembled Hao in face and form; it was said Du had replaced him on the throne.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His nephew He Du looked like Sun Hao, fueling rumors that Du had taken the throne.

manualTranslations.zh: 臨海太守奚熙信訛言，舉兵欲還誅都，都叔父植時為備海督，擊殺熙，夷三族，訛言乃息，而人心猶疑。
manualTranslations.literal: Grand Administrator of Linhai Xi Xi believed the rumor, raised troops wishing to return and execute Du; Du's uncle Zhi was at the time Coastal Defense commander, struck and killed Xi, exterminated three clans, the rumor then ceased, yet hearts still doubted.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Linhai grand administrator Xi Xi believed the rumor and marched to kill He Du; Du's uncle Zhi, coastal defense commander, defeated and killed Xi and wiped out three clans, silencing the rumor though suspicion lingered.

manualTranslations.zh: 孫皓滕夫人，故太常胤之族女也。
manualTranslations.literal: Sun Hao's Lady Teng was a clanswoman of the former Grand Master of Ceremonies Yin.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sun Hao's empress Lady Teng was a kinswoman of former Grand Master of Ceremonies Teng Yin.

manualTranslations.zh: 胤夷滅，夫人父牧，以疏遠徙邊郡。
manualTranslations.literal: When Yin was exterminated, the lady's father Mu, as a distant relation, was banished to a frontier commandery.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After Teng Yin's clan was destroyed, her father Teng Mu was exiled to a frontier commandery as a distant kinsman.

manualTranslations.zh: 孫休即位，大赦，得還，以牧為五官中郎。
manualTranslations.literal: When Sun Xiu succeeded, there was a general amnesty; he was able to return, and Mu was made Gentlemen of the Five Offices.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sun Xiu's general amnesty let him return; Teng Mu was named a Gentlemen of the Five Offices.

manualTranslations.zh: 皓既封烏程侯，聘牧女為妃。
manualTranslations.literal: After Hao was enfeoffed as Marquis of Wucheng, he betrothed Mu's daughter as consort.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Sun Hao was enfeoffed as Marquis of Wucheng, he betrothed Teng Mu's daughter.

manualTranslations.zh: 皓即位，立為皇后，封牧高密侯，拜衛將軍，錄尚書事。
manualTranslations.literal: When Hao succeeded, he established her as empress, enfeoffed Mu as Marquis of Gaomi, appointed him Guards General, and recorded Masters of Writing affairs.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At his accession he made her empress, enfeoffed Teng Mu as Marquis of Gaomi, and named him Guards General with oversight of the Secretariat.

manualTranslations.zh: 後朝士以牧尊戚，頗推令諫爭。
manualTranslations.literal: Later court gentlemen, because Mu was an honored affine, largely urged him to remonstrate.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Later courtiers, seeing Teng Mu's rank as empress kin, pressed him to remonstrate with the throne.

manualTranslations.zh: 而夫人寵漸衰，皓滋不悅，皓母何恆左右之。
manualTranslations.literal: But the lady's favor gradually declined; Hao grew ever more displeased; Hao's mother He constantly sided with her.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: As Lady Teng's favor waned Sun Hao grew angry, while his mother Lady He always sided against her.

manualTranslations.zh: 又太史言，於運歷，后不可易，皓信巫覡，故得不廢，常供養昇平宮。
manualTranslations.literal: Moreover the grand astrologer said that in the cycle of fate the empress could not be changed; Hao trusted shamans and sorcerers, therefore she was not deposed, and he regularly maintained offerings at the Palace of Shengping.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Astrologers said the empress could not be changed by fate; Sun Hao trusted diviners, so she kept her title though he maintained rites at the Palace of Shengping instead.

manualTranslations.zh: 牧見遣居蒼梧郡，雖爵位不奪，其實裔也，遂道路憂死。
manualTranslations.literal: Mu was seen off to dwell in Cangwu Commandery; although rank was not taken away, in reality he was an exile, and on the road he died of grief.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Teng Mu was sent to Cangwu; though his title remained, he was effectively exiled and died of grief on the road.

manualTranslations.zh: 長秋官僚，備員而已，受朝賀表疏如故。
manualTranslations.literal: The Long Autumn officials were names only; receiving court congratulations and memorials continued as before.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The empress's household staff existed in name only; formal congratulations still reached her as before.

manualTranslations.zh: 而皓內諸寵姬，佩皇后璽紱者多矣。
manualTranslations.literal: Yet among Hao's favored concubines within, many wore the empress's seal and ribbon.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Meanwhile many of Sun Hao's favorite concubines wore the empress's seal and sash.

manualTranslations.zh: 《江表傳》曰：皓又使黃門備行州郡，科取將吏家女。
manualTranslations.literal: The Jiang biao zhuan states: Hao also sent Yellow Gate attendants through the provinces and commanderies to levy and take daughters of generals and clerks' households.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Jiang biao zhuan adds that Sun Hao sent eunuchs through the provinces to levy daughters of officials.

manualTranslations.zh: 其二千石大臣子女，皆當歲歲言名，年十五六一簡閱，簡閱不中，乃得出嫁。
manualTranslations.literal: Daughters of ministers at the two-thousand-bushel rank all had to report their names every year; at ages fifteen or sixteen they were inspected, and only if they failed inspection could they marry out.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Ministers' daughters had to register yearly; at fifteen or sixteen they were inspected, and only those rejected could marry.

manualTranslations.zh: 后宮千數，而採擇無已。
manualTranslations.literal: The rear palace numbered in the thousands, yet selection never ceased.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The harem held thousands of women, yet the levies never stopped.

manualTranslations.zh: 天紀四年，隨皓遷於洛陽。
manualTranslations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianji, she followed Hao in removal to Luoyang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Tianji 4 she followed Sun Hao into exile at Luoyang.

sourceRange.text: 及權少年統業，夫人助治軍國，甚有補益。《會稽典錄》曰：策功曹魏騰，以迕意見譴，將殺之，士大夫憂恐，計無所出。夫人乃倚大井而謂策曰：「汝新造江南，其事未集，方當優賢禮士，舍過錄功。魏功曹在公盡規，汝今日殺之，則明日人皆叛汝。吾不忍見禍之及，當先投此井中耳。」策大驚，遽釋騰。夫人智略權譎，類皆如此。建安七年，臨薨，引見張昭等，屬以後事，合葬高陵。《志林》曰：按會稽貢舉簿，建安十二年到十三年闕，無舉者，云府君遭憂，此則吳后以十二年薨也。八年九年皆有貢舉，斯甚分明。

context.beforeSource: 銜命南行，表景為揚武將軍，領郡如故。
context.afterSource: 八年，景卒宮，子奮授兵為將，封新亭侯，卒。
context.beforeLocal: 銜命南行，表景為揚武將軍，領郡如故。
context.afterLocal: 八年，景卒宮，子奮授兵為將，封新亭侯，卒。
