manualTranslations.zh: 及權少年統業，夫人助治軍國，甚有補益。
manualTranslations.literal: When Quan in youth took sole charge of the enterprise, the lady assisted in governing army and state, with much benefit.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Sun Quan came to power while still young, Lady Wu helped him run army and state and proved a great asset.

manualTranslations.zh: 《會稽典錄》曰：策功曹魏騰，以迕意見譴，將殺之，士大夫憂恐，計無所出。
manualTranslations.literal: The Kuaiji dian lu states: Ce had credited Cao Teng of Wei for merit; because he gave offense he was reprimanded and was about to be executed; scholar-officials were anxious and fearful, with no plan to offer.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Kuaiji dian lu says Sun Ce had credited Cao Teng of Wei for service; when Teng gave offense and was condemned to death, the gentry were terrified and could see no way out.

manualTranslations.zh: 夫人乃倚大井而謂策曰：「汝新造江南，其事未集，方當優賢禮士，舍過錄功。
manualTranslations.literal: The lady then leaned against the great well and said to Ce, "You have newly built Jiangnan; the enterprise is not yet settled; you should just now honor the worthy and treat scholars with ceremony, pardon faults and record merit.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Lady Wu leaned against the great well and told Sun Ce, "You have only just begun to build Jiangnan; the work is unfinished. Now is the time to honor the worthy, treat scholars with courtesy, pardon faults, and record merit.

manualTranslations.zh: 魏功曹在公盡規，汝今日殺之，則明日人皆叛汝。
manualTranslations.literal: The Wei merit clerk has in your service fully offered remonstrance; if you kill him today, then tomorrow everyone will rebel against you.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Cao Teng has served you faithfully with honest counsel. Kill him today and tomorrow every man will turn against you.

manualTranslations.zh: 吾不忍見禍之及，當先投此井中耳。」
manualTranslations.literal: I cannot bear to see calamity reach us; I shall first throw myself into this well."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I cannot bear to see disaster fall on us—I would rather throw myself into this well first."

manualTranslations.zh: 策大驚，遽釋騰。
manualTranslations.literal: Ce was greatly alarmed and immediately released Teng.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sun Ce was shaken and released Cao Teng at once.

manualTranslations.zh: 夫人智略權譎，類皆如此。
manualTranslations.literal: The lady's wisdom, stratagem, and resourcefulness were all of this kind.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Lady Wu's shrewd counsel was often of this sort.

manualTranslations.zh: 建安七年，臨薨，引見張昭等，屬以後事，合葬高陵。
manualTranslations.literal: In the seventh year of Jian'an, as she neared death, she summoned Zhang Zhao and others, entrusted them with later affairs, and was buried together at Gaoling.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Jian'an 7, on her deathbed she summoned Zhang Zhao and others to entrust them with affairs after her death; she was buried with Sun Jian at Gaoling.

manualTranslations.zh: 《志林》曰：按會稽貢舉簿，建安十二年到十三年闕，無舉者，云府君遭憂，此則吳后以十二年薨也。
manualTranslations.literal: The Zhi lin states: According to the Kuaiji tribute-and-recommendation register, from the twelfth to the thirteenth year of Jian'an there is a gap with no recommendees; it says the prefect suffered bereavement—this shows the Wu empress died in the twelfth year.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Zhi lin notes that Kuaiji's recommendation register has no entries for Jian'an 12–13, citing the prefect's bereavement—evidence that Lady Wu died in Jian'an 12.

manualTranslations.zh: 八年九年皆有貢舉，斯甚分明。
manualTranslations.literal: The eighth and ninth years both have tribute recommendations; this is very clear.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Recommendations resume in Jian'an 8 and 9, which makes the dating plain.

sourceRange.text: 」建安四年，策遣紘奉章至許宮，留為侍御史。少府孔融等皆與親善。吳書曰：纮至，與在朝公卿及知舊述策材略絕異，平定三郡，風行草偃，加以忠敬款誠，乃心王室。時曹公為司空，欲加恩厚，以悅遠人，至乃優文褒崇，改號加封，辟纮為掾，舉高第，補侍御吏，後以纮為九江太守。纮心戀舊恩，思還反命，以疾固辭。曹公聞策薨，欲因喪伐吳。紘諫，以為乘人之喪。既非古義，若其不克，成仇棄好，不如因而厚之。曹公從其言，即表權為討虜將軍，領會稽太守。曹公欲令紘輔權內附，出紘為會稽東部都尉。《吳書》曰：權初承統，春秋方富，太夫人以方外多難，深懷憂勞，數有優令辭謝，付屬以輔助之義。纮輒拜箋答謝，思惟補察。每有異事密計及章表書記，與四方交結，常令纮與張昭草創撰作。纮以破虜有破走董卓，扶持漢室之勳；討逆平定江外，建立大業，宜有紀頌以昭公義。既成，呈權，權省讀悲感，曰：「君真識孤家門閥閱也。」乃遣纮之部。或以纮本受北任，嫌其志趣不止於此，權不以介意。初，琅邪趙昱為廣陵太守，察纮孝廉，昱後為笮融所殺，纮甚傷憤，而力不能討。昱門戶絕滅，及纮在東部，遣主簿至琅邪設祭，並求親戚為之後，以書屬琅邪相臧宣，宣以趙宗中五歲男奉昱祀，權聞而嘉之。及討江夏，以東部少事，命纮居守，遙領所職。孔融遺纮書曰：「聞大軍西征，足下留鎮。不有居者，誰守社稷？深固折衝，亦大勳也。無乃李廣之氣，倉發益怒，樂一當單于，以盡餘憤乎？南北並定，世將無事，孫叔投戈，絳、灌俎豆，亦在今日，但用離析，無緣會面，為愁嘆耳。道直途清，相見豈复難哉？」權以纮有鎮守之勞，欲論功加賞。纮厚自挹損，不敢蒙寵，權不奪其志。每從容侍燕，微言密指，常有以規諷。《江表傳》曰：初，權於群臣多呼其字，惟呼張昭曰張公，纮曰東部，所以重二人也。後權以紘為長史，從徵合肥。吳書曰：合肥城久不拔，纮進計曰：「古之圍城，開其一面，以疑眾心。今圍之甚密，攻之又急，誠懼並命戮力。死戰之寇，固難卒拔，及救未至，可小寬之，以觀其變。」議者不同。會救騎至，數至圍下，馳騁挑戰。權率輕騎將往突敵，紘諫曰：「夫兵者凶器，戰者危事也。今麾下恃盛壯之氣，忽強暴之虜，三軍之眾，莫不寒心，雖斬將搴旗，威震敵場，此乃偏將之任，非主將之宜也。願抑賁、育之勇，懷霸王之計。」權納紘言而止。既還，明年將復出軍，紘又諫曰：「自古帝王受命之君，雖有皇靈佐於上，文德播於下，亦賴武功以昭其勳。然而貴於時動，乃後為威耳。今麾下值四百之厄，有扶危之功，宜且隱息師徒，廣開播殖，任賢使能，務祟寬惠，順天命以行誅，可不勞而定也。」於是遂止不行。

context.afterSource: 紘建計宜出都秣陵，權從之。

manualTranslations.zh: 建安四年，策遣紘奉章至許宮，留為侍御史。
manualTranslations.literal: In the fourth year of Jian'an, Ce sent Hong to present a memorial at the Xu capital, where he was retained as attendant censor.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Jian'an 4 Sun Ce sent Zhang Hong to the Xu capital with a memorial; Hong was kept there as attendant censor.

manualTranslations.zh: 少府孔融等皆與親善。
manualTranslations.literal: The Privy Treasurer Kong Rong and others all treated him with intimacy.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Kong Rong, privy treasurer, and other court figures all befriended him.

manualTranslations.zh: 吳書曰：纮至，與在朝公卿及知舊述策材略絕異，平定三郡，風行草偃，加以忠敬款誠，乃心王室。
manualTranslations.literal: The Book of Wu states: When Hong arrived, with the high ministers at court and old acquaintances he described Ce's talent and strategy as utterly extraordinary, his pacification of three commanderies as making grass bow before the wind, and added that he was loyal, reverent, sincere, and true of heart to the royal house.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Book of Wu records that on reaching the capital Hong told court ministers and old friends how Sun Ce's genius had pacified three commanderies like wind flattening grass, and how his loyalty was fixed on the Han throne.

manualTranslations.zh: 時曹公為司空，欲加恩厚，以悅遠人，至乃優文褒崇，改號加封，辟纮為掾，舉高第，補侍御吏，後以纮為九江太守。
manualTranslations.literal: At that time Lord Cao was Minister of Works and wished to add favor and kindness to please distant men; he even issued fine documents of praise and ennoblement, changed titles and added fiefs, summoned Hong as an aide, nominated him for highest rank, appointed him attendant censor, and later made Hong grand warden of Jiujiang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Cao Cao, then minister of works, showered honors on distant allies: he praised Sun Ce in edicts, changed his titles, summoned Hong as an aide, ranked him at the top of the nomination list, made him attendant censor, and later offered Hong the grand wardenship of Jiujiang.

manualTranslations.zh: 纮心戀舊恩，思還反命，以疾固辭。
manualTranslations.literal: Hong's heart clung to old kindness and wished to return and report back; on grounds of illness he firmly declined.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhang Hong longed to return to Sun Ce and declined the Jiujiang post on grounds of illness.

manualTranslations.zh: 曹公聞策薨，欲因喪伐吳。
manualTranslations.literal: Lord Cao heard that Ce had died and wished to exploit the mourning to attack Wu.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Cao Cao learned of Sun Ce's death he planned to strike Wu while the court was in mourning.

manualTranslations.zh: 紘諫，以為乘人之喪。
manualTranslations.literal: Hong remonstrated, holding that it would be taking advantage of another's bereavement.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhang Hong remonstrated that attacking during mourning would be taking advantage of another's grief.

manualTranslations.zh: 既非古義，若其不克，成仇棄好，不如因而厚之。
manualTranslations.literal: It was not the ancient meaning; if it did not succeed, enmity would be made and friendship cast away—better therefore to treat them generously.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: It was not the ancient way; failure would turn friendship to enmity, so it was better to show generosity instead.

manualTranslations.zh: 曹公從其言，即表權為討虜將軍，領會稽太守。
manualTranslations.literal: Lord Cao followed his words and at once memorialized that Quan be made General Who Attacks Barbarians and act as grand warden of Kuaiji.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Cao Cao accepted the advice and memorialized Sun Quan as general who attacks barbarians and acting grand warden of Kuaiji.

manualTranslations.zh: 曹公欲令紘輔權內附，出紘為會稽東部都尉。
manualTranslations.literal: Lord Cao wished to have Hong assist Quan in submitting inwardly, and sent Hong out as commandant of the eastern division of Kuaiji.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Cao Cao meant to keep Hong near Sun Quan to encourage submission, so he posted Hong as commandant of Kuaiji's eastern division.

manualTranslations.zh: 《吳書》曰：權初承統，春秋方富，太夫人以方外多難，深懷憂勞，數有優令辭謝，付屬以輔助之義。
manualTranslations.literal: The Book of Wu states: When Quan first succeeded to the leadership, his years were still abundant; the Grand Lady, because of many difficulties abroad, deeply bore worry and toil, repeatedly issued gracious orders declining thanks, and entrusted him with the duty of assistance.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Book of Wu adds that when Sun Quan first took command, still young, his mother saw danger on every frontier and repeatedly sent gracious messages entrusting Hong with the work of steady counsel.

manualTranslations.zh: 纮輒拜箋答謝，思惟補察。
manualTranslations.literal: Hong always bowed in written reply and thanks, thinking how to supplement and examine.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhang Hong answered each message with a memorial of thanks and bent his mind to watchful counsel.

manualTranslations.zh: 每有異事密計及章表書記，與四方交結，常令纮與張昭草創撰作。
manualTranslations.literal: Whenever there were unusual affairs, secret plans, memorials, letters, or dealings with the four directions, Quan regularly had Hong and Zhang Zhao draft the compositions.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: For secret plans, memorials, and dealings with every quarter, Sun Quan regularly had Zhang Hong and Zhang Zhao draft the texts.

manualTranslations.zh: 纮以破虜有破走董卓，扶持漢室之勳；
manualTranslations.literal: Hong considered that the Slayer of the Bandit had the merit of routing Dong Zhuo and supporting the Han house;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhang Hong argued that Sun Ce, the Slayer of the Bandit, had routed Dong Zhuo and upheld the Han house—

manualTranslations.zh: 討逆平定江外，建立大業，宜有紀頌以昭公義。
manualTranslations.literal: in subduing rebels and pacifying the lands beyond the Yangzi he had established the great enterprise—there ought to be a recorded encomium to make public righteousness manifest.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: that in suppressing rebels and pacifying the lands beyond the Yangzi he had founded a great enterprise deserving a recorded encomium to proclaim public righteousness.

manualTranslations.zh: 既成，呈權，權省讀悲感，曰：「君真識孤家門閥閱也。」
manualTranslations.literal: When it was finished he presented it to Quan; Quan read it through, moved to grief, and said, "You truly know Our house's lineage and worth."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When it was finished he presented it to Sun Quan, who read it through, moved to grief, and said, "You truly know our house's lineage and worth."

manualTranslations.zh: 乃遣纮之部。
manualTranslations.literal: Thereupon he dispatched Hong to his post.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He then sent Zhang Hong to take up his command.

manualTranslations.zh: 或以纮本受北任，嫌其志趣不止於此，權不以介意。
manualTranslations.literal: Some, because Hong had originally received northern appointment, suspected his ambition extended beyond this; Quan did not mind.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Some, knowing Hong had once held office under Cao Cao, suspected his ambitions ran higher; Sun Quan paid no heed.

manualTranslations.zh: 初，琅邪趙昱為廣陵太守，察纮孝廉，昱後為笮融所殺，纮甚傷憤，而力不能討。
manualTranslations.literal: Earlier Zhao Yu of Langya was grand warden of Guangling and nominated Hong as filial and incorrupt; Yu was later killed by Ze Rong, and Hong grieved and raged deeply, but lacked the strength to punish him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Earlier Zhao Yu of Langya, grand warden of Guangling, had nominated Zhang Hong as filial and incorrupt; when Ze Rong killed Yu, Hong grieved deeply but lacked the power to avenge him.

manualTranslations.zh: 昱門戶絕滅，及纮在東部，遣主簿至琅邪設祭，並求親戚為之後，以書屬琅邪相臧宣，宣以趙宗中五歲男奉昱祀，權聞而嘉之。
manualTranslations.literal: Yu's line was extinguished; when Hong was in the eastern division he sent his chief clerk to Langya to perform sacrifices and seek a kinsman to serve as successor, writing Langya Administrator Zang Xuan; Xuan offered a five-year-old boy of the Zhao clan to maintain Yu's sacrifices, and Quan heard and praised it.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: With Yu's line extinguished, Hong from his eastern post sent his chief clerk to Langya to sacrifice and seek a kinsman to carry on the rites, writing Langya administrator Zang Xuan; Xuan appointed a five-year-old boy of the Zhao clan to maintain Yu's cult, and Sun Quan praised the act.

manualTranslations.zh: 及討江夏，以東部少事，命纮居守，遙領所職。
manualTranslations.literal: When the campaign against Jiangxia began, because the eastern division had little business, Quan ordered Hong to remain on guard while still holding his office from afar.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: During the Jiangxia campaign, with little business in the eastern division, Sun Quan left Zhang Hong to hold the rear while he still held the post in name.

manualTranslations.zh: 孔融遺纮書曰：「聞大軍西征，足下留鎮。
manualTranslations.literal: Kong Rong sent Hong a letter saying, "I hear the main army is campaigning west while you remain to hold the defense.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Kong Rong wrote Zhang Hong: "I hear the main army has marched west while you remain to hold the defense.

manualTranslations.zh: 不有居者，誰守社稷？
manualTranslations.literal: Without those who stay behind, who will guard the altars of state?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Without those who stay behind, who will guard the altars of state?

manualTranslations.zh: 深固折衝，亦大勳也。
manualTranslations.literal: Holding firm against the enemy at close quarters is also a great merit.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Standing firm against the enemy at the frontier is also a great merit.

manualTranslations.zh: 無乃李廣之氣，倉發益怒，樂一當單于，以盡餘憤乎？
manualTranslations.literal: Might it not be Li Guang's temper—suddenly bursting into greater rage, delighted to meet the Xiongnu chieftain alone and exhaust one's remaining resentment?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Or is this Li Guang's temper—suddenly flaring hotter, eager to meet the chieftain alone and spend the last of one's rage?

manualTranslations.zh: 南北並定，世將無事，孫叔投戈，絳、灌俎豆，亦在今日，但用離析，無緣會面，為愁嘆耳。
manualTranslations.literal: When north and south are both settled the age will be at peace—Sun Shu relinquished his weapons, and Jiang and Guan entered the sacrificial hall; that day too is near, but we are scattered and have no chance to meet; I can only sigh in sorrow.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When north and south are both settled the age will be at peace—Sun Shu will lay down his weapons and Jiang and Guan will take up the sacrificial vessels; that day is near, but we are scattered and cannot meet—I can only sigh.

manualTranslations.zh: 道直途清，相見豈复難哉？」
manualTranslations.literal: The road is straight and the way clear—would meeting again really be hard?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The road is straight and the way clear—would meeting again really be so hard?"

manualTranslations.zh: 權以纮有鎮守之勞，欲論功加賞。
manualTranslations.literal: Quan, because Hong had merit in holding the defense, wished to weigh his achievement and add reward.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sun Quan, crediting Zhang Hong's service in holding the rear, wished to reward him according to merit.

manualTranslations.zh: 纮厚自挹損，不敢蒙寵，權不奪其志。
manualTranslations.literal: Hong greatly restrained himself and dared not accept favor; Quan did not override his intent.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhang Hong modestly declined and would not accept honors; Sun Quan did not override his wish.

manualTranslations.zh: 每從容侍燕，微言密指，常有以規諷。
manualTranslations.literal: Whenever he attended at leisure in banquets, subtle words and secret indications often served as remonstrance and satire.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At ease in banquets he often offered subtle hints and private counsel by way of remonstrance.

manualTranslations.zh: 《江表傳》曰：初，權於群臣多呼其字，惟呼張昭曰張公，纮曰東部，所以重二人也。
manualTranslations.literal: The Jiang biao zhuan states: At first Quan among his ministers mostly called them by their courtesy names; only Zhang Zhao he called Lord Zhang, and Hong he called Eastern Division—thus honoring the two men.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Jiang biao zhuan notes that Sun Quan usually called ministers by their courtesy names, but honored Zhang Zhao as Lord Zhang and Zhang Hong as Eastern Division.

manualTranslations.zh: 後權以紘為長史，從徵合肥。
manualTranslations.literal: Later Quan made Hong chief clerk and followed him on the campaign against Hefei.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Later Sun Quan made Zhang Hong chief clerk and took him on the Hefei campaign.

manualTranslations.zh: 吳書曰：合肥城久不拔，纮進計曰：「古之圍城，開其一面，以疑眾心。
manualTranslations.literal: The Book of Wu states: Hefei city long could not be taken; Hong advanced a plan, saying, "In ancient sieges one opened a single face of the wall to sow doubt in the enemy's mind.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Book of Wu records that when Hefei long resisted capture, Zhang Hong proposed: "Ancient besiegers opened one face of a wall to sow doubt among the defenders.

manualTranslations.zh: 今圍之甚密，攻之又急，誠懼並命戮力。
manualTranslations.literal: Now the siege is very tight and the assault very pressing; I truly fear they will stake their lives together in united effort.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Now the ring is tight and the assault fierce; I fear the defenders will stake their lives together in one desperate stand.

manualTranslations.zh: 死戰之寇，固難卒拔，及救未至，可小寬之，以觀其變。」
manualTranslations.literal: A foe fighting to the death is hard to take at once; before relief arrives, one might relax the siege slightly to observe how matters shift."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: An enemy fighting to the death is hard to take quickly; before relief arrives, loosen the siege slightly and watch how matters shift."

manualTranslations.zh: 議者不同。
manualTranslations.literal: The debaters did not agree.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The council was divided.

manualTranslations.zh: 會救騎至，數至圍下，馳騁挑戰。
manualTranslations.literal: Relief cavalry arrived and repeatedly came below the siege lines, galloping to provoke battle.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Relief cavalry arrived and repeatedly rode below the walls to challenge battle.

manualTranslations.zh: 權率輕騎將往突敵，紘諫曰：「夫兵者凶器，戰者危事也。
manualTranslations.literal: Quan led light cavalry and was about to charge the enemy; Hong remonstrated, saying, "Arms are instruments of misfortune; battle is a perilous affair.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sun Quan led light cavalry to charge the enemy; Zhang Hong remonstrated: "Arms are instruments of misfortune, and battle is perilous business.

manualTranslations.zh: 今麾下恃盛壯之氣，忽強暴之虜，三軍之眾，莫不寒心，雖斬將搴旗，威震敵場，此乃偏將之任，非主將之宜也。
manualTranslations.literal: Now the men under Your command rely on overflowing vigor and rush upon fierce enemies; the whole host of the three armies, none fail to chill at heart—even if you behead generals and seize banners and your awe shakes the enemy field, this is the work of a lieutenant commander, not what the commander-in-chief should do.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Your men now rely on raw strength and rush a fierce foe; the whole army shudders. Even beheading generals and seizing banners to awe the field is a lieutenant's work, not a commander-in-chief's.

manualTranslations.zh: 願抑賁、育之勇，懷霸王之計。」
manualTranslations.literal: I beg you to restrain the valor of Ben and Yu and embrace the plan of a hegemon-king."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Restrain the raw courage of Ben and Yu, and keep to the plan of a hegemon-king."

manualTranslations.zh: 權納紘言而止。
manualTranslations.literal: Quan accepted Hong's words and stopped.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sun Quan accepted Zhang Hong's counsel and desisted.

manualTranslations.zh: 既還，明年將復出軍，紘又諫曰：「自古帝王受命之君，雖有皇靈佐於上，文德播於下，亦賴武功以昭其勳。
manualTranslations.literal: After returning, the next year he was about to lead the army out again; Hong again remonstrated, saying, "From antiquity the sovereign who receives the Mandate, though aided by imperial numen above and with civil virtue spread below, also relies on martial achievement to display his merit.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After returning, the next year he planned to campaign again; Zhang Hong remonstrated once more: "From antiquity a Mandate-bearing sovereign, though aided by Heaven above and civil virtue below, still relies on martial achievement to display merit.

manualTranslations.zh: 然而貴於時動，乃後為威耳。
manualTranslations.literal: Yet what matters is acting at the right moment; only then does might follow.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yet what matters is timing; only then does true authority follow.

manualTranslations.zh: 今麾下值四百之厄，有扶危之功，宜且隱息師徒，廣開播殖，任賢使能，務祟寬惠，順天命以行誅，可不勞而定也。」
manualTranslations.literal: Now Your command has passed through the crisis of the four hundred years and has the merit of saving the realm from peril; you ought for the time being to hide and rest the armies, broadly open land for cultivation, appoint the worthy and employ the able, devote yourself to generous kindness, and follow Heaven's mandate in punishing wrong—then you can settle matters without labor."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Your house has passed through the crisis of Han's four centuries and won the merit of saving the realm; you should rest the armies, open land for cultivation, appoint the worthy, practice generous rule, and punish wrong only as Heaven ordains—then you can settle the realm without strain."

manualTranslations.zh: 於是遂止不行。
manualTranslations.literal: Thereupon he stopped and did not go.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Thereupon he abandoned the campaign.

items.acceptedSourceText: 建安四年，策遣紘奉章至許宮，留為侍御史。少府孔融等皆與親善。吳書曰：纮至，與在朝公卿及知舊述策材略絕異，平定三郡，風行草偃，加以忠敬款誠，乃心王室。時曹公為司空，欲加恩厚，以悅遠人，至乃優文褒崇，改號加封，辟纮為掾，舉高第，補侍御吏，後以纮為九江太守。纮心戀舊恩，思還反命，以疾固辭。曹公聞策薨，欲因喪伐吳。紘諫，以為乘人之喪。既非古義，若其不克，成仇棄好，不如因而厚之。曹公從其言，即表權為討虜將軍，領會稽太守。曹公欲令紘輔權內附，出紘為會稽東部都尉。《吳書》曰：權初承統，春秋方富，太夫人以方外多難，深懷憂勞，數有優令辭謝，付屬以輔助之義。纮輒拜箋答謝，思惟補察。每有異事密計及章表書記，與四方交結，常令纮與張昭草創撰作。纮以破虜有破走董卓，扶持漢室之勳；討逆平定江外，建立大業，宜有紀頌以昭公義。既成，呈權，權省讀悲感，曰：「君真識孤家門閥閱也。」乃遣纮之部。或以纮本受北任，嫌其志趣不止於此，權不以介意。初，琅邪趙昱為廣陵太守，察纮孝廉，昱後為笮融所殺，纮甚傷憤，而力不能討。昱門戶絕滅，及纮在東部，遣主簿至琅邪設祭，並求親戚為之後，以書屬琅邪相臧宣，宣以趙宗中五歲男奉昱祀，權聞而嘉之。及討江夏，以東部少事，命纮居守，遙領所職。孔融遺纮書曰：「聞大軍西征，足下留鎮。不有居者，誰守社稷？深固折衝，亦大勳也。無乃李廣之氣，倉發益怒，樂一當單于，以盡餘憤乎？南北並定，世將無事，孫叔投戈，絳、灌俎豆，亦在今日，但用離析，無緣會面，為愁嘆耳。道直途清，相見豈复難哉？」權以纮有鎮守之勞，欲論功加賞。纮厚自挹損，不敢蒙寵，權不奪其志。每從容侍燕，微言密指，常有以規諷。《江表傳》曰：初，權於群臣多呼其字，惟呼張昭曰張公，纮曰東部，所以重二人也。後權以紘為長史，從徵合肥。吳書曰：合肥城久不拔，纮進計曰：「古之圍城，開其一面，以疑眾心。今圍之甚密，攻之又急，誠懼並命戮力。死戰之寇，固難卒拔，及救未至，可小寬之，以觀其變。」議者不同。會救騎至，數至圍下，馳騁挑戰。權率輕騎將往突敵，紘諫曰：「夫兵者凶器，戰者危事也。今麾下恃盛壯之氣，忽強暴之虜，三軍之眾，莫不寒心，雖斬將搴旗，威震敵場，此乃偏將之任，非主將之宜也。願抑賁、育之勇，懷霸王之計。」權納紘言而止。既還，明年將復出軍，紘又諫曰：「自古帝王受命之君，雖有皇靈佐於上，文德播於下，亦賴武功以昭其勳。然而貴於時動，乃後為威耳。今麾下值四百之厄，有扶危之功，宜且隱息師徒，廣開播殖，任賢使能，務祟寬惠，順天命以行誅，可不勞而定也。」於是遂止不行。

manualTranslations.literal: Xu's younger brother Ying, courtesy name Daoyan, at first served as palace writer in the secret repository; when Sun Xiu ascended the throne he became attendant palace censor of the scattered cavalry.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Xue Xu's younger brother Ying, styled Daoyan, first served as palace writer in the secret repository; when Sun Xiu ascended the throne he became attendant palace censor of the scattered cavalry.

manualTranslations.zh: 數年，以病去官。
manualTranslations.literal: After several years he left office on grounds of illness.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After several years he left office on grounds of illness.

manualTranslations.zh: 孫皓初，為左執法，遷選曹尚書，及立太子，又領少傅。

manualTranslations.zh: 瑩獻詩曰：惟臣之先，昔仕於漢，奕世綿綿，頗涉臺觀。

manualTranslations.idiomatic: Ying presented a poem opening: "My forebears once served Han; generation after generation without end, they rose into the palace bureaucracy."

sourceRange.text: 闞澤字德潤，會稽山陰人也。家世農夫，至澤好學，居貧無資，常為人傭書，以供紙筆，所寫既畢，誦讀亦遍。追師論講，究覽群籍，兼通歷數，由是顯名。察孝廉，除錢唐長，遷郴令。孫權為驃騎將軍，辟補西曹掾；及稱尊號，以澤為尚書。嘉禾中，為中書令，加待中。赤烏五年，拜太子太傅，領中書如故。澤以經傳文多，難得盡用，乃斟酌諸家，刊約《禮》文及諸注說以授二宮，為制行出入及見賓儀，又著《乾象歷注》以正時日。每朝廷大議，經典所疑，輒諮訪之。以儒學勤勞，封都鄉侯。性謙恭篤慎，宮府小吏，呼召對問，皆為抗禮。人有非短，口未嘗及，容貌似不足者，然所聞少窮。權常問：「書傳篇賦，何者為美？」釋欲諷喻以明治亂，因對賈誼《過秦論》最善，權覽讀焉。初，以呂壹姦罪發聞，有司窮治，奏以大辟，或以為宜加焚裂，用彰元惡。權以訪澤，澤曰：「盛明之世，不宜復有此刑。」權從之。又諸官司有所患疾，欲增重科防，以檢禦臣下，澤每曰：「宜依禮、律」，其和而有正，皆此類也。吳錄曰：虜翻稱澤曰：「闞生矯傑，蓋蜀之揚雄。」又曰：「闞子儒術德行，亦今之仲舒也。」初，魏文帝即位，權嘗從容問群臣曰：「曹丕以盛年即位，恐孤不能及之，諸卿以為如何？」群臣未對，澤曰：「不及十年，丕其沒矣，大王勿憂也。」權曰：「何以知之？」澤曰：「以字言之，不十為丕，此其數也。」文帝果七年而崩。臣松之計孫權年大文帝五歲，其為長幼也微矣。六年冬卒，權痛惜感悼，食不進者數日。澤州裡先輩丹楊唐固亦修身積學，稱為儒者，著《國語》《公羊》《轂梁傳》注，講授常數十人。權為吳王，拜固儀郎，自陸遜、張溫、駱統等皆拜之。黃武四年尚書僕射，卒。吳錄曰：固字子正，卒時年七十餘矣。

manualTranslations.zh: 闞澤字德潤，會稽山陰人也。
manualTranslations.literal: Kan Ze, courtesy name Derun, was a man of Shanyin in Kuaiji.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Kan Ze, styled Derun, came from Shanyin in Kuaiji.

manualTranslations.zh: 家世農夫，至澤好學，居貧無資，常為人傭書，以供紙筆，所寫既畢，誦讀亦遍。
manualTranslations.literal: His family for generations were farmers; when it came to Ze he loved learning, lived in poverty without resources, and often copied texts for others to supply paper and brush; when the copying was finished he had also read through it all.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His family had been farmers for generations; Ze loved learning but lived in poverty and often copied texts for others to pay for paper and brush, reading each work through as he finished copying it.

manualTranslations.zh: 追師論講，究覽群籍，兼通歷數，由是顯名。
manualTranslations.literal: He pursued teachers for discussion and exposition, exhaustively perused the corpus of books, and also mastered calendrical reckoning; thereby he became famous.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He sought out teachers for debate, mastered the classics, and also learned calendrical science, winning fame thereby.

manualTranslations.zh: 察孝廉，除錢唐長，遷郴令。
manualTranslations.literal: Nominated filial and incorrupt, he was appointed magistrate of Qiantang and transferred to chief of Chen county.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Nominated filial and incorrupt, he was appointed magistrate of Qiantang and later chief of Chen county.

manualTranslations.zh: 孫權為驃騎將軍，辟補西曹掾；
manualTranslations.literal: When Sun Quan was General Who Spurs the Cavalry, Ze was summoned and appointed aide in the western bureau;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Sun Quan was general who spurs the cavalry, Ze was summoned as an aide in the western bureau;

manualTranslations.zh: 及稱尊號，以澤為尚書。
manualTranslations.literal: when Quan assumed the imperial title, Ze was made palace writer.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: and when Quan assumed the imperial title, Ze was made palace writer.

manualTranslations.zh: 嘉禾中，為中書令，加待中。
manualTranslations.literal: In the Jiahe era he became director of the palace secretariat and was additionally made palace attendant.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the Jiahe era he became director of the palace secretariat and was additionally made palace attendant.

manualTranslations.zh: 赤烏五年，拜太子太傅，領中書如故。
manualTranslations.literal: In the fifth year of Chiwu he was appointed grand tutor to the heir and continued to hold the secretariat as before.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Chiwu 5 he was appointed grand tutor to the heir while continuing to head the secretariat.

manualTranslations.zh: 澤以經傳文多，難得盡用，乃斟酌諸家，刊約《禮》文及諸注說以授二宮，為制行出入及見賓儀，又著《乾象歷注》以正時日。
manualTranslations.literal: Ze, because the classical texts were many and hard to use in full, weighed the various schools, edited and condensed the Ritual texts and commentaries to instruct the two palaces, established rules for going in and out and for receiving guests, and also composed Commentaries on the Qianxiang Calendar to rectify days and months.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Because the classics were too vast for daily use, Ze distilled the Ritual texts and major commentaries for the two palaces, set rules for court movement and receiving guests, and wrote Commentaries on the Qianxiang Calendar to fix the calendar.

manualTranslations.zh: 每朝廷大議，經典所疑，輒諮訪之。
manualTranslations.literal: Whenever the court held great deliberations and the classics raised doubts, Quan at once consulted him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Whenever the court debated doubts in the classics, Sun Quan consulted him at once.

manualTranslations.zh: 以儒學勤勞，封都鄉侯。
manualTranslations.literal: For scholarly labor he was enfeoffed as marquis of Duxiang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: For scholarly service he was enfeoffed as marquis of Duxiang.

manualTranslations.zh: 性謙恭篤慎，宮府小吏，呼召對問，皆為抗禮。
manualTranslations.literal: By nature humble, respectful, and deeply cautious, when palace and office petty clerks were summoned for questioning he treated them all with ceremony due equals.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Humble and deeply cautious by nature, he treated even petty palace clerks summoned for questioning with the courtesy due equals.

manualTranslations.zh: 人有非短，口未嘗及，容貌似不足者，然所聞少窮。
manualTranslations.literal: When others had faults he never spoke of them; his bearing seemed insufficient, yet what he heard was seldom exhausted.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He never spoke of others' faults; his manner seemed unassuming, yet his learning was seldom exhausted.

manualTranslations.zh: 權常問：「書傳篇賦，何者為美？」
manualTranslations.literal: Quan often asked, "Among books, documents, essays, and rhapsodies, which is finest?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sun Quan often asked, "Among books, essays, and rhapsodies, which is finest?"

manualTranslations.zh: 釋欲諷喻以明治亂，因對賈誼《過秦論》最善，權覽讀焉。
manualTranslations.literal: Ze wished to admonish by allegory to clarify order and disorder, and therefore answered that Jia Yi's "On the Qin" was best; Quan read it through.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Ze wished to admonish by allegory on order and disorder and answered that Jia Yi's "On the Qin" was best; Sun Quan read it through.

manualTranslations.zh: 初，以呂壹姦罪發聞，有司窮治，奏以大辟，或以為宜加焚裂，用彰元惡。
manualTranslations.literal: At first, when Lü Yi's crimes of treachery came to light, the officials investigated to the end and memorialized capital punishment; some thought dismemberment by burning should be added to display the chief evil.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Lü Yi's treachery came to light, the officials investigated thoroughly and memorialized capital punishment; some urged burning and dismemberment to expose the chief evil.

manualTranslations.zh: 權以訪澤，澤曰：「盛明之世，不宜復有此刑。」
manualTranslations.literal: Quan consulted Ze; Ze said, "In an age of glorious enlightenment such a punishment ought not be revived."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sun Quan consulted Kan Ze, who said, "In an enlightened age such a punishment ought not be revived."

manualTranslations.zh: 權從之。
manualTranslations.literal: Quan followed this.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sun Quan agreed.

manualTranslations.zh: 又諸官司有所患疾，欲增重科防，以檢禦臣下，澤每曰：「宜依禮、律」，其和而有正，皆此類也。
manualTranslations.literal: Also when various offices had concerns and wished to increase punishments and guard against officials, Ze always said, "One ought to follow the Rituals and the Code"; his harmonizing yet upright conduct was all of this kind.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When offices wished to tighten punishments to control officials, Ze always said, "Follow the Rituals and the Code"; his harmonizing yet principled counsel was always of this kind.

manualTranslations.zh: 吳錄曰：虜翻稱澤曰：「闞生矯傑，蓋蜀之揚雄。」
manualTranslations.literal: The Wu lu states: Lu Fan praised Ze, saying, "Master Kan is lofty and outstanding—surely Shu has its Yang Xiong in him."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Wu lu records that Lu Fan praised Ze: "Master Kan is lofty and outstanding—Wu has its Yang Xiong in him."

manualTranslations.zh: 又曰：「闞子儒術德行，亦今之仲舒也。」
manualTranslations.literal: He also said, "Master Kan's Confucian learning and virtue make him today's Dong Zhongshu."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He also said, "Master Kan's Confucian learning and virtue make him today's Dong Zhongshu."

manualTranslations.zh: 初，魏文帝即位，權嘗從容問群臣曰：「曹丕以盛年即位，恐孤不能及之，諸卿以為如何？」
manualTranslations.literal: At first, when Wei Emperor Wen ascended the throne, Quan once at leisure asked his ministers, "Cao Pi took the throne in his prime; I fear I cannot match him—what do you all think?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Wei Emperor Wen ascended the throne, Sun Quan once asked his ministers at leisure, "Cao Pi took the throne in his prime; I fear I cannot match him—what do you think?"

manualTranslations.zh: 群臣未對，澤曰：「不及十年，丕其沒矣，大王勿憂也。」
manualTranslations.literal: The ministers had not answered when Ze said, "In less than ten years Pi will be gone; Great King, do not worry."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Before the ministers answered, Ze said, "In less than ten years Pi will be gone; Great King, do not worry."

manualTranslations.zh: 權曰：「何以知之？」
manualTranslations.literal: Quan said, "How do you know this?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sun Quan asked, "How do you know?"

manualTranslations.zh: 澤曰：「以字言之，不十為丕，此其數也。」
manualTranslations.literal: Ze said, "Speaking of the written name, 'not ten' makes Pi—such is the number."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Ze said, "By the written name, 'not ten' makes the character for Pi—that is the number."

manualTranslations.zh: 文帝果七年而崩。
manualTranslations.literal: Emperor Wen indeed died after seven years.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen indeed died after seven years.

manualTranslations.zh: 臣松之計孫權年大文帝五歲，其為長幼也微矣。
manualTranslations.literal: Your servant Songzhi calculates that Sun Quan was five years older than Emperor Wen—their seniority was slight indeed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi notes that Sun Quan was only five years older than Emperor Wen—their ages were scarcely different.

manualTranslations.zh: 六年冬卒，權痛惜感悼，食不進者數日。
manualTranslations.literal: In the winter of the sixth year he died; Quan grieved and mourned deeply and for several days ate nothing.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He died in the winter of the sixth year; Sun Quan grieved deeply and for several days ate nothing.

manualTranslations.zh: 澤州裡先輩丹楊唐固亦修身積學，稱為儒者，著《國語》《公羊》《轂梁傳》注，講授常數十人。
manualTranslations.literal: A senior of Ze's district, Tang Gu of Danyang, also cultivated himself and amassed learning, was styled a Confucian, composed commentaries on the Discourses of the States, the Gongyang, and Guliang Commentary, and regularly lectured to several dozen men.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: A senior of Ze's district, Tang Gu of Danyang, also cultivated himself and amassed learning, was styled a Confucian, wrote commentaries on the Discourses of the States, the Gongyang, and Guliang texts, and regularly taught several dozen pupils.

manualTranslations.zh: 權為吳王，拜固儀郎，自陸遜、張溫、駱統等皆拜之。
manualTranslations.literal: When Quan was King of Wu he appointed Gu gentleman for ceremony; from Lu Xun, Zhang Wen, Luo Tong, and others down, all bowed to him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Sun Quan was king of Wu he appointed Tang Gu gentleman for ceremony; Lu Xun, Zhang Wen, Luo Tong, and others all bowed to him.

manualTranslations.zh: 黃武四年尚書僕射，卒。
manualTranslations.literal: In the fourth year of Huangwu he served as vice director of the masters of writing and died.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Huangwu 4 he served as vice director of the masters of writing and died.

manualTranslations.zh: 吳錄曰：固字子正，卒時年七十餘矣。
manualTranslations.literal: The Wu lu states: Gu's courtesy name was Zizheng; at death he was past seventy.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Wu lu adds that Tang Gu, styled Zizheng, was past seventy at his death.

items.acceptedSourceText: 闞澤字德潤，會稽山陰人也。家世農夫，至澤好學，居貧無資，常為人傭書，以供紙筆，所寫既畢，誦讀亦遍。追師論講，究覽群籍，兼通歷數，由是顯名。察孝廉，除錢唐長，遷郴令。孫權為驃騎將軍，辟補西曹掾；及稱尊號，以澤為尚書。嘉禾中，為中書令，加待中。赤烏五年，拜太子太傅，領中書如故。澤以經傳文多，難得盡用，乃斟酌諸家，刊約《禮》文及諸注說以授二宮，為制行出入及見賓儀，又著《乾象歷注》以正時日。每朝廷大議，經典所疑，輒諮訪之。以儒學勤勞，封都鄉侯。性謙恭篤慎，宮府小吏，呼召對問，皆為抗禮。人有非短，口未嘗及，容貌似不足者，然所聞少窮。權常問：「書傳篇賦，何者為美？」釋欲諷喻以明治亂，因對賈誼《過秦論》最善，權覽讀焉。初，以呂壹姦罪發聞，有司窮治，奏以大辟，或以為宜加焚裂，用彰元惡。權以訪澤，澤曰：「盛明之世，不宜復有此刑。」權從之。又諸官司有所患疾，欲增重科防，以檢禦臣下，澤每曰：「宜依禮、律」，其和而有正，皆此類也。吳錄曰：虜翻稱澤曰：「闞生矯傑，蓋蜀之揚雄。」又曰：「闞子儒術德行，亦今之仲舒也。」初，魏文帝即位，權嘗從容問群臣曰：「曹丕以盛年即位，恐孤不能及之，諸卿以為如何？」群臣未對，澤曰：「不及十年，丕其沒矣，大王勿憂也。」權曰：「何以知之？」澤曰：「以字言之，不十為丕，此其數也。」文帝果七年而崩。臣松之計孫權年大文帝五歲，其為長幼也微矣。六年冬卒，權痛惜感悼，食不進者數日。澤州裡先輩丹楊唐固亦修身積學，稱為儒者，著《國語》《公羊》《轂梁傳》注，講授常數十人。權為吳王，拜固儀郎，自陸遜、張溫、駱統等皆拜之。黃武四年尚書僕射，卒。吳錄曰：固字子正，卒時年七十餘矣。

sourceRange.text: 〈孫氏異同評曰：〔魏書〕及《江表傳》云，然以景初元年、正始二年241年再出為寇，所破胡質、蒲忠在景初元年。魏志承魏書，依違不說質等為然所破，而直云然退耳。吳志說赤烏五年，於魏為正始三年242年，魏將蒲忠與朱然戰，忠不利，質等皆退。按魏少帝紀及孫權傳，是歲並無事，當是陳壽誤以吳嘉禾六年為赤烏五年耳。

localRange.text: 〈孙氏异同评曰：魏书及江表传云然以景初元年、正始二年再出为寇，所破胡质、蒲忠在景初元年。魏志承魏书，依违不说质等为然所破，而直云然退耳。吴志说赤乌五年，於魏为正始三年，魏将蒲忠与硃然战，忠不利，质等皆退。按魏少帝纪及孙权传，是岁并无事，当是陈寿误以吴嘉禾六年为赤乌五年耳。

sourceRange.text: 黃武元年，劉備率大眾來向西界，權命遜為大都督、假節，督朱然、潘璋、宋謙、韓當、徐盛、鮮于丹、孫桓等五萬人拒之。備從巫峽、建平連圍至夷陵界，立數十屯，以金錦爵賞誘動諸夷，使將軍馮習為大督，張南為前部，輔匡，趙融、廖淳、傅肜等各為別督，先遣吳班將數千人於平地立營，欲以挑戰。諸將皆欲擊之，遜曰：「此必有譎，且觀之。」吴书曰：诸将并欲迎击备，逊以为不可，曰：「备举军东下，锐气始盛，且乘高守险，难可卒攻，攻之纵下，犹难尽克，若有不利，损我大势，非小故也。今但且奖厉将士，广施方略，以观其变。若此间是平原旷野，当恐有颠沛交驰之忧，今缘山行军，势不得展，自当罢於木石之间，徐制其弊耳。」诸将不解，以为逊畏之，各怀愤恨。備知其計不可，乃引伏兵八千，從谷中出。遜曰：「所以不聽諸君擊班者，揣之必有巧故也。」遜上疏曰：夷陵要害，國之關限，雖為易得，亦復易失。

sourceRange.text: 黃龍元年229年，拜上大將軍、右都護。是歲，權東巡建業，留太子，皇子及尚書九官，征遜輔太子，並掌荊州及豫章三郡事，董督軍國。時建昌侯慮於堂前作斗鴨欄，頗施小巧。遜正色曰：「君候宜勤覽經典以自新益，用此何為？」慮即時毀徹之。射聲校尉松於公子中最親，戲兵不整，遜對之髡其職吏。南陽謝景善劉廙先刑後禮之論，遜呵景曰：「禮之長於刑久矣，廙以細辯而詭先聖之教，皆非也。君今侍東宮，宜遵仁義以彰德音，若彼之談，不須講也。」遜雖身在外，乃心於國。上疏陳時事曰：臣以為科法嚴峻，下犯者多。

sourceRange.text: 鳳皇元年，西陵督步闡據城以叛，遣使降晉。抗聞之，日部分諸軍，令將軍左奕、吾彥、蔡貢等徑赴西陵。敕軍營更築嚴圍，自赤谿至故市，內以圍闡，外以禦寇，晝夜催切，如敵以至，眾甚苦之。諸將咸諫曰：「今及三軍之銳，亟以攻闡，比晉救至，闡必可拔。何事於圍，而以弊士民之力乎？」抗曰：「此城處勢既固，糧谷又足，且所繕修備御之具，皆抗所宿規。今反身攻之，既非可卒克，且北救必至，至而無備，表裡受難，何以御之？」諸將咸欲攻闡，抗每不許。宜都太守雷譚言至懇切，抗欲服眾，聽令一攻。攻果無利，圍備始合。晉車騎將軍羊祜率師向江陵，諸將咸以抗不宜上。抗曰：「江陵城固兵足，無所憂患。假令敵沒江陵，必不能守，所損者小。如使西陵槃結，則南山群夷皆當擾動，則所憂慮，難可而竟也。吾寧棄江陵而赴西陵，況江陵牢固乎？」初，江陵平衍，道路通利，抗敕江陵督張咸作大堰遏水，漸漬平中，以絕寇叛。祜欲因所遏水，浮船運糧，揚聲將破堰以通步軍。抗聞，使咸亟破之。諸將皆惑，屢諫不聽。祜至當陽。聞堰敗，乃改船以車運，大費損功力。

sourceRange.text: 恪上牋諫曰：「」奮得牋懼，遂移南昌，游獵彌甚，官屬不堪命。

localRange.text: 恪上牋諫曰：「帝王之尊，與天同位，是以家天下，臣父兄，四海之內，皆爲臣妾。仇讎有善，不得不舉，親戚有惡，不得不誅，所以承天理物，先國後身，蓋聖人立制，百代不易之道也。昔漢初興，多王子弟至於太彊，輒爲不軌，上則幾危社稷，下則骨肉相殘，其後懲戒，以爲大諱。自光武以來，諸王有制，惟得自娛於宮內，不得臨民，干與政事，其與交通，皆有重禁，遂以全安，各保福祚。此則前世得失之驗也。近袁紹、劉表各有國土，土地非狹，人衆非弱，以適庶不分，遂滅其宗祀。此乃天下愚智，所共嗟痛。大行皇帝覽古戒今，防芽遏萌，慮於千載。是以寢疾之日，分遣諸王，各早就國，詔策殷勤，科禁嚴峻，其所戒勑，無所不至，誠欲上安宗廟，下全諸王，使百世相承，無凶國害家之悔也。大王宜上惟太伯順父之志，中念河間獻王、東海王彊恭敬之節，下當裁抑驕恣荒亂以爲警戒。而聞頃至武昌以來，多違詔勑，不拘制度，擅發諸將兵治護宮室。又左右常從有罪過者，當以表聞，公付有司，而擅私殺，事不明白。大司馬呂岱親受先帝詔勑，輔導大王，旣不承用其言，令懷憂怖。華錡先帝近臣，忠良正直，其所陳道，當納用之，而聞怒錡，有收縛之語。又中書楊融，親受詔勑，所當恭肅，云『正自不聽禁，當如我何』？聞此之日，大小驚怪，莫不寒心。里語曰：『明鏡所以照形，古事所以知今。大王宜深以魯王爲戒，改易其行，戰戰兢兢，盡敬朝廷，如此則無求不得。若棄忘先帝法教，懷輕慢之心，臣下寧負大王，不敢負先帝遺詔，寧爲大王所怨疾，豈敢忘尊主之威，而令詔勑不行於藩臣邪？此古今正義，大王所照知也。夫福來有由，禍來有漸，漸生不憂，將不可悔。向使魯王早納忠直之言，懷驚懼之慮，享祚無窮，豈有滅亡之禍哉？夫良藥苦口，惟疾者能甘之。忠言逆耳，惟達者能受之。今者恪等慺慺欲爲大王除危殆於萌芽，廣福慶之基原，是以不自知言至，願蒙三思。奮得牋懼，遂移南昌，游獵彌甚，官屬不堪命。

sourceRange.text: 霸二子，基、壹。五鳳中，封基爲吳侯，壹宛陵侯。基侍孫亮在內，太平二年257年，盜乘御馬，收付獄。亮問侍中刁玄曰：「盜乘御馬罪云何？」玄對曰：「科應死。然魯王早終，惟陛下哀原之。」亮曰：「法者，天下所共，何得阿以親親故邪？當思惟可以釋此者，柰何以情相迫乎？」玄曰：「舊赦有大小，或天下，亦有千里、五百里赦，隨意所及。」亮曰：「解人不當爾邪！」乃赦宮中，基以得免。孫皓即位，追和、霸舊隙，削基、壹爵土，與祖母謝姬俱徙會稽烏傷縣。

context.beforeSource: 霸賜死後，又誅寄、安、奇等，咸以黨霸搆和故也。
context.afterSource: 孫奮字子揚，霸弟也，母曰仲姬。

manualTranslations.zh: 基侍孫亮在內，太平二年257年，盜乘御馬，收付獄。
manualTranslations.literal: Ji attended Sun Liang within the inner palace; in the second year of Taiping (257) he stole and rode an imperial horse and was taken into custody.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Ji served Sun Liang in the inner palace. In 257 (the second year of Taiping) he stole and rode an imperial horse and was imprisoned.

manualTranslations.zh: 亮問侍中刁玄曰：「盜乘御馬罪云何？」
manualTranslations.literal: Liang asked Attendant-in-Ordinary Diao Xuan, saying: "What is the penalty for stealing and riding an imperial horse?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sun Liang asked Attendant-in-Ordinary Diao Xuan, "What is the penalty for stealing and riding an imperial horse?"

manualTranslations.zh: 玄對曰：「科應死。
manualTranslations.literal: Xuan replied, saying: "By statute the penalty is death.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Diao Xuan replied, "By statute the penalty is death.

manualTranslations.zh: 然魯王早終，惟陛下哀原之。」
manualTranslations.literal: Yet the Prince of Lu died young; I beg Your Majesty to show pity and pardon him."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yet the Prince of Lu died young; I beg Your Majesty to show pity and pardon him."

manualTranslations.zh: 亮曰：「法者，天下所共，何得阿以親親故邪？
manualTranslations.literal: Liang said: "Law is what all under Heaven share; how can one show favoritism because of kinship?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sun Liang said, "Law belongs to all under Heaven—how can one show favoritism because of kinship?

manualTranslations.zh: 當思惟可以釋此者，柰何以情相迫乎？」
manualTranslations.literal: One ought to think of what could release this case—why press me with personal sentiment?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: One ought to think of what could release him—why press me with personal sentiment?"

manualTranslations.zh: 玄曰：「舊赦有大小，或天下，亦有千里、五百里赦，隨意所及。」
manualTranslations.literal: Xuan said: "Amnesties of old came in great and small forms—sometimes for all the realm, sometimes for a radius of a thousand or five hundred li, according to what the sovereign wished to reach."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Diao Xuan said, "Amnesties of old came in great and small forms—sometimes for the whole realm, sometimes for a radius of a thousand or five hundred li, as far as the sovereign wished to extend mercy."

manualTranslations.zh: 亮曰：「解人不當爾邪！」
manualTranslations.literal: Liang said: "Should not someone who understands matters act thus!"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sun Liang said, "Should not someone who understands matters act thus!"

manualTranslations.zh: 乃赦宮中，基以得免。
manualTranslations.literal: Thereupon he proclaimed an amnesty within the palace, and Ji thereby escaped punishment.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He then proclaimed an amnesty within the palace, and Ji was spared.

manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Sun Hao succeeded, he revived the old feud between Sun He and Sun Ba, stripped Ji and Yi of their titles and fiefs, and exiled them with their grandmother Lady Xie to Wushang in Kuaiji.

localRange.text: 臨終，上疏曰：「臣以無狀，嬰抱篤疾，自省微劣，懼卒隕斃。臣不自惜，念當委離供養，埋胔后土，長不復奉望宮省，朝覲日月，生無益於國，死貽陛下重慼，以此爲哽結耳。臣聞死生有命，長短自天，周晉、顏回有上智之才，而尚夭折，況臣愚陋，年過其壽，生爲國嗣，沒享榮祚，於臣已多，亦何悲恨哉！方今大事未定，逋寇未討，萬國喁喁，係命陛下，危者望安，亂者仰治。願陛下棄忘臣身，割下流之恩，脩黃老之術，篤養神光，加羞珍膳，廣開神明之慮，以定無窮之業，則率土幸賴，臣死無恨也。皇子和仁孝聦哲，德行清茂，宜早建置，以繫民望。諸葛恪才略博達，器任佐時。張休、顧譚、謝景，皆通敏有識斷，入宜委腹心，出可爲爪牙。范慎、華融矯矯壯節，有國士之風。羊衜辯捷，有專對之材。刁玄優弘，志履道真。裴欽博記，翰采足用。蔣脩、虞翻，志節分明。凡此諸臣，或宜廊廟，或任將帥，皆練時事，明習法令，守信固義，有不可奪之志。此皆陛下日月所照，選置臣宮，得與從事，備知情素，敢以陳聞。臣重惟當今方外多虞，師旅未休，當厲六軍，以圖進取。軍以人爲衆，衆以財爲寶，竊聞郡縣頗有荒殘，民物凋弊，姦亂萌生，是以法令繁滋，刑辟重切。臣聞爲政聽民，律令與時推移，誠宜與將相大臣詳擇時宜，博采衆議，寬刑輕賦，均息力役，以順民望。陸遜忠勤於時，出身憂國，謇謇在公，有匪躬之節。諸葛瑾、步隲、朱然、全琮、朱據、呂岱、吾粲、闞澤、嚴畯、張承、孫怡忠於爲國，通達治體。可令陳上便宜，蠲除苛煩，愛養士馬，撫循百姓。五年之外，十年之內，遠者歸復，近者盡力，兵不血刃，而大事可定也。臣聞『鳥之將死其鳴也哀，人之將死其言也善』，故子囊臨終，遺言戒時，君子以爲忠，豈況臣登，其能已乎？願陛下留意聽采，臣雖死之日，猶生之年也。旣絕而後書聞，權益以摧感，言則隕涕。是歲，赤烏四年也。

sourceRange.text: 督軍使者羊衜上疏曰：「」時全寄、吳安、孫奇、楊笁等陰共附霸，圖危太子。

localRange.text: 督軍使者羊衜上疏曰：「臣聞古之有天下者，皆先顯別適庶，封建子弟，所以尊重祖宗，爲國藩表也。二宮拜授，海內稱宜，斯乃大吳興隆之基。頃聞二宮並絕賔客，遠近悚然，大小失望。竊從下風，聽採衆論，咸謂二宮智達英茂，自正名建號，於今三年，德行內著，美稱外昭，西北二隅，乆所服聞。謂陛下當副順遐邇所以歸德，勤命二宮賔延四遠，使異國聞聲，思爲臣妾。今旣未垂意於此，而發明詔，省奪備衞，抑絕賔客，使四方禮敬，不復得通，雖實陛下敦尚古義，欲令二宮專志於學，不復顧慮觀聽小宜，期於溫故博物而已，然非臣下傾企喁喁之至願也。或謂二宮不遵典式，此臣所以寢息不寧。就如所嫌，猶宜補察，密加斟酌，不使遠近得容異言。臣懼積疑成謗，乆將宣流，而西北二隅，去國不遠，異同之語，易以聞達。聞達之日，聲論當興，將謂二宮有不順之愆，不審陛下何以解之？若無以解異國，則亦無以釋境內。境內守疑，異國興謗，非所以育巍巍，鎮社稷也。願陛下早發優詔，使二宮周旋禮命如初，則天清地晏，萬國幸甚矣。時全寄、吳安、孫奇、楊笁等陰共附霸，圖危太子。

sourceRange.text: 乆之，尚書僕射存上疏曰：「」權乃許之，於是假節開府，治半州。《吳書》載權詔曰：「」慮以皇子之尊，富於春秋，遠近嫌其不能留意。

localRange.text: 乆之，尚書僕射存上疏曰：「帝王之興，莫不襃崇至親，以光羣后，故魯衞於周，寵冠諸侯，高帝五王，封列于漢，所以藩屏本朝，爲國鎮衞。建昌侯慮稟性聦敏，才兼文武，於古典制，宜正名號。陛下謙光，未肯如舊，羣寮大小，咸用於邑。方今姦寇恣睢，金鼓未弭，腹心爪牙，惟親與賢。輒與丞相雍等議，咸以慮宜爲鎮軍大將軍，授任偏方，以光大業。權乃許之，於是假節開府，治半州。〈《吳書》載權詔曰：「期運擾亂，凶邪肆虐，威罰有序，干戈不戢。以慮氣志休懿，武略夙昭，必能爲國佐定大業，故授以上將之位，至以殊特之榮，寵以兵馬之勢，委以偏方之任。外欲威振敵虜，厭難萬里，內欲鎮撫遠近，慰卹將士，誠慮建功立事竭命之秋也。慮其內脩文德，外經武訓，持盈若沖，則滿而不溢。敬慎乃心，無忝所受。慮以皇子之尊，富於春秋，遠近嫌其不能留意。

sourceRange.text: 太元二年252年正月，封和爲南陽王，遣之長沙。《吳書》曰：和之長沙，行過蕪湖，有鵲巢于帆檣，故官寮聞之皆憂慘，以爲檣末傾危，非乆安之象。或言鵲巢之詩有「積行累功以致爵位」之言，今王至德茂行，復受國土，儻神靈以此告寤人意乎？四月，權薨，諸葛恪秉政。恪即和妃張之舅也。妃使黃門陳遷之建業上疏中宮，并致問於恪。臨去，恪謂遷曰：「爲我達妃，期當使勝他人。」此言頗泄。又恪有徙都意，使治武昌宮，民間或言欲迎和。及恪被誅，孫峻因此奪和璽綬，徙新都，又遣使者賜死。和與妃張辭別，張曰：「吉凶當相隨，終不獨生活也。」亦自殺，舉邦傷焉。

context.beforeSource: 《吳書》曰：權寢疾，意頗感寤，欲徵和還立之，全公主及孫峻、孫弘等固爭之，乃止。

manualTranslations.zh: 太元二年252年正月，封和爲南陽王，遣之長沙。
manualTranslations.literal: In the first month of the second year of Taiyuan (252), He was enfeoffed as Prince of Nanyang and sent to Changsha.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the first month of 252 (the second year of Taiyuan), Sun He was made Prince of Nanyang and sent to Changsha.

manualTranslations.zh: 《吳書》曰：和之長沙，行過蕪湖，有鵲巢于帆檣，故官寮聞之皆憂慘，以爲檣末傾危，非乆安之象。
manualTranslations.literal: The Wu shu states: On He's road to Changsha he passed Wuhu, and a magpie nested on the sail mast; when his former retainers heard of it they were all distressed, taking it as a sign that the mast's tip was tipping and not an omen of lasting peace.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Wu shu says that on the way to Changsha Sun He passed Wuhu, where a magpie nested on the sail mast. His former retainers were all distressed, taking it as a sign that the mast's tip was tipping and not an omen of lasting peace.

manualTranslations.zh: 或言鵲巢之詩有「積行累功以致爵位」之言，今王至德茂行，復受國土，儻神靈以此告寤人意乎？
manualTranslations.literal: Some said the Ode of the Magpie's Nest contains the words "accumulated conduct and accumulated merit to attain rank and position"; now the prince's supreme virtue and abundant conduct have again received a state—might the spirits be using this to awaken people's hearts?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Some said the Ode of the Magpie's Nest speaks of "accumulated conduct and accumulated merit to attain rank and position"; now the prince's supreme virtue and abundant conduct have again received a state—might the spirits be using this to awaken people's hearts?

manualTranslations.zh: 四月，權薨，諸葛恪秉政。
manualTranslations.literal: In the fourth month Sun Quan died, and Zhuge Ke took charge of government.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Sun Quan died, and Zhuge Ke took charge of government.

manualTranslations.zh: 恪即和妃張之舅也。
manualTranslations.literal: Ke was the maternal uncle of He's consort Zhang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhuge Ke was the maternal uncle of Sun He's consort, Lady Zhang.

manualTranslations.zh: 妃使黃門陳遷之建業上疏中宮，并致問於恪。
manualTranslations.literal: The consort sent Yellow Gate Attendant Chen Qian to Jiankang to submit a memorial to the inner palace and also to convey inquiries to Ke.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The consort sent Yellow Gate Attendant Chen Qian to Jiankang to submit a memorial to the inner palace and also to convey inquiries to Zhuge Ke.

manualTranslations.zh: 臨去，恪謂遷曰：「爲我達妃，期當使勝他人。」
manualTranslations.literal: As he was leaving, Ke told Qian, saying: "Convey to the consort for me: I intend to see that she prevails over the others."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: As he was leaving, Zhuge Ke told Chen Qian, "Convey to the consort for me: I intend to see that she prevails over the others."

manualTranslations.zh: 此言頗泄。
manualTranslations.literal: This remark was rather leaked.

sourceRange.text: "初，皓常銜凱數犯顏忤旨，加何定譖構非-，既以重臣，難繩以法，又陸抗時為大將在疆場，故以計容忍。抗卒後，竟徙凱家於建安。或曰寶鼎元年十二月，凱與大司馬丁奉、御史大夫丁固謀，因皓謁廟，欲廢皓立孫休子。時左將軍留平領兵先驅，故密語平，平拒而不許，誓以不洩，是以所圖不果。太史郎陳苗奏皓久陰不雨，風氣回逆，將有陰謀，皓深警懼雲。《吴录》曰：旧拜庙，选兼大将军领三千兵为卫，凯欲因此兵以图之，令选曹白用丁奉。皓偶不欲，曰：「更选。」凯令执据，虽蹔兼，然宜得其人。皓曰：「用留平。」凯令其子祎谋语平。平素与丁奉有隙，祎未及得宣凯旨，平语祎曰：「闻野猪入丁奉营，此凶徵也。」有喜色。祎乃不敢言，还，因具启凯，故辍止。

sourceRange.text: 權歎曰："使人盡如是儀，當安用科法為?"及寢疾，遺令素棺，斂以時服，務從省約，年八十一卒。胡綜字偉則。汝南固始人也。少孤，母將避難江東。孫策領會稽太守，綜年十四，為門下循行，留吳與孫權共讀書。策薨，權為討虜將軍，以綜為金曹從事，從討黃祖，拜鄂長。權為將軍，都京，召綜還，為書部。與是儀、徐詳俱典軍國密事。劉備下白帝，權以見兵少，使綜料諸縣，得六千人，立解煩兩部，詳領左部、綜領右部督。吳將晉宗叛歸魏，魏以宗為蘄春太守，去江數百里，數為寇害。權使綜與賀齊輕行掩襲，生虜得宗。加建武中郎將。魏拜權為吳王，封綜、儀、詳皆為亭侯。

sourceRange.text: ”其二曰：“昔伊尹去夏人商，陳平委楚歸漢，書功竹帛，遺名陵後世，世主不謂之背誕者，以為知天命也。臣昔為曹氏所見交接，外托群臣，內如骨肉，恩義綢繆，有合無離，遂受偏方之任，總河北之軍。當此之時，志望高大，永與曹氏同死懼生。惟恐功之不建，事之不成耳。及曹氏之亡，後嗣繼位，幼沖統政，讒言彌興。同儕者以勢相害，異趣者得間其言，而臣受性簡略，素不下人，視彼數子，意實迫之，此亦臣之過也。遂為邪議所見構會，招至猜疑，誣臣欲叛。雖識真者保明其心，世亂讒勝，余嫌猶在，常懼一旦橫受無辜，憂心孔疚，如覆冰炭。昔樂毅為燕昭王立功於齊，惠王即位，疑奪其任，遂去燕之趙，休烈不虧。彼豈欲二三其德，蓋畏功名不建，而懼禍之將及也。昔遣魏郡周光以賈販為名，托叛南詣，宣達密計。時以倉卒，未敢便有章表，使光口傳而已。以為天下大歸可見，天意所在，非吳復誰?此方之民，思為臣妾，延頸舉踵，惟恐兵來之遲耳。若使聖恩少加信納，當以河北承望王師，疑心赤實，天日是鑒。而光去經年，不聞咳唾，未審此意竟得達不?瞻望長歎，日月以幾，魯望高子，何足以喻!又臣今日見待稍薄，蒼蠅之聲，綿綿不絕，必受此禍，遲速事耳。臣私度陛下未垂明慰者，必以臣質貫穿仁義之道，不行若此之事，謂光所傳，多虛少實，或謂比中有他消息，不知臣質構讒見疑，恐受大害也。且臣質著有罪之日，自當奔赴鼎鑊，束身待罪，此蓋人臣之宜也。今日無罪，橫見譖毀，將有商鞅、白起之禍。尋惟事勢，去亦直也。死而弗義，不去何為!樂毅之出，吳起之走，君子傷其不遇，未有非之者也。願陛下推古況今，不疑怪於臣質也。又念人臣獲罪，當如伍員奉己自效，不當繞幸因事為利。然今與古，厥勢不同，南北悠遠。江湖隔絕，自不舉事，何得濟免!是以忘志士之節，而思立功之義也之也。且臣質又以曹氏之嗣，非天命所在，政弱刑亂，柄奪於臣，諸將專威於外，各自為政，莫或同心，士卒衰耗，帑藏空虛，綱紀毀廢，上下並昏，想前後數得降叛，具聞此問，兼弱攻昧，宜應天時，此實陛下進取之秋。是以區區敢獻其計。今若內兵淮、泗，據有下邳，荊、揚二州，聞聲響應，臣從河北席眷而南，形勢一連，根牙永固。關西之兵繫於所衛，青、徐二州不敢徹守，許，洛余兵眾不滿萬，誰能來東與陛下爭者?此城千載一會之期，可不深思而熟計乎!及臣所在，既自多馬，加以羌、胡常以三四月中美草時，驅馬來出，隱度今者，可得三千餘匹。陛下出軍，當投此時，多將騎士來就馬耳。此皆先定所一二知。凡兩軍不能相究虛實，今此間實羸，易可克定，陛下舉動，應者必多。上定洪業，使普天一統，下令臣質建非常之功，此乃天也。若不見納，此亦天也。願陛下思之，不復多陳。

sourceRange.text: 綝遣將軍孫耽送亮之國，徙尚於零陵，遷公主於豫章。綝意彌溢，侮慢民神，遂燒大橋頭伍子胥廟，又壞浮屠祠，斬道人。休既即位，稱草莽臣。詣闕上書曰：「臣伏自省，才非干國，因緣肺腑，位極人臣，傷錦敗駕，罪負彰露，尋愆惟闕，夙夜憂懼。臣聞天命棐諶，必就有德，是以幽、厲失度，閡宣中興，陛下聖德，纂承大統，宜得良輔；以協雍熙，雖堯之盛，猶求稷契之佐；以協明聖之德。古人有言：『陳力就列，不能者止。』臣雖自展竭，無益庶政，謹上印綬節鉞，退還田裡，以避賢路。」休引見慰喻。又下詔曰：「朕以不德，守藩於外，值茲際會，群公卿士，暨於朕躬，以奉宗廟。朕用撫然，若涉淵冰。大將軍忠計內發，扶危定傾，安康社稷，功勳赫然。昔漢孝宣踐阼，霍光尊顯，褒德賞功，古今之通義也。其以大將軍為丞相、荊州牧，食五縣。」恩為禦史大夫、衛將軍，據右將軍。皆縣侯。幹雜號將軍、亭侯。闓亦封亭侯。綝一門五侯，皆典禁兵，權傾人主，自吳國朝臣未嘗有也。

context.afterSource: 綝奉牛酒詣休，休不受，齎詣左將軍張布。

manualTranslations.zh: 綝遣將軍孫耽送亮之國，徙尚於零陵，遷公主於豫章。
manualTranslations.literal: Lin sent General Sun Dan to escort Liang to his fief, moved Shang to Lingling, and transferred the princess to Yuzhang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sun Lin sent Sun Dan to escort Sun Liang to his fief, banished Quan Shang to Lingling, and moved the princess to Yuzhang.

manualTranslations.zh: 綝意彌溢，侮慢民神，遂燒大橋頭伍子胥廟，又壞浮屠祠，斬道人。
manualTranslations.literal: Lin's arrogance overflowed; he insulted folk spirits, burned the Wu Zixu temple at Daqiao, destroyed Buddhist shrines, and executed Daoist clergy.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sun Lin grew ever more arrogant, insulted gods and people, burned the Wu Zixu temple at Daqiao, wrecked Buddhist shrines, and executed Daoist clergy.

manualTranslations.zh: 休既即位，稱草莽臣。
manualTranslations.literal: After Xiu took the throne, Lin styled himself a rustic subject.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Once Emperor Xiu reigned, Sun Lin called himself a rustic subject.

manualTranslations.zh: 詣闕上書曰：「臣伏自省，才非干國，因緣肺腑，位極人臣，傷錦敗駕，罪負彰露，尋愆惟闕，夙夜憂懼。
manualTranslations.literal: He went to court and submitted a memorial saying, "Your subject reflects in humility: talent unfit to sustain the state, yet through kinship rose to the summit of ministers; I have torn brocade and wrecked the carriage—guilt stands revealed; reviewing faults I fear day and night.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He went to court and wrote, "I reflect that my talent cannot sustain the state, yet kinship raised me to the summit of power; I have torn brocade and wrecked the carriage, and guilt stands clear; day and night I fear my faults.

manualTranslations.zh: 臣聞天命棐諶，必就有德，是以幽、厲失度，閡宣中興，陛下聖德，纂承大統，宜得良輔；
manualTranslations.literal: Your subject has heard that Heaven's mandate is aided and sincere and must settle on the virtuous; thus You and Li lost measure yet Xuan restored the house; Your Majesty's sagely virtue inherits the great succession and deserves worthy assistants;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Heaven aids the sincere and settles on virtue; You and Li lost the way yet Xuan restored the house; Your Majesty inherits the great succession and deserves worthy assistants;

manualTranslations.zh: 以協雍熙，雖堯之盛，猶求稷契之佐；
manualTranslations.literal: to harmonize peace and glory; even in Yao's greatness he still sought assistants like Ji and Qi;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: to harmonize peace; even Yao sought men like Ji and Qi;

manualTranslations.zh: 以協明聖之德。
manualTranslations.literal: to harmonize with enlightened and sagely virtue.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: to match enlightened and sagely virtue.

manualTranslations.zh: 古人有言：『陳力就列，不能者止。』
manualTranslations.literal: The ancients said, "Offer strength and take your place; if unable, withdraw."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The ancients said, "Offer strength and take your place; if unable, withdraw."

manualTranslations.zh: 臣雖自展竭，無益庶政，謹上印綬節鉞，退還田裡，以避賢路。」
manualTranslations.literal: Though your subject has exhausted himself, he benefits no common governance; I respectfully return seals, ribbons, and credential staff, withdraw to fields and hamlets, and yield the path for the worthy."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Though I have exhausted myself I benefit no governance; I return seals, ribbons, and the staff of authority, withdraw to my fields, and yield the path for the worthy."

manualTranslations.zh: 休引見慰喻。
manualTranslations.literal: Xiu received him in audience and comforted him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiu received him in audience and comforted him.

manualTranslations.zh: 又下詔曰：「朕以不德，守藩於外，值茲際會，群公卿士，暨於朕躬，以奉宗廟。
manualTranslations.literal: He also issued an edict saying, "We lack virtue, guarded a fief abroad, met this juncture, and lords, ministers, and scholars together with Our person uphold the ancestral temple.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He also issued an edict: "Lacking virtue I guarded a fief abroad until this juncture, when lords and ministers with me uphold the ancestral temple.

manualTranslations.zh: 朕用撫然，若涉淵冰。
manualTranslations.literal: We are apprehensive, as if treading deep ice.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I am apprehensive, as if treading deep ice.

manualTranslations.zh: 大將軍忠計內發，扶危定傾，安康社稷，功勳赫然。
manualTranslations.literal: The Grand General's loyal plan arose within, braced peril and steadied the tipping, brought peace to altars and state, and his merit blazed bright.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The grand general's loyal counsel braced peril, steadied the state, and his merit blazed bright.

manualTranslations.zh: 昔漢孝宣踐阼，霍光尊顯，褒德賞功，古今之通義也。
manualTranslations.literal: Formerly when Han's Emperor Xuan ascended the throne, Huo Guang was honored and exalted—praising virtue and rewarding merit is the constant principle of past and present.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan of Han took the throne he honored Huo Guang—praising merit is the constant way of past and present.

manualTranslations.zh: 其以大將軍為丞相、荊州牧，食五縣。」
manualTranslations.literal: Let the Grand General be Chancellor and Governor of Jing Province with income from five counties."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Let the grand general be chancellor and governor of Jing with income from five counties."

manualTranslations.idiomatic: En was made grandee secretary and guard general; Lü Ju was made general of the right.

manualTranslations.zh: 皆縣侯。

manualTranslations.idiomatic: All were enfeoffed as district marquises.

manualTranslations.idiomatic: Kan was also enfeoffed as village marquis.

manualTranslations.idiomatic: Five marquises in one Sun Lin household, all commanding palace troops—power beyond any Wu minister before.

sourceRange.text: 永安元年258年十二月丁卯，建業中謠言明會有變。綝聞之，不悅。夜大風發木揚沙，綝益恐。戊辰臘會，綝稱疾。休強起之，使者十餘輩。綝不得已，將人，眾止焉。綝曰：「國家屢有命，不可辭。可豫整兵，令府內起火，因是可得速還。」遂入，尋而火起，綝求出，休曰：「外兵自多，不足煩丞相也。」綝起離席，奉、布目左右縛之。綝叩首曰：「願徙交州。」休曰：「卿何以不徙滕胤、呂據？」綝復曰：「願沒為官奴。」休曰：「何不以胤、據為奴乎！」遂斬之。以綝首令其眾曰：「諸與綝同謀皆赦。」放仗者五千人。闓乘船欲北降，追殺之。夷三族。發孫峻棺，取其印綬，綝其木而埋之，以殺魯育等故也。

context.beforeSource: 將軍魏邈說休曰「綝居外必有變」，武衛士施朔又告「綝欲反有徵」休密問張布，布與丁奉謀於會殺綝。
context.afterSource: 綝死時年二十八。

manualTranslations.zh: 綝聞之，不悅。
manualTranslations.literal: Lin heard it and was displeased.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sun Lin heard and was displeased.

manualTranslations.zh: 夜大風發木揚沙，綝益恐。
manualTranslations.literal: That night a great wind uprooted trees and raised sand; Lin grew more fearful.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: That night gale winds uprooted trees and raised sand; Lin grew more afraid.

manualTranslations.zh: 戊辰臘會，綝稱疾。
manualTranslations.literal: On day wuchen at the year-end assembly Lin claimed illness.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At the year-end assembly on day wuchen Sun Lin claimed illness.

manualTranslations.zh: 休強起之，使者十餘輩。
manualTranslations.literal: Xiu forced him to rise; over ten messengers came.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiu forced him to attend; more than ten messengers came.

manualTranslations.zh: 綝不得已，將人，眾止焉。
manualTranslations.literal: Lin had no choice and was about to lead men when the crowd stopped him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sun Lin had no choice and was about to bring men when the crowd stopped him.

manualTranslations.zh: 綝曰：「國家屢有命，不可辭。
manualTranslations.literal: Lin said, "The state has repeatedly commanded; one cannot refuse.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sun Lin said, "The state has repeatedly commanded; I cannot refuse.

manualTranslations.zh: 可豫整兵，令府內起火，因是可得速還。」
manualTranslations.literal: You may ready troops in advance, set fire inside the mansion, and thereby return quickly."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Ready troops in advance, set fire inside the mansion, and I can return quickly."

manualTranslations.zh: 遂入，尋而火起，綝求出，休曰：「外兵自多，不足煩丞相也。」
manualTranslations.literal: He then entered; soon fire rose; Lin begged to leave; Xiu said, "Outside troops are plentiful enough—no need to trouble the Chancellor."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He entered; soon fire rose; Lin begged to leave; Emperor Xiu said, "Outside troops are plentiful—no need to trouble the chancellor."

manualTranslations.zh: 綝起離席，奉、布目左右縛之。
manualTranslations.literal: Lin rose from his seat; Feng and Bu signaled attendants to bind him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sun Lin rose; Ding Feng and Zhang Bu signaled attendants to bind him.

manualTranslations.zh: 綝叩首曰：「願徙交州。」
manualTranslations.literal: Lin kowtowed and said, "I wish to be banished to Jiaozhou."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Lin kowtowed: "Banish me to Jiaozhou."

manualTranslations.zh: 休曰：「卿何以不徙滕胤、呂據？」
manualTranslations.literal: Xiu said, "Why did you not banish Teng Yin and Lü Ju?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiu said, "Why did you not banish Teng Yin and Lü Ju?"

manualTranslations.zh: 綝復曰：「願沒為官奴。」
manualTranslations.literal: Lin again said, "I wish to be reduced to government slaves."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Lin said, "Make me a government slave."

manualTranslations.zh: 休曰：「何不以胤、據為奴乎！」
manualTranslations.literal: Xiu said, "Why not make Yin and Ju the slaves!"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiu said, "Why not make Yin and Ju the slaves!"

manualTranslations.zh: 遂斬之。
manualTranslations.literal: Thereupon he was beheaded.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Then he was beheaded.

manualTranslations.zh: 以綝首令其眾曰：「諸與綝同謀皆赦。」
manualTranslations.literal: With Lin's head he addressed the host saying, "All who plotted with Lin are pardoned."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Holding Lin's head he told the host, "All who plotted with Lin are pardoned."

manualTranslations.zh: 放仗者五千人。
manualTranslations.literal: Five thousand who laid down weapons were released.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Five thousand who laid down weapons were released.

manualTranslations.zh: 闓乘船欲北降，追殺之。
manualTranslations.literal: Kan took ship intending to surrender north; pursuers killed him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Kan tried to flee north by ship; pursuers killed him.

manualTranslations.zh: 夷三族。
manualTranslations.literal: Three clans were exterminated.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Three clans were exterminated.

manualTranslations.zh: 發孫峻棺，取其印綬，綝其木而埋之，以殺魯育等故也。
manualTranslations.literal: Sun Jun's coffin was opened, his seals and ribbons taken, the wood flayed and buried—because of the killing of Lu Yu and others.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sun Jun's coffin was opened, his seals taken, the wood flayed and buried—for the killing of Lu Yu and others.

sourceRange.text: 滕胤字承嗣，北海劇人也。伯父耽，父冑，與劉繇州裡通家。以世擾亂，渡江依繇。孫權為車騎將軍，拜耽右司馬，以寬厚稱，早卒，無嗣。冑善屬文，權待以賓禮，軍國書疏，常令損益潤色之，亦不幸短命。權為吳王，迫錄舊恩，封胤都亭侯。少有節操，美容儀。《吳書》曰：胤年十二，而孤單煢立，能治身厲行。為人白晳，威儀可觀。每正朔朝賀脩勤，在位大臣見者，無不歎賞。弱冠尚公主。年三十，起家為丹楊太守，徙吳郡、會稽，所在見稱。《吳書》曰：胤上表陳及時宜，及民間優劣，多所匡弼。權以胤故，增重公主之賜，屢加存問。胤每聽辭訟，斷罪法，察言觀色，務盡情理。人有窮冤悲苦之言，對之流涕。太元元年251年，權寢疾，詣都，留為太常；與諾葛恪等俱受遺詔輔政。孫亮即位，加衛將軍。

context.beforeSource: 後為將，討儋耳，還拜丹楊太守，年三十三卒。

manualTranslations.zh: 滕胤字承嗣，北海劇人也。
manualTranslations.literal: Teng Yin, courtesy name Chengsi, was a man of Ju in Beihai.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Teng Yin, styled Chengsi, came from Ju in Beihai.

manualTranslations.zh: 伯父耽，父冑，與劉繇州裡通家。
manualTranslations.literal: His father's elder brother was Dan; his father was Zhou; they were family friends with Liu Yao in the same province.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His uncle Dan and his father Zhou were old family friends of Liu Yao in the province.

manualTranslations.zh: 以世擾亂，渡江依繇。
manualTranslations.literal: Because the age was in turmoil, they crossed the river and relied on Yao.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the turmoil of the times they crossed the Yangzi and attached themselves to Liu Yao.

manualTranslations.zh: 孫權為車騎將軍，拜耽右司馬，以寬厚稱，早卒，無嗣。
manualTranslations.literal: When Sun Quan was General of Chariots and Cavalry he appointed Dan Right Major; Dan was praised for generosity and died young without heirs.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Sun Quan was general of chariots and cavalry he made Dan right major; Dan was known for generosity, died young, and left no heirs.

manualTranslations.zh: 冑善屬文，權待以賓禮，軍國書疏，常令損益潤色之，亦不幸短命。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhou excelled at composition; Quan treated him with guest ceremony and often had him revise and polish state and military documents; he too died young by misfortune.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhou was a skilled writer whom Sun Quan honored as a guest and often asked to polish state papers; he too died young.

manualTranslations.zh: 權為吳王，迫錄舊恩，封胤都亭侯。
manualTranslations.literal: When Quan became King of Wu he, mindful of old kindness, enfeoffed Yin as Marquis of the Capital Precinct.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Sun Quan became king of Wu he remembered old debts and enfeoffed Yin as marquis of the capital precinct.

manualTranslations.zh: 少有節操，美容儀。
manualTranslations.literal: From youth he had integrity and handsome bearing.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: From youth he was principled and handsome.

manualTranslations.zh: 《吳書》曰：胤年十二，而孤單煢立，能治身厲行。
manualTranslations.literal: The Wu shu states: Yin at twelve stood alone and orphaned, yet could discipline himself and enforce conduct.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Wu shu states that at twelve Yin was orphaned yet disciplined himself sternly.

manualTranslations.zh: 為人白晳，威儀可觀。
manualTranslations.literal: He was fair-skinned and his bearing was admirable.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Fair-skinned, his bearing was imposing.

manualTranslations.zh: 每正朔朝賀脩勤，在位大臣見者，無不歎賞。
manualTranslations.literal: At each New Year court congratulation he was diligent in ritual; ministers who saw him all sighed in admiration.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At New Year audiences his ritual diligence moved every minister who saw him.

manualTranslations.zh: 弱冠尚公主。
manualTranslations.literal: At coming of age he married an imperial princess.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At his capping he married an imperial princess.

manualTranslations.zh: 年三十，起家為丹楊太守，徙吳郡、會稽，所在見稱。
manualTranslations.literal: At thirty he first left home to serve as Administrator of Danyang, was transferred to Wu and Kuaiji commanderies, and was praised wherever he served.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At thirty he became administrator of Danyang, then served Wu and Kuaiji, winning praise in each post.

manualTranslations.zh: 《吳書》曰：胤上表陳及時宜，及民間優劣，多所匡弼。
manualTranslations.literal: The Wu shu states: Yin memorialized on timely policy and on the merits and faults among the people, correcting much.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Wu shu states that Yin memorialized on policy and popular conditions and corrected much.

manualTranslations.zh: 權以胤故，增重公主之賜，屢加存問。
manualTranslations.literal: Because of Yin, Quan increased the princess's gifts and repeatedly sent inquiries.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: For Teng Yin's sake Sun Quan enriched the princess's gifts and often sent inquiries.

manualTranslations.zh: 胤每聽辭訟，斷罪法，察言觀色，務盡情理。
manualTranslations.literal: Whenever Yin heard lawsuits he judged by law, watched words and expressions, and strove to exhaust reason and feeling.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In court Teng Yin judged by law, read faces, and strove for justice tempered by mercy.

manualTranslations.zh: 人有窮冤悲苦之言，對之流涕。
manualTranslations.literal: When people spoke of desperate wrongs and bitter grief he wept before them.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He wept openly when petitioners told tales of desperate wrong.

manualTranslations.zh: 太元元年251年，權寢疾，詣都，留為太常；
manualTranslations.literal: In the first year of Taixuan, 251 CE, when Quan lay ill Yin went to the capital and was retained as Chamberlain for Ceremonies;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Taixuan 1 (251), when Sun Quan fell ill, Teng Yin came to court and was kept as chamberlain for ceremonies;

manualTranslations.zh: 與諾葛恪等俱受遺詔輔政。
manualTranslations.literal: together with Zhuge Ke and others he received the deathbed edict to assist government.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: and with Zhuge Ke and others received the deathbed regency.

manualTranslations.zh: 孫亮即位，加衛將軍。
manualTranslations.literal: When Sun Liang took the throne Yin was made Guard General.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Sun Liang succeeded, Yin was made guard general.

sourceRange.text: 」恪嘗獻權馬，先其耳。

localRange.text: 恪嘗獻權馬，先钅芻其耳。

context.afterSource: 範慎時在坐，嘲恪曰：「馬雖大畜，禀氣於天，今殘其耳，豈不傷仁？

sourceRange.text: 孫峻字子遠，孫堅弟靜之曾孫也。靜生暠，暠生恭，為散騎侍郎。恭生峻。少便弓馬，精果膽決。孫權末，徙武衛都尉，為侍中。權臨薨，受遺輔政，領武衛將軍，故典宿衛，封都鄉侯。既誅諸葛恪，遷丞相大將軍，督中外諸軍事、假節，進封富春侯。滕胤以恪子竦妻父辭位。峻曰：「鯀、禹罪不相及，滕侯何為？」峻、胤雖內不沾洽，而外相包容，進胤爵高密侯，共事如前。《吳錄》曰：群臣上奏，共推峻為太尉，議胤為司徒。時有媚峻者，以為大統宜在公族，若滕胤為亞公，聲名素重，眾心所附，不可貳也。乃表以峻為丞相，又不置御史大夫，士人皆失望矣。峻素無重名，驕矜險害，多所刑殺，百姓囂然。又姦亂宮人，與公主魯班私通。五鳳元年254年，吳侯英謀殺峻，英事洩死。

context.beforeSource: 《吳書》曰：胤寵任彌高，接士愈勤，表奏書疏，皆自經意，不以委下。
context.afterSource: 二年，魏毋丘儉、文欽以眾叛，與魏人戰於樂嘉，峻帥驃騎將軍呂據、左將軍留贊襲壽春，會欽敗降，軍還。

manualTranslations.zh: 孫峻字子遠，孫堅弟靜之曾孫也。
manualTranslations.literal: Sun Jun, courtesy name Ziyuan, was a great-grandson of Jing, younger brother of Sun Jian.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sun Jun, styled Ziyuan, was a great-grandson of Sun Jian's brother Jing.

manualTranslations.zh: 靜生暠，暠生恭，為散騎侍郎。
manualTranslations.literal: Jing begot Gao; Gao begot Gong, who was Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Jing's line ran Gao to Gong, a regular attendant of scattered cavalry.

manualTranslations.zh: 恭生峻。
manualTranslations.literal: Gong begot Jun.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Gong was Jun's father.

manualTranslations.zh: 少便弓馬，精果膽決。
manualTranslations.literal: From youth he was skilled with bow and horse, decisive and daring.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: From youth he excelled at arms and acted with bold decisiveness.

manualTranslations.zh: 孫權末，徙武衛都尉，為侍中。
manualTranslations.literal: Late in Sun Quan's reign he was moved to Commandant of Martial Guards and made Palace Attendant.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Late in Sun Quan's reign he became commandant of martial guards and palace attendant.

manualTranslations.zh: 權臨薨，受遺輔政，領武衛將軍，故典宿衛，封都鄉侯。
manualTranslations.literal: As Quan lay dying Jun received the testament to assist government, took command as General of Martial Guards, continued to oversee palace guards, and was enfeoffed as Marquis of the Capital District.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At Sun Quan's deathbed Sun Jun received the regency, commanded the martial guards, kept palace security, and was enfeoffed as marquis of the capital district.

manualTranslations.zh: 既誅諸葛恪，遷丞相大將軍，督中外諸軍事、假節，進封富春侯。
manualTranslations.literal: After Zhuge Ke was executed he was moved to Chancellor and Grand General, put in charge of all military affairs inside and outside with credential staff, and advanced to Marquis of Fuchun.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After Zhuge Ke's execution he became chancellor and grand general with full military command and was advanced to marquis of Fuchun.

manualTranslations.zh: 滕胤以恪子竦妻父辭位。
manualTranslations.literal: Teng Yin, as father-in-law to Ke's son Song, declined office.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Teng Yin, Zhuge Ke's son-in-law, declined office.

manualTranslations.zh: 峻曰：「鯀、禹罪不相及，滕侯何為？」
manualTranslations.literal: Jun said, "Gun and Yu's crimes did not reach one another—why should Marquis Teng do so?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sun Jun said, "Gun and Yu were not punished for each other's crimes—why should Marquis Teng?"

manualTranslations.zh: 峻、胤雖內不沾洽，而外相包容，進胤爵高密侯，共事如前。
manualTranslations.literal: Though Jun and Yin were not close within, outwardly they accommodated each other; Jun advanced Yin to Marquis of Gaomi and they worked together as before.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Though Sun Jun and Teng Yin were cold in private, outwardly they cooperated; Jun made Yin marquis of Gaomi and business continued.

manualTranslations.zh: 《吳錄》曰：群臣上奏，共推峻為太尉，議胤為司徒。
manualTranslations.literal: The Wu lu states: The ministers jointly memorialized, recommending Jun as Grand Commandant and Yin as Minister over the Masses.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Wu lu states that ministers recommended Sun Jun as grand commandant and Teng Yin as minister over the masses.

manualTranslations.zh: 時有媚峻者，以為大統宜在公族，若滕胤為亞公，聲名素重，眾心所附，不可貳也。
manualTranslations.literal: At the time flatterers of Jun held that the great succession should rest with the ducal clan; if Teng Yin became deputy minister, his fame was already weighty and hearts attached to him—he could not be made second.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Flatterers argued the succession belonged to the imperial clan; if famed Teng Yin became deputy minister hearts would divide.

manualTranslations.zh: 乃表以峻為丞相，又不置御史大夫，士人皆失望矣。
manualTranslations.literal: Thereupon they memorialized to make Jun Chancellor and again did not appoint a Grandee Secretary; scholars all despaired.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: They made Sun Jun chancellor instead and left the censorate empty; scholars despaired.

manualTranslations.zh: 峻素無重名，驕矜險害，多所刑殺，百姓囂然。
manualTranslations.literal: Jun had never had great reputation; he was arrogant, dangerous, and harmful, executed many, and the common people were in uproar.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sun Jun had never been esteemed; arrogant and cruel, he killed freely and the people seethed.

manualTranslations.zh: 又姦亂宮人，與公主魯班私通。
manualTranslations.literal: He also debauched palace women and privately consorted with Princess Lu Ban.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He debauched palace women and kept Princess Lu Ban as a lover.

manualTranslations.zh: 五鳳元年254年，吳侯英謀殺峻，英事洩死。
manualTranslations.literal: In the first year of Wufeng, 254 CE, Marquis of Wu Ying plotted to kill Jun; Ying's affair leaked and he died.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wufeng 1 (254): Marquis Ying of Wu plotted to kill Sun Jun; the plot leaked and Ying died.

sourceRange.text: 」濮陽興字子元，陳留人也。父逸，漢末避亂江東，官至長沙太守。逸事見《陸瑁傳》。興少有士名，孫權時除上虞令，稍遷至尚書左曹，以五官中郎將使蜀，還為會稽太守。時琅邪王休居會稽，興深與相結。及休即位，徵興為太常衛將軍、平軍國事，封外黃侯。永安三年260年，都尉嚴密建丹楊湖田，作浦裡塘。

context.beforeSource: 其罹恪等事見遠徙者，一切召還。
context.afterSource: 詔百官會議，咸以為用功多而田不保成，唯興以為可成。
context.beforeLocal: 其罹恪等事見遠徙者，一切召還。
context.afterLocal: 詔百官會議，咸以為用功多而田不保成，唯興以為可成。

manualTranslations.zh: 濮陽興字子元，陳留人也。
manualTranslations.literal: Puyang Xing, courtesy name Ziyuan, was a man of Chenliu.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Puyang Xing, styled Ziyuan, came from Chenliu.

manualTranslations.zh: 父逸，漢末避亂江東，官至長沙太守。
manualTranslations.literal: His father Yi, fleeing chaos at the end of Han, crossed to Jiangdong and rose to Administrator of Changsha.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His father Yi fled the late-Han turmoil to Jiangdong and became administrator of Changsha.

manualTranslations.zh: 逸事見《陸瑁傳》。
manualTranslations.literal: Yi's career appears in the biography of Lu Mao.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yi's career is recorded in the biography of Lu Mao.

manualTranslations.zh: 興少有士名，孫權時除上虞令，稍遷至尚書左曹，以五官中郎將使蜀，還為會稽太守。
manualTranslations.literal: Xing early gained a scholar's reputation; under Sun Quan he was appointed magistrate of Shangyu, gradually rose to the left bureau of the Masters of Writing, served as General of the Five Offices as envoy to Shu, and on return became Administrator of Kuaiji.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Puyang Xing won early fame as a gentleman; under Sun Quan he served as magistrate of Shangyu, rose through the secretariat, went to Shu as envoy, and returned as administrator of Kuaiji.

manualTranslations.zh: 時琅邪王休居會稽，興深與相結。
manualTranslations.literal: At that time Prince of Langye Xiu resided in Kuaiji, and Xing formed a deep bond with him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: While Prince Xiu of Langye lived in Kuaiji, Puyang Xing became his close ally.

manualTranslations.zh: 及休即位，徵興為太常衛將軍、平軍國事，封外黃侯。
manualTranslations.literal: When Xiu took the throne, Xing was summoned as Chamberlain for Ceremonies and Guard General and charged with settling military affairs, enfeoffed as Marquis of Waihuang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiu ascended the throne, Xing was made chamberlain for ceremonies and guard general, charged with military affairs, and enfeoffed as marquis of Waihuang.

manualTranslations.zh: 永安三年260年，都尉嚴密建丹楊湖田，作浦裡塘。
manualTranslations.literal: In the third year of Yongan, 260 CE, Commandant Yan Mi proposed Danyang lake-field works, building Puli Pool.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yongan 3 (260): Commandant Yan Mi proposed the Danyang lake-field project and the Puli reclamation.

items.acceptedSourceText: 濮陽興字子元，陳留人也。父逸，漢末避亂江東，官至長沙太守。逸事見《陸瑁傳》。興少有士名，孫權時除上虞令，稍遷至尚書左曹，以五官中郎將使蜀，還為會稽太守。時琅邪王休居會稽，興深與相結。及休即位，徵興為太常衛將軍、平軍國事，封外黃侯。永安三年260年，都尉嚴密建丹楊湖田，作浦裡塘。

sourceRange.text: 初，權黃龍元年229年遷都建業。二年築東興堤遏湖水。後徵淮南，敗，以內船，由是廢不復修。恪以建興元年252年十月會眾於東興，更作大堤，左右結山俠築兩城，各留千人，使全端、留略守之，引軍而還。魏以吳軍入其疆土，恥於受侮，命大將胡遵、諸葛誕等率眾七萬，欲攻圍兩塢，圖壞堤遏。恪興軍四萬，晨夜赴救。遵等敕其諸軍作浮橋度，陳於堤上，分兵攻兩城。城在高峻，不可卒拔。恪遣將軍留贊、呂據、唐諮、丁奉為前部。時天寒雪，魏諸將會飲，見贊等兵少，而解置鎧甲，不持矛戟。但兜鍪刀楯，夥身緣遏，大笑之，不即嚴兵。兵得上，便鼓譟亂斫。魏軍驚擾散走，爭渡浮橋，橋壞絕，自投於水，更相蹈藉。樂安太守桓嘉等同時並沒，死者數萬。故叛將韓綜為魏前軍督，亦斬之。獲車乘牛馬驢騾各數千，資器山積，振旅而歸。進封恪陽都侯，加荊揚州牧，督中外諸軍事，賜金一百斤，馬二百匹，繒佈各萬匹。

context.beforeSource: 恪每出入，百姓延頸思見其狀。
context.afterSource: 恪遂有輕敵之心，以十二月戰克，明年春，復欲出軍。
context.beforeLocal: 恪每出入，百姓延頸思見其狀。
context.afterLocal: 恪遂有輕敵之心，以十二月戰克，明年春，復欲出軍。

manualTranslations.zh: 初，權黃龍元年229年遷都建業。
manualTranslations.literal: At first, in the first year of Huanglong, 229 CE, Quan moved the capital to Jianye.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At first, in Huanglong 1 (229), Sun Quan moved the capital to Jianye.

manualTranslations.zh: 二年築東興堤遏湖水。
manualTranslations.literal: In the second year he built the Dongxing embankment to dam the lake waters.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The next year he built the Dongxing dyke to hold back the lake.

manualTranslations.zh: 後徵淮南，敗，以內船，由是廢不復修。
manualTranslations.literal: Later a Huainan campaign failed; because the boats were internal, the works were abandoned and never repaired.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: A later Huainan campaign failed; the boats were unsuited, and the works were abandoned.

manualTranslations.zh: 恪以建興元年252年十月會眾於東興，更作大堤，左右結山俠築兩城，各留千人，使全端、留略守之，引軍而還。
manualTranslations.literal: Ke, in the tenth month of the first year of Jianxing, 252 CE, assembled forces at Dongxing, rebuilt the great embankment, linked mountain flanks to erect two forts, left a thousand men in each, appointed Quan Duan and Liu Lue to hold them, and withdrew the main army.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Jianxing 1, month 10 (252), Zhuge Ke rebuilt the great Dongxing dyke, threw up twin forts on the flanks with a thousand men each under Quan Duan and Liu Lue, and marched home.

manualTranslations.zh: 魏以吳軍入其疆土，恥於受侮，命大將胡遵、諸葛誕等率眾七萬，欲攻圍兩塢，圖壞堤遏。
manualTranslations.literal: Wei, shamed that Wu troops had entered its territory, ordered Grand Generals Hu Zun, Zhuge Dan, and others to lead seventy thousand men to attack and besiege the two forts and break the dam.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Humiliated by Wu incursion, Wei sent Hu Zun, Zhuge Dan, and seventy thousand men to storm the twin forts and break the dyke.

manualTranslations.zh: 恪興軍四萬，晨夜赴救。
manualTranslations.literal: Ke raised an army of forty thousand and rushed to the rescue day and night.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhuge Ke marched forty thousand men to the rescue without rest.

manualTranslations.zh: 遵等敕其諸軍作浮橋度，陳於堤上，分兵攻兩城。
manualTranslations.literal: Zun and the others ordered their hosts to build pontoon bridges to cross, arrayed on the embankment, and divided forces to attack the two forts.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zun ordered pontoon bridges thrown across, lined the dyke, and split forces to assault both forts.

manualTranslations.zh: 城在高峻，不可卒拔。
manualTranslations.literal: The forts stood high and steep and could not be taken at once.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The forts were too high and steep to storm quickly.

manualTranslations.zh: 恪遣將軍留贊、呂據、唐諮、丁奉為前部。
manualTranslations.literal: Ke sent Generals Liu Zan, Lü Ju, Tang Zi, and Ding Feng as the van.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhuge Ke sent Liu Zan, Lü Ju, Tang Zi, and Ding Feng ahead as the van.

manualTranslations.zh: 時天寒雪，魏諸將會飲，見贊等兵少，而解置鎧甲，不持矛戟。
manualTranslations.literal: It was bitterly cold and snowing; the Wei generals were drinking together, saw that Zan and the others had few troops, and doffed their armor, laying aside spears and halberds.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In driving snow the Wei generals drank, saw how few Wu troops faced them, and stripped off armor and spears.

manualTranslations.zh: 但兜鍪刀楯，夥身緣遏，大笑之，不即嚴兵。
manualTranslations.literal: They wore only helmets, swords, and shields, climbed the embankment in a crowd, laughed at them, and did not immediately ready their troops.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Helmets, swords, and shields only, they swarmed the dyke laughing and did not immediately ready their troops.

manualTranslations.zh: 兵得上，便鼓譟亂斫。
manualTranslations.literal: Once Wu troops gained the height, they beat drums, shouted, and hacked in disorder.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wu soldiers surged up, drums roaring, blades flailing.

manualTranslations.zh: 魏軍驚擾散走，爭渡浮橋，橋壞絕，自投於水，更相蹈藉。
manualTranslations.literal: The Wei army panicked and scattered, scrambling for the pontoon bridges; the bridges broke, men threw themselves into the water, and trampled one another.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wei troops broke, crushed the bridges, drowned and trampled one another in flight.

manualTranslations.zh: 樂安太守桓嘉等同時並沒，死者數萬。
manualTranslations.literal: Administrator of Le'an Huan Jia and others perished together; the dead numbered in the tens of thousands.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Le'an administrator Huan Jia and others drowned with them; tens of thousands died.

manualTranslations.zh: 故叛將韓綜為魏前軍督，亦斬之。
manualTranslations.literal: The former rebel general Han Zong, serving as Wei van commander, was also beheaded.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Han Zong, the turncoat now commanding Wei van, was beheaded too.

manualTranslations.zh: 獲車乘牛馬驢騾各數千，資器山積，振旅而歸。
manualTranslations.literal: They captured thousands of carts, cattle, horses, donkeys, and mules, with stores piled like hills, and returned in good order.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: They seized thousands of wagons and beasts, booty heaped like hills, and marched home in triumph.

manualTranslations.zh: 進封恪陽都侯，加荊揚州牧，督中外諸軍事，賜金一百斤，馬二百匹，繒佈各萬匹。
manualTranslations.literal: Ke was advanced to Marquis of Yangdu, made Governor of Jing and Yang provinces, put in charge of all military affairs inside and outside, and granted one hundred jin of gold, two hundred horses, and ten thousand bolts each of silk and cloth.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhuge Ke was made marquis of Yangdu, governor of Jing and Yang, commander of all forces, and given a hundred jin of gold, two hundred horses, and ten thousand bolts each of silk and cloth.
